metadata.source: Tadeusz Skorupski: The Sarvadurgatiparisodhana Tantra, Elimination of All Destinies, Sanskrit and Tibetan Texts with Introduction, English Translation and Notes. Delhi 1983.

body.translated_text: I
<s>Oṃ</s>. Homage to the glorious <s>Vajrasattva</s>!

body.text: evaṃ mayā śrutam ekasmin samaye bhagavān sarvadevottamanandavane viharati sma / maṇisuvarṇaśākhālatābaddhavanaspatigulmauṣadhikamalotpalakarṇikārabakulatilakāśokamāndāravamahāmāndāravādibhir nānāvidhaiḥ puṣpair upaśobhite / kalpavṛkṣasamalaṃkṛte / nānālaṃkāravibhūṣite / nānāpakṣigaṇakūjite / tūryamukundaveṇubherīprabhṛtipraṇadite / śakrabrahmādidevāpsarobhir nānāvidhābhir vikrīḍite / sarvabuddhabodhisattvādhiṣṭhite / sarvaśakrabrahmādidevavidyādharadevāpsaraḥparṣatkoṭīniyutaśatasahasrair anekayakṣarākṣasāsuragaruḍagandharvakinnaramahoraganāgādiparṣadbhir nānāvidhābhir mahābodhisattvakoṭīśatasahasrair aṣṭābhiḥ /
body.translated_text: Thus have I heard. At one time, the <s>Bhagavān</s> was dwelling in the supreme celestial <s>Nandavana</s> (Garden of Delight) of all the gods, adorned with various flowers—crystal, gem, and golden branches, vines, trees, shrubs, herbs, lotuses, blue lotuses, <s>karṇikāra</s>, <s>bakula</s>, <s>tilaka</s>, <s>aśoka</s>, <s>māndārava</s>, great <s>māndārava</s>, and others—embellished with wish-fulfilling trees, decorated with various ornaments, resounding with flocks of various birds, reverberating with musical instruments, <s>mukunda</s> drums, flutes, kettledrums, and the like, a place of sport for <s>Śakra</s>, <s>Brahmā</s>, and other gods and <s>apsaras</s> of various kinds, blessed by all Buddhas and <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, surrounded by assemblies of hundreds of thousands of <s>koṭīs</s> and <s>niyutas</s> of all <s>Śakra</s>, <s>Brahmā</s>, and other gods, <s>vidyādharas</s>, divine <s>apsaras</s>, many <s>yakṣas</s>, <s>rākṣasas</s>, <s>asuras</s>, <s>garuḍas</s>, <s>gandharvas</s>, <s>kinnaras</s>, <s>mahoragas</s>, <s>nāgas</s>, and other assemblies of various kinds, and by eight hundreds of thousands of <s>koṭīs</s> of great <s>Bodhisattvas</s>—
namely:

body.text:
pratibhānamatinā ca bodhisattvena mahāsattvena / acalamatinā ca / vipulamatinā ca / samantamatinā ca / anantamatinā ca / asamantamatinā ca / kamalamatinā ca / mahāmatinā ca / divāmatinā ca / vividhamatinā ca / aśeṣamatinā ca / samantabhadreṇa ca / evaṃ pramukhair avaivartikabodhisattvamahāsattvasaṃghair anantāparyantaiḥ satkṛtaḥ /
gurukṛto 'rcitaḥ pūjitaḥ suprakṛṣṭo mahāparṣadgaṇamadhye mahābrahmā padmāsane niṣaṇṇaḥ sarvadurgatipariśodhananāmasamādhiṃ samāpannaḥ samanantaram evāpāyatrayasantativimokṣakanāmamahābodhisattvaraśmispharaṇasaṃharaṇānekamālā svorṇākośānniścacāra / tena trisahasramahāsahasralokadhātur avabhāsitaḥ / tenāvabhāsena sarvasattvāś cittakleśabandhanān mocayitvā pṛthak pṛthak saṃprāpito nandavanaṃ ca samantādavabhāsayitvā /
body.translated_text: the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> <s>Pratibhānamati</s>, <s>Acalamati</s>, <s>Vipulamati</s>, <s>Samantamati</s>, <s>Anantamati</s>, <s>Asamantamati</s>, <s>Kamalamati</s>, <s>Mahāmati</s>, <s>Divāmati</s>, <s>Vividhamati</s>, <s>Aśeṣamati</s>, <s>Samantabhadra</s>—headed by these, honored, revered, worshipped, and venerated by assemblies of irreversible <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattvas</s>, infinite and boundless. The great <s>Brahmā</s>, most excellent among the great assembly, seated on a lotus throne, entered the <s>samādhi</s> (meditative concentration) called "Purification of All Evil Destinies." Immediately thereupon, manifold garlands of great <s>Bodhisattva</s> light-rays named "Liberation from the Continuity of the Three Lower Realms" issued forth from their golden sheaths, spreading and withdrawing. By that, the great trichiliocosm was illuminated. By that illumination, having liberated all beings from the bonds of mental afflictions, each and every one was brought to the <s>Nandavana</s>, and having illuminated it entirely on all sides,

body.text: nānāpūjāmeghaiḥ pūjayitvā śatasahasraṃ pradakṣiṇīkṛtya śirasā vanditvā bhagavataḥ purastād vimalāsaner upari niṣadyaivam āhuḥ aho buddha aho buddhasya dharmaśobhanam //
body.translated_text: having worshipped with various clouds of offerings, having circumambulated a hundred thousand times, having bowed with their heads, they sat upon the stainless throne before the <s>Bhagavān</s> and spoke thus: 'Oh, the Buddha! Oh, the splendor of the Buddha's <s>Dharma</s>!'
'For what reason?'
'The purification of our evil destinies,'
'and the establishment in <s>Bodhisattva</s> conduct.'

body.text: atha devendro bhagavantaṃ śatasahasraṃ pradakṣiṇīkṛtya vanditvā bhagavantam etad avocat / bhagavan kena kāraṇena buddharaśmisamantāvabhāsena durgatisamantān mocayitvā vimuktimārge pratiṣṭhāpitā āścaryaṃ sugata / bhagavān āha / nedaṃ devendrāścaryaṃ buddhānāṃ bhagavatāṃ sūpacitāpramāṇapuṇyasaṃbhārāṇām /
body.translated_text: Then <s>Devendra</s> (Lord of the Gods), having circumambulated the <s>Bhagavān</s> a hundred thousand times and having bowed, said this to the <s>Bhagavān</s>: '<s>Bhagavān</s>, for what reason, by the all-pervading illumination of the Buddha's light-rays, have beings been liberated from all evil destinies and established on the path of liberation? How wondrous, O <s>Sugata</s>!' The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'This is not wondrous for Buddhas, <s>Bhagavāns</s>, who have well-accumulated immeasurable stores of merit, O <s>Devendra</s>.'

body.text: devendra samyaksaṃbuddhā aparimitaguṇaratnākarabhūtāḥ / devendra samyaksaṃbuddhānām apramāṇopāyāḥ parmiṣpannāḥ / devendra buddhānāṃ bhagavatām aparimitā prajñopacitā / devendra buddhānām apramāṇā vīryā / buddhena bhagavatāpramānā vineyajanā bhājanībhūtāḥ kṛtāḥ / asamasamajñānābhi buddhā bhagavanto 'samasamarddhisamanvāgatāḥ / bhagavanto 'samasamapraṇidhānasamanvāgatāḥ / tasmād devendra buddhānāṃ bhagavatāṃ yathā bhājanaṃ tathā sattvārthakaraṇañ ca / yathā vineyaṃ tathā sattvānām arthakaraṇañ ca / yathābhiprāyaṃ tathā sattvārthakaraṇaṃ bhavatīti / jñātavyam ity atra saṃśayaśaṅkāvimatir na kartavyā / tathāgatavaineyaṃ na bhavatīti nedaṃ sthānaṃ vidyate /
body.translated_text: '<s>Devendra</s>, the Perfectly Awakened Ones are oceans of immeasurable virtuous jewels. <s>Devendra</s>, the Perfectly Awakened Ones have perfected immeasurable skillful means. <s>Devendra</s>, the <s>Bhagavān</s> Buddhas have accumulated immeasurable wisdom. <s>Devendra</s>, the Buddhas possess immeasurable vigor. By the <s>Bhagavān</s> Buddha, immeasurable beings to be trained have been made into worthy vessels. The <s>Bhagavān</s> Buddhas, with incomparable, peerless knowledge, are endowed with incomparable, peerless powers. The <s>Bhagavāns</s> are endowed with incomparable, peerless vows. Therefore, <s>Devendra</s>, the <s>Bhagavān</s> Buddhas accomplish the welfare of beings according to their capacity, accomplish the welfare of beings according to what can be trained, and accomplish the welfare of beings according to their intentions. This should be known—no doubt, suspicion, or disagreement should be entertained here. That there could be anyone not trainable by the <s>Tathāgata</s>—such a situation does not exist.'

body.text: atha devendraḥ svakīyād āsanād utthāya punar api bhagavato vipulāṃ mahatīṃ pūjāṃ kṛtvā bhagavantam etad avocat / sarvasattvānāṃ hitakaraṇāyānukampākaraṇāya śaraṇakaraṇāya samahākṛpākaraṇāya sarvāśāparipūraṇakaraṇāya bhagavan mama pratibhānam utpādaya sugata mama pratibhānam utpādaya / bhagavan
body.translated_text: Then <s>Devendra</s>, rising from his own seat, again having made vast and great worship to the <s>Bhagavān</s>, said this to the <s>Bhagavān</s>: 'For the sake of benefiting all beings, for showing compassion, for providing refuge, for exercising great mercy, for fulfilling all wishes—<s>Bhagavān</s>, generate inspiration in me! <s>Sugata</s>, generate inspiration in me! <s>Bhagavān</s>,

body.text: itas trayastriṃśaddevanikāyād vimalamaṇiprabhanāmno devaputrasya cyutasya kālagatasya saptadivasā abhūvan / bhagavan sa kutropapannaḥ sukhaṃ duḥkhaṃ vānubhavati / idaṃ bhagavan vyākuru sugata vyākuru / bhagavān āha / devendra prāptakālasamayaṃ jñātvā śroṣyasi / devendra āha / bhagavan ayaṃ kālaḥ / ayaṃ samayaḥ sugata / bhagavān āha / devendra vimalamaṇiprabhanāmadevaputra itaś cyutvāvīcau mahānaraka utpannas tatra dvādaśavarṣasahasrāṇi tīvraṃ kaṭukaṃ duḥkham anubhavati / punar alpanarake daśavarṣasahasrāṇi duḥkham anubhavati / punar api tiryakpreteṣūtpanno daśavarṣasahasrāṇi duḥkham anubhavati / punar api pratyantajanapadeṣūtpanno badhiramūkāvyaktasvabhāvatām anubhavati ṣaṣṭivarṣasahasrāṇi / punar api caturaśītivarṣasahasrāṇi vyādhiraktātisārakuṣṭhavighātapīḍitaś ca bahujananindito 'śeṣaparityakto hīnakulo bhavati / duḥkhaduḥkhaparaṃparāṃ na vicchedayati / anyeṣām apy ahitaṃ karoti / nānākarmāvaraṇāni cāvicchedena karoti / punar apy anyonyaduḥkhaparaṃparām anubhavati /
body.translated_text: from this assembly of the Thirty-Three Gods, the <s>devaputra</s> (divine son) named <s>Vimalamaṇiprabha</s> has passed away and died seven days ago. <s>Bhagavān</s>, where has he been reborn? Does he experience happiness or suffering? Declare this, <s>Bhagavān</s>! Declare this, <s>Sugata</s>!' The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: '<s>Devendra</s>, knowing the appropriate time and occasion, you shall hear.' <s>Devendra</s> said: '<s>Bhagavān</s>, this is the time! This is the occasion, <s>Sugata</s>!' The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: '<s>Devendra</s>, the <s>devaputra</s> named <s>Vimalamaṇiprabha</s>, having passed away from here, has been reborn in the great <s>Avīci</s> hell. There he will experience intense, severe suffering for twelve thousand years. Then in a lesser hell, he will experience suffering for ten thousand years. Then again, reborn among animals and <s>pretas</s> (hungry ghosts), he will experience suffering for ten thousand years. Then again, born in border regions, he will experience the state of being deaf, mute, and inarticulate for sixty thousand years. Then again, for eighty-four thousand years, afflicted by diseases—dysentery, leprosy, and bodily harm—reviled by many people, completely abandoned by all, he will be of low birth. He does not interrupt the succession of suffering upon suffering. He also harms others. He continuously creates various <s>karmāvaraṇas</s> (karmic obstructions). And again he experiences one suffering after another in succession.'

body.text: atha khalu śakrādayaḥ sarvadevaputrāḥ śrutvā bhrāntās trastāḥ khinnā adhomukhaṃ patitāḥ / punar utthāyaivam āhuḥ / kathaṃ bhagavan tasmād duḥkhaparaṃparāto mucyate / kathaṃ sugata mucyate / kenopāyena bhagavan duḥkharāśeḥ tasmān mucyata iti / paritrānaṃ kuru bhagavan / paritrāṇaṃ kuru sugata / bhagavān āha / devendra caturaśītibuddhakoṭibhir bhāṣitam idam aham api bhāṣe śṛṇu / atha khalu devendraḥ punar api bhagavantaṃ māndāravamahāmāndāravapuṣpair nānāvidhair ratnamukuṭakeyūrakarṇālaṃkārahārārdhahārādyanekālaṃkāraviśeṣair abhyarcyānekaśatasahasravāraṃ pradakṣiṇīkṛtya praṇamya sādhu bhagavan sādhu sugateti / sādhukāreṇa harṣayitvā sadevakasya lokasya hitasukhakaraṇāyānāgatānāṃ sattvānām apāyasantativimokṣaṇāya subhāṣitārthaṃ vijñāpayāmi / atha punar api brahmādayo devagaṇā
body.translated_text: Then <s>Śakra</s> and all the <s>devaputras</s>, having heard this, were bewildered, terrified, and distressed, and fell face-downward. Rising again, they said: 'How, <s>Bhagavān</s>, can one be freed from that succession of suffering? How, <s>Sugata</s>, can one be freed? By what means, <s>Bhagavān</s>, can one be freed from that mass of suffering? Grant protection, <s>Bhagavān</s>! Grant protection, <s>Sugata</s>!' The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: '<s>Devendra</s>, what has been spoken by eighty-four <s>koṭīs</s> (tens of millions) of Buddhas, that I too shall speak. Listen!' Then <s>Devendra</s> again worshipped the <s>Bhagavān</s> with <s>māndārava</s> and great <s>māndārava</s> flowers, with various jeweled crowns, armlets, ear ornaments, necklaces, half-necklaces, and many other special ornaments, circumambulated a hundred thousand times, bowed down, and with cries of 'Excellent, <s>Bhagavān</s>! Excellent, <s>Sugata</s>!'—having gladdened him with such acclaim—said: 'For the benefit and happiness of the world with its gods, for the liberation from the continuity of evil destinies of future beings, I request the well-spoken meaning.' Then again <s>Brahmā</s> and the other hosts of gods

body.text: evam āhuḥ / sādhu bhagavan sādhu sugata yenānāgatānāṃ sattvānāṃ nāmamātram api śrutavatām apāyatrayamārgavimokṣo bhavati / svargadevaloke vā manuṣyaloke cotpannānām anuttarasamyaksaṃbodhiprāptyarthaṃ bhāṣatu /
body.translated_text: spoke thus: 'Excellent, <s>Bhagavān</s>! Excellent, <s>Sugata</s>! May you speak so that for future beings, even those who merely hear the name, there will be liberation from the path of the three evil destinies, and for those born in the heavenly realm of the gods or in the human world, for the attainment of supreme, perfect awakening (<s>anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi</s>)!'

body.text: atha khalu bhagavān śakrabrahmādidevaputrāṇāṃ sarvatathāgatahṛdayenādhiṣṭhānārtham amoghavajrādhiṣṭhānanāmasamādhiṃ samāpannaḥ /
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bhagavān</s>, for the purpose of blessing the <s>devaputras</s> led by <s>Śakra</s> and <s>Brahmā</s> with the heart of all <s>Tathāgatas</s>, entered the <s>samādhi</s> called <s>Amoghavajrādhiṣṭhāna</s> (Infallible Vajra Empowerment).
<s>Oṃ vajrādhiṣṭhāna-samaye huṃ</s>

body.text: evañ ca samādhiṃ samāpanno 'nabhibhavanīyavajrādhiṣṭhānenādhiṣṭhāyedaṃ sarvadurgatipariśodhanarājanāmatathāgatahṛdayaṃ niścārayām āsa /
body.translated_text: And having entered that <s>samādhi</s>, through the unconquerable vajra empowerment, he uttered this heart [<s>dhāraṇī</s>] of the <s>Tathāgata</s> called <s>Sarvadurgatipariśodhana-rāja</s> (King of the Purification of All Evil Destinies):

body.text: oṃ śodhane śodhane sarvapāpaviśodhani śuddhe viśuddhe sarvakarmāvaraṇaviśuddhe svāhā /
body.translated_text: <s>Oṃ śodhane śodhane sarva-pāpa-viśodhani śuddhe viśuddhe sarva-karmāvaraṇa-viśuddhe svāhā</s>

body.text: asyā vidyāyā bhāṣaṇānantaram eva sarvasattvānāṃ durgatir vinipātitā sarvanarakatiryakpretagatiḥ śodhitā /
body.translated_text: Immediately upon the utterance of this <s>vidyā</s> (sacred formula), the evil destinies of all beings were cast down, and all the realms of hell, animals, and hungry ghosts were purified.

body.text: tīvraduḥkhāni praśāntāni bahavaś ca jātāḥ sukhīmukhībhūtāḥ / punar aparaṃ guhyahṛdayam abhāṣata /
body.translated_text: Intense sufferings were pacified, and many beings became happy and joyful. Furthermore, he spoke the secret heart [<s>dhāraṇī</s>]:

body.text: oṃ śodhane śodhane śodhaya sarvāpāyān sarvasattvebhyo huṃ punar aparaṃ devendredaṃ sarvatathāgatahṛdayaṃ /
body.translated_text: <s>Oṃ śodhane śodhane śodhaya sarvāpāyān sarva-sattvebhyo huṃ</s>. Furthermore, '<s>Devendra</s>, this is the heart of all <s>Tathāgatas</s>:'
<s>Oṃ sarvāpāya-viśodhani huṃ phaṭ</s>
Furthermore, '<s>Devendra</s>, this is the sub-heart (<s>upahṛdaya</s>) of the heart of all <s>Tathāgatas</s>:'
<s>Oṃ trāṭ</s>

body.text: punar aparaṃ devendra sarvadurgatipariśodhanahṛdayam / huṃ / punar aparaṃ devendra saṃkṣepataḥ smaraṇamātreṇāpy alpapuṇyasattvānāṃ sarvadurgatiśāntikaraṇāyānāyāsato vimokṣaṇakaram idaṃ bhavati /
body.translated_text: Furthermore, '<s>Devendra</s>, this is the heart of the Purification of All Evil Destinies:' <s>Huṃ</s>. Furthermore, '<s>Devendra</s>, in brief, even by mere recollection, for beings of little merit, for the pacification of all evil destinies, this effortlessly brings about liberation:'

body.text: oṃ namo bhagavate sarvadurgatipariśodhanarājāya tathāgatāyārhate samyaksaṃbuddhāya / tadyathā /
body.translated_text: <s>Oṃ namo bhagavate Sarvadurgatipariśodhana-rājāya tathāgatāyārhate samyak-saṃbuddhāya</s>. Namely:

body.text: oṃ śodhane śodhane sarvapāpaviśodhani śuddhe viśuddhe sarvakarmāvaraṇaviśodhani svāhā / mūlavidyā /
body.translated_text: <s>Oṃ śodhane śodhane sarva-pāpa-viśodhani śuddhe viśuddhe sarva-karmāvaraṇa-viśodhani svāhā</s>. [This is] the root <s>vidyā</s> (fundamental sacred formula).

body.text:
oṃ sarvavit sarvāvaraṇāni viśodhaya hana huṃ phaṭ /
oṃ sarvavid huṃ /
oṃ sarvavid hrīḥ phaṭ /
oṃ sarvavid aḥ / oṃ sarvavit trāṃ trāṭ / oṃ sarvavid oṃ /
oṃ sarvavid dhīm / oṃ sarvavid huṃ / oṃ sarvavit krīṃ traṭ /
oṃ sarvavid mahāvajrodbhavadānapāramitāpūje huṃ / lāsyāyā mantraḥ /
oṃ sarvavid mahāvajrodbhavaśīlapāramitāpūje trāṃ / mālāyā mantraḥ /
oṃ sarvavid mahāvajrodbhavakṣāntipāramitāpūje hrīḥ / gītāyā mantraḥ /
oṃ sarvavid mahāvajrodbhavavīryapāramitāpūje aḥ / nṛtyāyā mantraḥ /
oṃ sarvavit sarvāpāyaviśodhani dhama dhama dhyānapāramitāpūje huṃ huṃ phaṭ / dhūpāyā mantraḥ /
oṃ sarvavit sarva durgatipariśodhane kleśopakleśacchedani puṣpālokini prajñāpāramitāpūje trāṃ huṃ phaṭ / puṣpāyā mantraḥ /
oṃ sarvavit sarvāpāyaviśodhani jñānālokakari praṇidhipāramitāpūje hrīḥ huṃ phaṭ / dīpāyā mantraḥ /
oṃ sarvavit sarvāpāyagandhanāśani vajragandhopāyapāramitāpūje aḥ huṃ phaṭ / gandhāyā mantraḥ /
oṃ sarvavid narakagatyākarṣaṇi huṃ jaḥ phaṭ / vajrāṅkuśasya mantraḥ /
oṃ sarvavid narakoddharaṇi huṃ huṃ phaṭ / vajrapāśasya mantraḥ /
oṃ sarvavit sarvāpāyabandhanamocani huṃ vaṃ phaṭ / vajrasphoṭasya mantraḥ /
oṃ sarvavit sarvāpāyagatigahanaviśodhani huṃ hoḥ phat / vajrāveśasya mantraḥ /
oṃ maitrīyaharaṇāya svāhā / maitreyasya mantraḥ /
oṃ amoghe amoghadarśini huṃ / amoghadarśinaḥ /
body.translated_text:
<s>Oṃ sarvavit sarvāvaraṇāni viśodhaya hana huṃ phaṭ</s>.
<s>Oṃ sarvavid huṃ</s>.
<s>Oṃ sarvavid hrīḥ phaṭ</s>.
<s>Oṃ sarvavid aḥ</s>. <s>Oṃ sarvavit trāṃ trāṭ</s>. <s>Oṃ sarvavid oṃ</s>.
<s>Oṃ sarvavid dhīṃ</s>. <s>Oṃ sarvavid huṃ</s>. <s>Oṃ sarvavit krīṃ traṭ</s>.
<s>Oṃ sarvavid mahāvajrodbhava-dāna-pāramitā-pūje huṃ</s>—the <s>mantra</s> of <s>Lāsyā</s>.
<s>Oṃ sarvavid mahāvajrodbhava-śīla-pāramitā-pūje trāṃ</s>—the <s>mantra</s> of <s>Mālā</s>.
<s>Oṃ sarvavid mahāvajrodbhava-kṣānti-pāramitā-pūje hrīḥ</s>—the <s>mantra</s> of <s>Gītā</s>.
<s>Oṃ sarvavid mahāvajrodbhava-vīrya-pāramitā-pūje aḥ</s>—the <s>mantra</s> of <s>Nṛtyā</s>.
<s>Oṃ sarvavit sarvāpāya-viśodhani dhama dhama dhyāna-pāramitā-pūje huṃ huṃ phaṭ</s>—the <s>mantra</s> of <s>Dhūpā</s> (incense).
<s>Oṃ sarvavit sarva-durgati-pariśodhane kleśopakleśa-cchedani puṣpālokini prajñā-pāramitā-pūje trāṃ huṃ phaṭ</s>—the <s>mantra</s> of <s>Puṣpā</s> (flowers).
<s>Oṃ sarvavit sarvāpāya-viśodhani jñānāloka-kari praṇidhi-pāramitā-pūje hrīḥ huṃ phaṭ</s>—the <s>mantra</s> of <s>Dīpā</s> (lamp).
<s>Oṃ sarvavit sarvāpāya-gandha-nāśani vajragandha-upāya-pāramitā-pūje aḥ huṃ phaṭ</s>—the <s>mantra</s> of <s>Gandhā</s> (perfume).
<s>Oṃ sarvavid naraka-gaty-ākarṣaṇi huṃ jaḥ phaṭ</s>—the <s>mantra</s> of <s>Vajrāṅkuśa</s> (vajra hook).
<s>Oṃ sarvavid narakoddharaṇi huṃ huṃ phaṭ</s>—the <s>mantra</s> of <s>Vajrapāśa</s> (vajra noose).
<s>Oṃ sarvavit sarvāpāya-bandhana-mocani huṃ vaṃ phaṭ</s>—the <s>mantra</s> of <s>Vajrasphoṭa</s> (vajra chain).
<s>Oṃ sarvavit sarvāpāya-gati-gahana-viśodhani huṃ hoḥ phaṭ</s>—the <s>mantra</s> of <s>Vajrāveśa</s> (vajra bell).
<s>Oṃ maitrīya-haraṇāya svāhā</s>—the <s>mantra</s> of <s>Maitreya</s>.
<s>Oṃ amoghe amogha-darśini huṃ</s>—the <s>mantra</s> of <s>Amoghadarśin</s>.

body.text:
oṃ sarvāpāyajahe sarvāpāyaviśodhani huṃ / sarvāpāyajahasya/
oṃ sarvaśokatamonirghātanamati huṃ / sarvaśokatamonirghātanamateḥ /
oṃ gandhahastini huṃ / gandhahastinaḥ /
oṃ śūraṃgame huṃ / śūraṃgamasya /
oṃ gagane gaganalocane huṃ / gaganagañjasya /
oṃ jñānaketo jñānavati huṃ / jñānaketoḥ /
om amṛtaprabhe amṛtavati huṃ / amṛtaprabhasya /
oṃ candrasthe candravyavalokini svāhā / candraprabhasya /
oṃ bhadravati bhadrapāle / bhadrapālasya /
oṃ jālini mahājālini huṃ / jālinīprabhasya /
oṃ vajragarbhe huṃ / vajragarbhasya /
om akṣaye huṃ huṃ akṣayakarmāvaraṇaviśodhani svāhā / akṣayamateḥ /
oṃ pratibhāne pratibhānakūṭe svāhā / pratibhānakūṭasya /
oṃ samantabhadre huṃ / samantabhadrasya /
body.translated_text:
Oṃ <s>sarvāpāyajahe</s> (remover of all evil destinies) <s>sarvāpāyaviśodhani</s> (purifier of all evil destinies) huṃ / [mantra] of <s>Sarvāpāyajaha</s> /
Oṃ <s>sarvaśokatamonirghātanamati</s> (intelligence that dispels all sorrow and darkness) huṃ / [mantra] of <s>Sarvaśokatamonirghātanamati</s> /
Oṃ <s>gandhahastini</s> (fragrant-elephant one) huṃ / [mantra] of <s>Gandhahastin</s> /
Oṃ <s>śūraṃgame</s> (heroic-goer) huṃ / [mantra] of <s>Śūraṃgama</s> /
Oṃ <s>gagane gaganalocane</s> (O sky! sky-eyed one!) huṃ / [mantra] of <s>Gaganagañja</s> /
Oṃ <s>jñānaketo jñānavati</s> (O wisdom-banner! wisdom-possessing one!) huṃ / [mantra] of <s>Jñānaketu</s> /
Oṃ <s>amṛtaprabhe amṛtavati</s> (O immortal-radiance! immortality-possessing one!) huṃ / [mantra] of <s>Amṛtaprabha</s> /
Oṃ <s>candrasthe candravyavalokini</s> (O moon-dwelling one! moon-gazing one!) svāhā / [mantra] of <s>Candraprabha</s> /
Oṃ <s>bhadravati bhadrapāle</s> (O auspicious one! guardian of the good!) / [mantra] of <s>Bhadrapāla</s> /
Oṃ <s>jālini mahājālini</s> (O net-bearer! great net-bearer!) huṃ / [mantra] of <s>Jālinīprabha</s> /
Oṃ <s>vajragarbhe</s> (O vajra-embryo!) huṃ / [mantra] of <s>Vajragarbha</s> /
Oṃ <s>akṣaye</s> (O inexhaustible one!) huṃ huṃ <s>akṣayakarmāvaraṇaviśodhani</s> (purifier of the inexhaustible obscurations of karma) svāhā / [mantra] of <s>Akṣayamati</s> /
Oṃ <s>pratibhāne pratibhānakūṭe</s> (O eloquence! peak of eloquence!) svāhā / [mantra] of <s>Pratibhānakūṭa</s> /
Oṃ <s>samantabhadre</s> (O universally auspicious one!) huṃ / [mantra] of <s>Samantabhadra</s> /

body.text: ete bhadrakalpikasya bodhisattvasya mantrān yathākramam uccārayet /
body.translated_text: One should recite these mantras of the <s>Bhadrakalpika</s> (Fortunate Aeon) <s>Bodhisattvas</s> in their proper sequence.

body.text: anena yathoktatantrānusārānukrameṇa vidhānena pratyahaṃ prabhātakāla utpattikrameṇa bhāvayamāno bhāvayet / devatāyogaṃ samādhitrayam uttamaṃ yatnato durgatipariśodhanasiddhir bhavati / punar aparaṃ devendra sarvadurgatipariśodhanatejorājasya tathāgatasya guhyahṛdayam idam / kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā yaḥ kaścid nāmamātraṃ śṛṇoti dhārayati vācayati likhitvā ca śirasi śikhāyāṃ vā bāhau grīvāyāṃ vā baddhvā dhārayati tasyehaiva janmany aṣṭāv akālamaraṇāni nmaraṇasaṃbandhasvapnaprakārā
body.translated_text: By this procedure, following the sequence as stated in the <s>tantra</s>, one should meditate daily at dawn through the generation stage (<s>utpattikrama</s>). Through diligent [practice of] the deity-yoga (<s>devatāyoga</s>) and the three supreme <s>samādhis</s> (concentrations), the accomplishment of the purification of evil destinies is achieved. Furthermore, O Lord of Gods (<s>Devendra</s>), this is the secret heart [<s>dhāraṇī</s>] of the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Sarvadurgatipariśodhanatejarāja</s>. Whatever son of good family or daughter of good family hears even merely the name [of this <s>dhāraṇī</s>], retains it, recites it, or having written it, binds it on the head, on the topknot, on the arm, or on the neck and bears it—for that person, in this very life, the eight kinds of untimely death, dream-experiences related to death,

body.text:
vā durgatinimittāni vā tāni sarvāṇi svapnamātrato nopasarpanti / maṇḍalañ ca yathāvat praveśyābhiṣikto hṛdayañ ca japtvā mantrārthaṃ ye kecid bhāvayanti kaḥ punar vādas tesāṃ yāni kānicit pāpāni na nikaṭībhavantīti na durgatiṃ gacchantīti /
puruṣastrīdevanāgayakṣarākṣasapretatiryagnarakādīnāṃ yeṣāṃ keṣāñcit mṛtakāyeṣu maṇḍalaṃ praveśyābhiśikteṣu te narakeṣūtpannāḥ samanantaram evaṃ vimucyante devanikāyeṣūtpadyante / tatrotpannāḥ santaḥ sarvatathāgatānāṃ dharmatām abhimukhīkurvanty avaivartikāś ca bhavanti / santatiś ca niyatā bhavati / sarvatathāgatakule prajātāś ca bhavanti / prahīṇāvaraṇāś ca / sarvatathāgatakuleṣu devakuleṣu vānyasmin vā sukham anubhavanti / devendra saṃkṣepato laukikalokottarasarvahitasukham anubhavanti /
body.translated_text:
or omens of evil destinies—all of these do not come near, even in dreams. And what more need be said of those who, having been properly initiated into the <s>maṇḍala</s> and consecrated, recite the heart [mantra] and meditate on the meaning of the mantra—whatever sins there may be do not come near them, and they do not go to evil destinies.
For those among men, women, gods, <s>Nāgas</s>, <s>Yakṣas</s>, <s>Rākṣasas</s>, <s>Pretas</s>, animals, hell-beings, and others—whoever they may be—whose dead bodies are initiated into the <s>maṇḍala</s> and consecrated, those who have been born in the hells are immediately liberated and are reborn in the divine assemblies. Having been born there, they turn toward the <s>dharmatā</s> (true nature of reality) of all <s>Tathāgatas</s> and become non-retrogressing (<s>avaivartika</s>). Their continuity becomes fixed. They are born in the families of all <s>Tathāgatas</s>. Their obscurations are abandoned. In the families of all <s>Tathāgatas</s>, in divine families, or in other [fortunate states], they experience happiness. O <s>Devendra</s>, in brief, they experience all mundane and supramundane benefit and happiness.

body.text: atha devendro bhagavantaṃ pūrvavat pradakṣiṇīkṛtya vanditvaivam āha / bhagavan sarvadurgativaśībhūtānāṃ hitasukhakaraṇāya yathāsattvaiḥ sarvadurgatipṛṣṭhīkaraṇāyānāyāsato 'nuttarasamyaksaṃbodhyadhigamārthaṃ dharmaṃ deśayatu /
body.translated_text: Then <s>Devendra</s> (Lord of Gods), having circumambulated the <s>Bhagavān</s> as before and saluted him, spoke thus: 'O <s>Bhagavān</s>, for the sake of bringing benefit and happiness to all those who are under the power of evil destinies, so that beings may put all evil destinies behind them and effortlessly attain unsurpassed perfect awakening (<s>anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi</s>), please teach the <s>Dharma</s>.'

body.text: atha khalu bhagavān śākyamuniḥ sarvadurgatipariśodhanajñānavajranāmasamādhiṃ samāpadya sarvatathāgatasarvadurgatipariśodhanatejorājanāmamaṇḍalam abhāṣata /
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bhagavān</s> <s>Śākyamuni</s>, having entered the <s>samādhi</s> (concentration) called <s>Sarvadurgatipariśodhanajñānavajra</s> (Vajra of the Wisdom that Purifies All Evil Destinies), proclaimed the <s>maṇḍala</s> called <s>Sarvatathāgata-sarvadurgati-pariśodhana-tejorāja</s> (Radiance-King that Purifies All Evil Destinies of All Tathāgatas).
That <s>sādhana</s> (method of accomplishment) was spoken by the Lord of the <s>Śākyas</s>.

body.text: prathamaṃ tāvad yogī vijane mano 'nukūlapradeśe mṛdusukumārāsane niṣaṇṇaḥ sugandhena maṇḍalaṃ kṛtvā pañcopahārapūjā karaṇīyā / tataḥ sarvadharmanairātmyaṃ bhāvayitvā / ātmānaṃ huṃkāreṇa vajrajvālānalārkaṃ bhāvayet / tasya kaṇṭhe hrīḥkāreṇa padmaṃ tasyopari dalāgra ākāreṇa candramaṇḍalaṃ tasyopari huṃkāreṇa pañcasūcikavajram / tad vajraṃ jihvāyāṃ rīṇaṃ bhavati / vajrajihveti / tena vajrajihvā bhavati / mantrajāpakṣamo bhavet / hastadvayasya madhye sitākāreṇa candramaṇḍalaṃ tasyopari huṃkāreṇa pañcasūcikavajram / tad vajraṃ karamadhye nilīyate vajrahasto bhavati /
body.translated_text: First, the <s>yogī</s>, seated on a soft and delicate seat in a secluded place agreeable to the mind, having made a <s>maṇḍala</s> with fragrance, should perform the five offerings (<s>pañcopahāra</s>). Then, having meditated on the selflessness of all phenomena (<s>sarvadharma-nairātmya</s>), one should visualize oneself through the syllable HŪṂ as a vajra-flame-fire-sun. At one's throat, through the syllable HRĪḤ, [visualize] a lotus; upon it, at the tip of the petal, through the syllable Ā, a moon-disc; upon that, through the syllable HŪṂ, a five-pronged vajra. That vajra dissolves into the tongue—[this is called] 'vajra-tongue.' By that, one obtains a vajra-tongue and becomes capable of <s>mantra</s>-recitation. In the center of both hands, through the white syllable Ā, [visualize] a moon-disc; upon that, through the syllable HŪṂ, a five-pronged vajra. That vajra merges into the center of the palm—one becomes vajra-handed.
One becomes capable of binding all <s>mudrās</s> (ritual gestures).
Then the visualization of the protection-wheel (<s>rakṣācakra</s>) should be performed.

body.text:
oṃ gṛhṇa vajrasamaye huṃ vam / iti bruvan krodhaterintirīṃ badhnīyāt /
vajrabandhaṃ tale kṛtvā cchādayet kruddhamānasaḥ // gāḍham aṅguṣṭhavajreṇa krodhaterintir smṛtā //
body.translated_text:
Oṃ gṛhṇa vajrasamaye huṃ vaṃ / Speaking thus, one should bind the <s>Krodhaterintirī</s> [mudrā].
Having made the vajra-bond at the base, one should cover [the space] with wrathful mind. // Firmly, with the thumb-vajra, [this] is known as the <s>Krodhaterintirī</s> //

body.text: tato vajrārdhāsananiṣaṇṇo vajraterintirīṃ baddhvā vajramālābhiṣekaṃ gṛhṇīyāt /
body.translated_text: Then, seated in the vajra half-posture (<s>vajrārdhāsana</s>), having bound the <s>Vajraterintirī</s> [mudrā], one should receive the vajra-garland consecration (<s>vajramālābhiṣeka</s>).

body.text: oṃ vajrajvālānalārka huṃ abhiṣiñca mām iti /
body.translated_text: Oṃ vajrajvālānalārka huṃ—'Consecrate me!' Thus.

body.text: vajrabandhe 'ṅguṣṭhadvayaṃ sahitotthitaṃ vajrabandhasyopari śliṣṭhaṃ dhārayet / vajraterintirī /
body.translated_text: In the vajra-bond, both thumbs raised together should be held joined above the vajra-bond. [This is] the <s>Vajraterintirī</s> [mudrā].

body.text:
oṃ ṭuṃ iti / anena dvyakṣarakavacena kavacayitvā /
oṃ vajrajvālānalārka huṃ ity udīrayet /
body.translated_text:
Oṃ ṭuṃ—thus. Having armored oneself with this two-syllable armor [mantra],
one should utter: Oṃ vajrajvālānalārka huṃ.

body.text: vāmavajramuṣṭiṃ hṛdaye kṛtvā dakṣiṇavajramuṣṭim ullālayan sarvavighnān hanyāt /
body.translated_text: Having placed the left vajra-fist at the heart, one should raise the right vajra-fist upward to strike away all obstacles.
Then, with the vajra-fire together with the <s>mudrā</s>, one should perform the burning of obstacles and so forth.

body.text: oṃ vajrānala hana daha paca matha bhañja rana huṃ phaṭ
body.translated_text: Oṃ vajrānala hana daha paca matha bhañja rana huṃ phaṭ

body.text: ity udīrayet / abhyantaravajrabandhe 'ṅgulijvālāgarbhe 'ṅguṣṭhavajram utthitam iyaṃ vajrānalamudrā /
body.translated_text: Thus one should utter. In the inner vajra-bond, with the finger-flames as the core and the thumb-vajra raised—this is the <s>Vajrānala-mudrā</s> (vajra-fire seal).

body.text: tad anu / vajranetri bandha sarvavighnān iti / mudrāyuktyā sarvavighnabandhaṃ kuryāt / vajrabandhaṃ baddhvāṅguṣṭhadvayaṃ prasārya samaṃ dhārayet / vajranetrimudrā /
body.translated_text: After that: '<s>Vajranetri</s>, bind all obstacles!'—thus. With the <s>mudrā</s>-method, one should perform the binding of all obstacles. Having bound the vajra-bond, one should extend both thumbs evenly. [This is] the <s>Vajranetrī-mudrā</s>.
Having placed the extended vajra-bond on the ground, one should make the downward binding.

body.text: oṃ vajra dṛḍho me bhava rakṣa sarvān svāhā /
body.translated_text: Oṃ vajra, be firm for me! Protect all! Svāhā!
With the <s>Vajrabhairavanetra</s> (Vajra-Terrible-Eye) together with the <s>mudrā</s>, one should make the upward binding.

body.text: oṃ hulu hulu huṃ phat / iti /
body.translated_text: Oṃ hulu hulu huṃ phaṭ! Thus.

body.text: vajramuṣṭidvayaṃ baddhvālātacakraṃ bhrāmayitvā śirasopari tarjanyaṅkuśākāreṇa dhārayet / vajrabhairavanetramudrā / tasyādhastād vajrayakṣeṇa mudrāsahitena punar bandhaṃ kuryāt /
body.translated_text: Having bound both vajra-fists, having whirled them like a firebrand-wheel, one should hold them above the head with the forefingers in hook-shape. [This is] the <s>Vajrabhairavanetra-mudrā</s>. Below that, with <s>Vajrayakṣa</s> together with the <s>mudrā</s>, one should again make a binding.

body.text: oṃ vajrayakṣa huṃ iti / vajrāñjaler aṅguṣṭhadvayaṃ prasāritaṃ tarjanīdvayaṃ damṣṭrā / vajrayakṣamudrā /
body.translated_text: Oṃ vajrayakṣa huṃ—thus. From the vajra-añjali, both thumbs extended, both forefingers [forming] fangs—[this is] the <s>Vajrayakṣa-mudrā</s>.
With <s>Vajroṣṇīṣa</s> (Vajra-Crown) together with the <s>mudrā</s>, one should bind the eastern direction.

body.text: oṃ druṃ bandha haṃ iti / druṃ 'iti vā /
body.translated_text: Oṃ druṃ bandha haṃ—thus. Or [simply] druṃ.

body.text: vajramuṣṭidvayaṃ kanyasāśrṅkhalābandhena tarjanīdvayasūcīmukhaṃ parivartoṣṇīṣe sthāpayet / vajroṣṇīṣamudrā /
body.translated_text: Having bound both vajra-fists, with a chain-binding from the two tips of the last [fingers], one should place both forefingers with needle-tips on the revolving crown. [This is] the <s>Vajroṣṇīṣa-mudrā</s>.
Again, with <s>Vajrapāśa</s> (Vajra-Noose), one should bind that same [direction].

body.text: huṃ vajrapāśe hrīḥ iti / vajramuṣṭidvayena bāhugranthiṃ kuryāt / vajrapāśamudrā /
body.translated_text: Huṃ vajrapāśe hrīḥ—thus. With both vajra-fists, one should make an arm-knot. [This is] the <s>Vajrapāśa-mudrā</s>.
With <s>Vajrapatākā</s> (Vajra-Banner), one should bind the western direction.

body.text: oṃ vajrapatāke pataṃgini raṭeti / vajrabandhe 'ṅguṣṭhasattvaparyaṅkasūcīṃ kṛtvāgrāsamānāmāvidāritāntyapaṭāgrī / vajrapatākāyāḥ /
body.translated_text: Oṃ vajrapatāke pataṃgini raṭa—thus. In the vajra-bond, making the thumb-being cross-legged needle, with the fingertips drawn together equally, the tip of the last finger-cloth [extended]—[this is the mudrā] of <s>Vajrapatākā</s>.

body.text: digvidikṣv adha ūrdhvañ ca vighnanikṛntanaṃ kuryāt / vajrakālyottarāṃ diśaṃ bandhet /
body.translated_text: In all directions and intermediate directions, below and above, one should perform the cutting of obstacles. With <s>Vajrakālī</s>, one should bind the northern direction.

body.text: hrīḥ vajrakāli ruṭ maṭ / iti / vajrayakṣamudrām eva mukhe dṛḍhīkṛtya vajrakālyāḥ / vajraśikharayā dakṣiṇāṃ diśaṃ bandhet /
body.translated_text: Hrīḥ vajrakāli ruṭ maṭ—thus. Having firmly fixed the <s>Vajrayakṣa-mudrā</s> itself at the mouth—[this is the mudrā] of <s>Vajrakālī</s>. With <s>Vajraśikhara</s> (Vajra-Peak), one should bind the southern direction.

body.text: oṃ vajraśikhare ruṭ maṭ / iti / vajramuṣṭidvayena parvatotkarṣaṇābhinayākāraṃ vajraśikharāyāḥ /
body.translated_text: Oṃ vajraśikhare ruṭ maṭ—thus. With both vajra-fists, [performing] the gesture of extracting a mountain—[this is the mudrā] of <s>Vajraśikhara</s>.
With <s>Vajrakarman</s> (Vajra-Action), having made the <s>maṇḍala</s>-binding, one should place the enclosure.

body.text: huṃ vajrakarmeti / punar abhyantaraprākāraṃ vajrahuṃkāreṇa huṃ iti / vajramuṣṭidvayaṃ baddhvā bāhuvajraṃ samādhāya kaniṣṭhāṅkuśabandhitā trilokavijayanāmatarjanīdvayaṃ tarjanī / vajrahuṃkārasya / iyam eva madhyāgradvayaṃ vajraṃ vajrakarmaṇaḥ /
body.translated_text: Huṃ vajrakarma—thus. Again, the inner enclosure with the vajra-HŪṂ-sound: huṃ—thus. Having bound both vajra-fists, placing the arm-vajra, with the little fingers bound as hooks—the two forefingers [called] <s>Trilokavijayanāma</s> (Conqueror of the Three Worlds)—forefingers [forming the mudrā] of <s>Vajrahuṃkāra</s>. This same [mudrā] with the two tips of the middle [fingers as] vajra is [the mudrā] of <s>Vajrakarman</s>.
Then, with the <s>Vajracakra-mudrā</s> (Vajra-Wheel seal), one should produce the <s>Sarvadurgatipariśodhana-maṇḍala</s> before oneself.
Oṃ vajracakra huṃ—thus.
Having bound both vajra-fists, from the vajra-binding of the two tips of the last [fingers],
the one known as <s>Vajracakra</s> (Vajra-Wheel) accomplishes all <s>maṇḍalas</s>.

body.text: anayā sarvadikṣu pradakṣiṇatayā bhrāmayitvā sarvamaṇḍalanirmāṇaṃ bhavati / imām eva mukhe nyasya nirīkṣamāṇo 'ṣṭau vārān vajracakraṃ japet /
body.translated_text: Having whirled this [mudrā] clockwise in all directions, the creation of all <s>maṇḍalas</s> takes place. Placing this same [mudrā] at the mouth and gazing [at it], one should recite the vajra-wheel [mantra] eight times.

body.text: tataḥ pratyakṣam iva maṇḍalaṃ buddhyālagyapuṣpādibhiḥ saṃpūjya sarvadikṣu pañcamaṇḍalakena praṇamed anena /
body.translated_text: Then, as if the <s>maṇḍala</s> were directly visible, having worshiped it with offerings such as unattached flowers and the like conceived by the mind, one should bow in all directions with the five-<s>maṇḍala</s> [prostration] using this [formula]:

body.text: oṃ sarvavit kāyavākcittapraṇāmena vajrabandhanaṃ karomīti / tataś catuḥpraṇāmaṃ kuryāt / tadyathā /
body.translated_text: Oṃ <s>Sarvavit</s> (All-Knowing One), with the prostration of body, speech, and mind, I make the vajra-bond!—thus. Then one should make the four prostrations, namely:

body.text: sarvaśarīreṇa vajrāñjaliprasāritena pūrvasyāṃ diśi praṇamed anena /
body.translated_text: With the entire body, with the vajra-añjali extended, one should prostrate in the eastern direction using this [formula]:

body.text: oṃ sarvavit pūjopasthānāyātmānaṃ niryātayāmi / sarvatathāgatavajrasattvādhitiṣṭhasva mām / iti /
body.translated_text: 'Oṃ <s>Sarvavit</s>, I surrender myself for the purpose of worship and attendance! All <s>Tathāgata</s>-<s>Vajrasattvas</s>, please empower me!'—thus.

body.text: tatas tathaivotthāya vajrāñjaliṃ hṛdi kṛtvā dakṣiṇasyāṃ diśi lalāṭeṇa bhūmiṃ spṛśan praṇamed anena /
body.translated_text: Then, having risen in the same manner, placing the vajra-añjali at the heart, touching the ground with the forehead in the southern direction, one should prostrate using this [formula]:

body.text: oṃ sarvavit pūjābhiṣekāyātmānaṃ niryātayāmi / sarvatathāgatavajraratnābhiṣiñca mām / iti /
body.translated_text: 'Oṃ <s>Sarvavit</s>, I surrender myself for the purpose of the worship-consecration! All <s>Tathāgata</s>-<s>Vajraratnas</s> (Vajra-Jewels), please consecrate me!'—thus.

body.text: tatas tathaivotthāya vajrāñjalibandhena śirasā paścimāyāṃ diśi mukhena bhūmiṃ spṛśan praṇamed anena /
body.translated_text: Then, having risen in the same manner, with the vajra-añjali bound, with the head [bowed], touching the ground with the face in the western direction, one should prostrate using this [formula]:

body.text: oṃ sarvavit pūjāpravartanāyātmānaṃ niryātayāmi / sarvatathāgatavajradharma pravartaya mām / iti /
body.translated_text: 'Oṃ <s>Sarvavit</s>, I surrender myself for the purpose of turning the worship [wheel]! All <s>Tathāgata</s>-<s>Vajradharmas</s>, please turn me [in the Dharma]!'—thus.

body.text: tatas tathaivotthito vajrāñjaliṃ śiraso 'vatārya hṛdi kṛtvottarasyāṃ diśi mūrdhnā bhūmiṃ spṛśan praṇamed anena /
body.translated_text: Then, having risen in the same manner, bringing down the vajra-añjali from the head and placing it at the heart, touching the ground with the crown of the head in the northern direction, one should prostrate using this [formula]:

body.text: oṃ sarvavit pūjākarmaṇā ātmānaṃ niryātayāmi / sarvatathāgatavajrakarma kuruṣva mām / iti /
body.translated_text: 'Oṃ <s>Sarvavit</s>, I surrender myself for the purpose of worship-activity! All <s>Tathāgata</s>-<s>Vajrakarmas</s>, please act upon me!'—thus.

body.text: jānumaṇḍaladvayaṃ pṛthivyāṃ pratiṣṭhāpya vajrāñjaliṃ hṛdi kṛtvā sarvapāpaṃ pratideśayet /
body.translated_text: Having placed both knee-circles on the ground and placing the vajra-añjali at the heart, one should confess all sins.

body.text: samanvāharantu māṃ daśasu dikṣu sarvabuddhabodhisattvāḥ sarvatathāgatavajramaṇipadmakarmakulāvasthitāś ca sarvamudrāmantravidyādevatā aham amukavajro daśasu dikṣu sarvabuddhabodhisattvānāṃ purataḥ sarvatathāgatavajramaṇipadmakarmakulāvasthitānāṃ sarvamudrāmantravidyādevatānāṃ ca purataḥ sarvapāpaṃ pratideśayāmi /
body.translated_text: May all <s>Buddhas</s> and <s>Bodhisattvas</s> in the ten directions attend to me, as well as all <s>mudrā</s>-<s>mantra</s>-<s>vidyā</s> deities abiding in the families of all <s>Tathāgata</s>-Vajra, -Jewel, -Lotus, and -Action! I, [named] so-and-so Vajra, in the presence of all <s>Buddhas</s> and <s>Bodhisattvas</s> in the ten directions, in the presence of all <s>mudrā</s>-<s>mantra</s>-<s>vidyā</s> deities abiding in the families of all <s>Tathāgata</s>-Vajra, -Jewel, -Lotus, and -Action, I confess all sins.

body.text: vistareṇa daśasu dikṣv atītānāgatapratyutpannānāṃ sarvabuddhabodhisattvapratyekabuddhāryaśrāvakasamyaggatasamyakpratipannānāṃ sarvasattvanikāyānāṃ ca sarvapuṇyam anumodayāmi / daśasu dikṣu sarvabuddhān bhagavataḥ / apravartitadharmacakrān adhyeṣe dharmacakrapravartanāya / daśasu dikṣu sarvabuddhān bhagavataḥ parinirvātukāmān yāce 'parinirvāṇāya /
body.translated_text: Extensively, I rejoice in all the merit of all <s>Buddhas</s>, <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s>, noble <s>Śrāvakas</s>, those who have gone rightly, those who are rightly practicing, and all assemblies of beings in the ten directions—past, future, and present. I request all <s>Buddhas</s> <s>Bhagavāns</s> in the ten directions who have not yet turned the wheel of <s>Dharma</s> to turn the wheel of <s>Dharma</s>. I beseech all <s>Buddhas</s> <s>Bhagavāns</s> in the ten directions who wish to enter <s>parinirvāṇa</s> not to enter <s>parinirvāṇa</s>.

body.text:
tataḥ puṣpamudrāṃ baddhvaivaṃ vadet /
oṃ sarvavit puṣpapūjāmeghasamudraspharaṇasamaye huṃ / iti /
body.translated_text:
Then, having bound the flower-<s>mudrā</s>, one should say thus:
Oṃ <s>Sarvavit</s>, at the time of the spreading of the ocean-cloud of flower-offering, huṃ!—thus.

body.text:
dhūpamudrāṃ baddhvaivaṃ vadet /
oṃ sarvavid dhūpapūjāmeghasamudraspharaṇasamaye huṃ /
body.translated_text:
Having bound the incense-<s>mudrā</s>, one should say thus:
Oṃ <s>Sarvavit</s>, at the time of the spreading of the ocean-cloud of incense-offering, huṃ!

body.text:
dīpamudrāṃ baddhvaivaṃ vadet /
oṃ sarvavid ālokapūjāmeghasamudraspharaṇasamaye huṃ /
body.translated_text:
Having bound the lamp-<s>mudrā</s>, one should say thus:
Oṃ <s>Sarvavit</s>, at the time of the spreading of the ocean-cloud of light-offering, huṃ!

body.text:
gandhamudrāṃ baddhvaivaṃ vadet /
oṃ sarvavid gandhapūjāmeghasamudraspharaṇasamaye huṃ /
body.translated_text:
Having bound the perfume-<s>mudrā</s>, one should say thus:
Oṃ <s>Sarvavit</s>, at the time of the spreading of the ocean-cloud of perfume-offering, huṃ!

body.text:
saṃpuṭānjaliṃ baddhvaivaṃ vadet /
oṃ sarvavid bodhyaṅgaratnālaṃkārapūjāmeghasamudraspharaṇasamaye huṃ / iti /
body.translated_text: Having formed the cupped <s>añjali</s> (joined palms), one should say thus: "Oṃ <s>Sarvavid</s>, at the time of the spreading of the ocean-cloud of offering adorned with the jewels of the <s>bodhyaṅgas</s> (factors of awakening), Hūṃ." Thus.
"Oṃ <s>Sarvavid</s>, at the time of the spreading of the ocean-cloud of unsurpassed offering of laughter, dance, passion, play, and bliss, Hūṃ." Thus.
"Oṃ <s>Sarvavid</s>, at the time of the spreading of the ocean-cloud of unsurpassed garment offering, Hūṃ." Thus.

body.text: tataḥ sarvasattvasaṃsāraduḥkham anusmṛtya bhagavato vajrasattvasya karmamudrāṃ baddhvā karuṇāvaśena sarvasattvottāraṇāya bodhicittam utpādayet / atīrṇatāraṇāyāmuktamocanāyānāśvastāśvāsanāyāparinirvṛtaparinirvātanāya sakalasattvadhātoḥ saṃsārasamudrād uttāraṇāya ca /
body.translated_text: Then, recollecting the suffering of <s>saṃsāra</s> of all beings, having formed the <s>karmamudrā</s> (action-seal) of <s>Bhagavān</s> <s>Vajrasattva</s>, out of compassion one should generate <s>bodhicitta</s> (the mind of awakening) for the deliverance of all beings — for ferrying across those not yet crossed, for liberating those not yet freed, for comforting those not yet comforted, for leading to complete <s>parinirvāṇa</s> those not yet passed into <s>parinirvāṇa</s>, and for lifting up the entire realm of beings from the ocean of <s>saṃsāra</s>.
"Oṃ <s>Sarvavid</s>, at the time of the spreading of the ocean-cloud of <s>vajra</s> offering, Hūṃ." Thus.

body.text:
tato lāsyāmudrāṃ baddhvaivaṃ vadet /
sarvasattvāḥ sarvopakaraṇasamanvāgatā bhavantu / icchāmātrapratibaddhasarvasaṃpattayaḥ /
body.translated_text: Then, having formed the <s>lāsyā-mudrā</s> (dance-seal), one should say thus: "May all beings be endowed with all requisites! May all prosperities be bound only by their wishes!"
"Oṃ <s>Sarvavid</s>, at the time of the spreading of the ocean-cloud of offering of <s>dāna-pāramitā</s> (perfection of giving), born from the great <s>vajra</s>, Hūṃ." Thus.

body.text:
vajramālāmudrāṃ baddhvaivaṃ vadet /
sarvasattvāḥ sarvākuśalakāyavāgmanaskarmāntavigatā bhavantu / sarvakuśalakāyavāgmanaskarmāntasamanvāgatā bhavantu /
body.translated_text: Having formed the <s>vajramālā-mudrā</s> (vajra-garland seal), one should say thus: "May all beings be free from all unwholesome bodily, verbal, and mental actions! May they be endowed with all wholesome bodily, verbal, and mental actions!"
"Oṃ <s>Sarvavid</s>, at the time of the spreading of the ocean-cloud of offering of the unsurpassed <s>śīla-pāramitā</s> (perfection of morality), the great food of awakening, Hūṃ." Thus.

body.text:
gītāmudrāṃ baddhvaivaṃ vadet /
sarvasattvāḥ sarvalakṣaṇānuvyañjanena samalaṃkṛtagātrā bhavantu / parasparato nityam abhayāvairapratipannā hṛdayanayanābhirāmā gambhīradharmakṣāntikāś ca /
body.translated_text: Having formed the <s>gītā-mudrā</s> (song-seal), one should say thus: "May all beings have bodies adorned with all the <s>lakṣaṇas</s> (major marks) and <s>anuvyañjanas</s> (minor marks)! May they always be disposed toward fearlessness and non-hostility toward one another, delightful to hearts and eyes, and possessed of patience for the profound <s>Dharma</s>!"

"Oṃ <s>Sarvavid</s>, at the time of the spreading of the ocean-cloud of offering of the unsurpassed great <s>kṣānti-pāramitā</s> (perfection of patience), the realization of the <s>Dharma</s>, Hūṃ." Thus.

body.text:
nṛtyāmudrāṃ baddhvaivaṃ vadet /
sarvasattvā bodhisattvacaryābhiyuktā bhavantu / buddhatattvaparāyaṇāḥ saṃsārāparityāgavīryayuktāḥ /
oṃ sarvavit saṃsārāparityāgavīryapāramitāpūjāmeghasamudraspharaṇasamaye huṃ / iti /
body.translated_text:
Having formed the <s>nṛtya-mudrā</s> (dance-seal), one should say thus: "May all beings be devoted to the practice of <s>bodhisattvas</s>! May they be intent on the reality of buddhahood, endowed with vigor for not abandoning <s>saṃsāra</s>!"
"Oṃ <s>Sarvavid</s>, at the time of the spreading of the ocean-cloud of offering of <s>vīrya-pāramitā</s> (perfection of vigor) for not abandoning <s>saṃsāra</s>, Hūṃ." Thus.

body.text:
puṣpāmudrāṃ baddhvaivaṃ vadet /
sarvasattvāḥ sarvakleśopakleśavigatā bhavantu / sarvadhyānavimokṣasamādhisamāpattyabhijñāvidyāvaśitāsaṃpannāḥ /
body.translated_text: Having formed the <s>puṣpa-mudrā</s> (flower-seal), one should say thus: "May all beings be free from all <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions) and <s>upakleśas</s> (secondary afflictions)! May they be accomplished in mastery of all <s>dhyānas</s> (meditations), <s>vimokṣas</s> (liberations), <s>samādhis</s>, <s>samāpattis</s> (attainments), <s>abhijñās</s> (superknowledges), and <s>vidyās</s> (sciences)!"
"Oṃ <s>Sarvavid</s>, at the time of the spreading of the ocean-cloud of offering of the unsurpassed <s>dhyāna-pāramitā</s> (perfection of meditation), the abode of bliss, Hūṃ." Thus.

body.text:
dhūpāmudrāṃ baddhvaivaṃ vadet /
sarvasattvāḥ sarvalaukikalokottaraprajñājñānasamanvitā bhavantu / catuḥpratisaṃvitprāptāḥ sarvaśāstraśilpajñānakalāyogaguṇaguhyavidhijñās tattvadarśinaḥ sarvakleśajñeyāvaraṇasamuchedajñānaprāptāḥ /
body.translated_text: Having formed the <s>dhūpa-mudrā</s> (incense-seal), one should say thus: "May all beings be endowed with all worldly and supramundane wisdom and knowledge! May they attain the four <s>pratisaṃvids</s> (analytical knowledges), be knowers of all sciences, crafts, knowledge-arts, yogic qualities, and secret rites, seers of reality, and attain the knowledge that completely cuts off all afflictive and cognitive obscurations!"

"Oṃ <s>Sarvavid</s>, at the time of the spreading of the ocean-cloud of offering of the unsurpassed great <s>prajñā-pāramitā</s> (perfection of wisdom) that cuts through <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions), Hūṃ." Thus.

body.text:
dīpāmudrāṃ baddhvaivaṃ vadet /
sarvasattvāḥ sarvāpāyavigatā bhavantu /
body.translated_text: Having formed the <s>dīpa-mudrā</s> (lamp-seal), one should say thus: "May all beings be free from all evil destinies!"

"Oṃ <s>Sarvavid</s>, purifier of all evil destinies, at the time of the spreading of the ocean-cloud of offering of <s>praṇidhāna-pāramitā</s> (perfection of aspiration), the light of knowledge, Hūṃ." Thus.

body.text:
gandhāmudrāṃ baddhvaivaṃ vadet /
sarvasattvāḥ sarvājñānavigatā bhavantu /
body.translated_text: Having formed the <s>gandha-mudrā</s> (fragrance-seal), one should say thus: "May all beings be free from all ignorance!"

body.text:
oṃ sarvavit sarvāpāyagandhanāśani vajragandhopāyapāramitāpūjāmeghasamudraspharaṇasamaye huṃ / iti /
daśasu dikṣv aśeṣasarvatathāgatapādamūlagatam ātmānam adhimucya kāyaparicaryārthaṃ /
body.translated_text:
"Oṃ <s>Sarvavid</s>, destroyer of the scent of all evil destinies, at the time of the spreading of the ocean-cloud of offering of <s>upāya-pāramitā</s> (perfection of skillful means), the <s>vajra</s>-fragrance, Hūṃ." Thus.
Visualizing oneself as having gone to the feet of all <s>Tathāgatas</s> throughout the ten directions without remainder, for the purpose of bodily service —

body.text:
oṃ sarvavit kāyaniryātanapūjāmeghasamudraspharaṇasamaye huṃ / iti /
asamācaletyādi / sarvatra jihvāśatamukhena stotropahāram adhimucya /
body.translated_text:
"Oṃ <s>Sarvavid</s>, at the time of the spreading of the ocean-cloud of offering of the surrender of the body, Hūṃ." Thus.
"Immovable" and so forth. Visualizing the presentation of praise with a hundred tongues and mouths everywhere —

body.text:
oṃ sarvavid vāgniryātanapūjāmeghasamudraspharaṇasamaye huṃ / iti /
sarvabodhisattvaikāśayaprayogatayā dharmasamatām adhimucya /
body.translated_text:
"Oṃ <s>Sarvavid</s>, at the time of the spreading of the ocean-cloud of offering of the surrender of speech, Hūṃ." Thus.
Visualizing the equality of <s>Dharma</s> through the unity of intention and practice of all <s>bodhisattvas</s> —

body.text:
oṃ sarvavit cittaniryātanapūjāmeghasamudraspharaṇasamaye huṃ / iti /
abhāvasvabhāvāḥ sarvadharmāḥ śūnyatānimittāpraṇihitākārā ity adhimucya /
body.translated_text:
"Oṃ <s>Sarvavid</s>, at the time of the spreading of the ocean-cloud of offering of the surrender of mind, Hūṃ." Thus.
Visualizing that all <s>dharmas</s> are without inherent nature, having the aspects of <s>śūnyatā</s> (emptiness), <s>ānimitta</s> (signlessness), and <s>apraṇihita</s> (wishlessness) —

body.text:
oṃ sarvavid guhyaniryātanapūjāmeghasamudraspharaṇasamaye huṃ / iti /
evaṃ viṃśatiprakārapūjayā sarvatathāgatān saṃpūjyātmānaṃ niryātayet /
body.translated_text:
"Oṃ <s>Sarvavid</s>, at the time of the spreading of the ocean-cloud of offering of the surrender of the secret, Hūṃ." Thus.
Thus, having worshipped all <s>Tathāgatas</s> with twenty kinds of offering, one should surrender oneself.

body.text: ātmānaṃ sarvabuddhabodhisattvebhyo niryātayāmi / sarvadā sarvakālaṃ pratigṛhṇantu māṃ mahākāruṇikā nāthā mahāsamayasiddhiñ ca prayacchantu / tac ca kuśalamūlaṃ sarvasattvasādhāraṇaṃ kartavyaṃ / anena kuśalamūlena sarvasattvāḥ sarvalaukikalokottaravipattivigatā bhavantu /
body.translated_text: "I surrender myself to all <s>Buddhas</s> and <s>Bodhisattvas</s>! May the great compassionate protectors always, at all times, accept me and grant the accomplishment of the great <s>samaya</s> (pledge)!" And that root of merit should be made common to all beings. "By this root of merit, may all beings be free from all worldly and supramundane misfortunes!"

children.translated_text: "And may they be endowed with all worldly and supramundane prosperity!"

children.text: sahaiva sukhena sahaiva saumanasyena buddhā bhavantu narottamā iti /
children.translated_text: "Together with happiness, together with joy, may they become <s>Buddhas</s>, the best of beings!"
"And by this wholesome action, may I become a <s>Buddha</s>!"

body.text: na cireṇa loke deśaye dharmaṃ jagato hitāya //
body.translated_text: "Before long in the world, may I teach the <s>Dharma</s> for the benefit of beings!"
"May I liberate beings afflicted by much suffering!" Thus.

children.translated_text: For the sake of dedication to unsurpassed perfect awakening, one should take the vow:
"I generate the supreme, unsurpassed <s>bodhicitta</s> (mind of awakening)!"

body.translated_text: "Just as the protectors of the three times have resolved upon awakening,"
"The threefold training in morality and the collection of wholesome <s>dharmas</s>,"
"And the morality of acting for the benefit of beings — I firmly undertake these!"

body.text: buddhaṃ dharmaṃ ca saṅghaṃ ca triratnāgram anuttaram //
body.translated_text: "The <s>Buddha</s>, the <s>Dharma</s>, and the <s>Saṅgha</s>, the supreme unsurpassed Three Jewels,"
"From this day forward I shall take the vow born of the <s>Buddha</s>-yoga!"

body.text: vajraghaṇṭāṃ ca mudrāṃ ca pratigṛhṇāmi tattvataḥ //
body.translated_text: "The <s>vajra</s>, the <s>ghaṇṭā</s> (bell), and the <s>mudrā</s> — I take these in their true nature!"
"And I shall accept the <s>ācārya</s> (master) in the supreme great <s>vajra</s> family!"

body.text: caturdānaṃ pradāsyāmi ṣaṭkṛtvā tu dine dine //
body.translated_text: "I shall give the four gifts six times daily!"
"In the delightful <s>samaya</s> (pledge) of the great jewel family yoga,"
"I undertake the true <s>Dharma</s>, outer, secret, and of three vehicles!"
"In the pure great lotus family, born of great awakening,"
"I take the vow conjoined with all, in its true nature!"
"The work of worship according to one's ability, in the supreme great karma family,"
"Having generated the supreme, unsurpassed <s>bodhicitta</s>,"
"Having taken the complete vow, for the sake of benefiting all beings,"
"Those not yet crossed, I shall ferry across; those not yet freed, I shall liberate!"

body.text: anāśvastān āśvāsayiṣyāmi sattvān sthāpayāmi nirvṛttāv iti //
body.translated_text: "Those not yet comforted, I shall comfort; beings I shall establish in <s>nirvṛtti</s> (cessation)!" Thus.

body.text: tata ākāśasthaṃ maṇḍalaṃ devādibhiḥ pūjyanānaṃ vicintayet / pañcopahārādinā pūjayet / samyak prapūjya buddhānāṃ guṇavarṇānāṃ stutiṃ kuryāt /
body.translated_text: Then one should visualize the <s>maṇḍala</s> situated in space being worshipped by <s>devas</s> and others. One should worship with the five offerings and so forth. Having properly worshipped, one should recite praise describing the qualities of the <s>Buddhas</s>:

body.text: aho buddha aho buddha sādhu buddha kṛtottama //
body.translated_text: "Wonderful are the <s>Buddhas</s>! Wonderful are the <s>Buddhas</s>! Excellent are the <s>Buddhas</s>, the supreme doers of good!"
"Having purified all evil destinies, the awakening of beings is attained!"

body.text:
tata oṃ vajrāñjalīti / vajrabandhanaṃ hṛdaye sphoṭayet /
oṃ sarvavid vajrabandha trāṭ bruvan / vajrāveśamudrāṃ baddhvā /
body.translated_text:
Then, "Oṃ <s>Vajrāñjali</s>." One should snap the <s>vajra</s>-bond at the heart.
Saying "Oṃ <s>Sarvavid</s> <s>Vajrabandha</s> Trāṭ," having formed the <s>vajrāveśa-mudrā</s> (vajra-entry seal) —

body.text: oṃ tiṣṭha vajra dṛḍho me bhava śāśvato me bhava hṛdayaṃ me 'dhitiṣṭha sarvasiddhiṃ ca me prayaccha huṃ ha ha ha ha hoḥ / iti /
body.translated_text: "Oṃ, remain, O <s>Vajra</s>! Be firm for me! Be eternal for me! Preside over my heart! And grant me all <s>siddhis</s> (accomplishments)! Hūṃ Ha Ha Ha Ha Hoḥ!" Thus.
"Oṃ <s>Vajramuṣṭi</s> Vaṃ!" Having formed the <s>sattvavajrī</s> —

body.text: oṃ sarvavit śodhane śodhane sarvapāpān apanaya huṃ / pāpākarṣaṇamantraḥ /
body.translated_text: "Oṃ <s>Sarvavid</s>, purify, purify, remove all sins, Hūṃ!" This is the mantra for drawing out sins.
Having firmly formed the <s>vajra</s>-bond, through the empowerment of the <s>vajra-mudrā</s>,

body.text: samutkṣipet kṣaṇād ūrdhvaṃ patitotkṣepaṇaṃ param // iti /
body.translated_text: One should instantly cast upward — this is the supreme casting up of the fallen. Thus.

body.text: oṃ sarvavit sarvāpāyaviśodhani huṃ phaṭ / pāpaviśodhanamantraḥ /
body.translated_text: "Oṃ <s>Sarvavid</s>, purifier of all evil destinies, Hūṃ Phaṭ!" This is the mantra for purifying sins.
Having made the <s>vajra</s>-bond firm, with the two middle fingers together with the mouth,
The four end-fingers touching the mouth — it destroys sin in an instant.

body.text: oṃ sarvavit trāṭ huṃ / sattvavajrīṃ baddhvā /
body.translated_text: "Oṃ <s>Sarvavid</s> Trāṭ Hūṃ!" Having formed the <s>sattvavajrī</s> —

body.text: oṃ sarvavit sarvāvaraṇaviśodhane muḥ huṃ phaṭ / uddharaṇalakṣaṇam /
body.translated_text: "Oṃ <s>Sarvavid</s>, purifier of all obscurations, Muḥ Hūṃ Phaṭ!" This is the sign of extraction.

body.text: tataḥ paścād yogino hṛdayamadhye 'kāreṇa candramaṇḍalaṃ tasyopari /
body.translated_text: Then, after that, in the middle of the yogin's heart, a moon-disc by means of the syllable 'A', above that —

body.text:
oṃ mune mune mahāmunaye svāhā /
oṃ namaḥ sarvadurgatipariśodhanarājāya tathāgatāyārhate samyaksaṃbuddhāya / tadyathā /
body.translated_text:
"Oṃ <s>Mune</s> <s>Mune</s> <s>Mahāmunaye</s> Svāhā!"
"Oṃ, homage to the King of the Purification of All Evil Destinies, the <s>Tathāgata</s>, the <s>Arhat</s>, the Perfectly Awakened One! That is to say:"

body.text: oṃ śodhane śodhane sarvapāpaviśodhaṃ śuddhe viśuddhe sarvakarmāvaraṇaviśuddhe svāhā /
body.translated_text: "Oṃ, purify, purify, the purification of all sins, O pure one, O completely pure one, the purification of all karmic obscurations, Svāhā!"

body.text: etena mantreṇa durgatipariśodhanamaṇḍalaṃ pariniṣpannaṃ bhavati / tato vajrāṅkuśādyair ākṛṣya praveśya baddhvā vaśīkṛtyākāśamaṇḍalapūjāṃ kṛtvā hṛdayamaṇḍale niveśayet / dvayamaṇḍalenaikamaṇḍalaṃ bhavatīti / niṣpannayogo bhūtvā samayamaṇḍalaṃ devatāparipūrṇaṃ bhavati / tatra maṇḍalamadhye cakravartirūpam ātmabhāvaṃ śākyasiṃhaṃ vibhāvayet / tataḥ śākyamuner hṛdyakāreṇa candramaṇḍalaṃ bhāvayet / candramaṇḍalamadhye /
body.translated_text: By this mantra, the <s>Durgatipariśodhana-maṇḍala</s> becomes fully accomplished. Then, having drawn in with the <s>vajrāṅkuśa</s> (vajra-hook) and so forth, having caused to enter, bound, and subjugated, having performed the worship of the space-<s>maṇḍala</s>, one should install it in the heart-<s>maṇḍala</s>. The two <s>maṇḍalas</s> become one <s>maṇḍala</s>. Having become accomplished in the <s>niṣpannayoga</s> (completion yoga), the <s>samaya-maṇḍala</s> becomes filled with deities. There, in the middle of the <s>maṇḍala</s>, one should visualize one's own form in the form of a <s>Cakravartin</s> as <s>Śākyasiṃha</s>. Then, one should visualize a moon-disc by means of the syllable 'A' in the heart of <s>Śākyamuni</s>. In the middle of the moon-disc —
"Oṃ <s>Mune</s> <s>Mune</s> <s>Mahāmunaye</s> Svāhā!"
Then, having constructed the <s>maṇḍala</s> with the <s>vajrahetu-karma-mudrā</s> (vajra-cause action-seal) —
"Oṃ <s>Sarvavid</s> <s>Vajracakra</s> Hūṃ!" Thus.

body.text: sattvavajrīṃ baddhvaiva madhyāṅgulidvayena mālām ādāya manasā praviśet / samaye huṃ ity anena tāṃ ca mālāṃ svaśirasi kṣipet / anena praticcha vajra hoḥ / iti / tataḥ svaśirasi bandhed anena /
body.translated_text: Having formed the <s>sattvavajrī</s> itself, taking the <s>mālā</s> (rosary) with the two middle fingers, one should mentally enter. With "Samaye Hūṃ," one should cast that <s>mālā</s> upon one's own head. With this: "Accept, O <s>Vajra</s>, Hoḥ!" Thus. Then one should bind it upon one's own head with this —

body.text: oṃ pratigṛhṇa tvam imāṃ sattva mahābaleti //
body.translated_text: "Oṃ, accept this, O being of great strength!"
And one should release the mouth-binding with this —
"Oṃ, <s>Vajrasattva</s> himself today, intent upon opening the eyes,"
"The all-eyed one opens the unsurpassed <s>vajra</s>-eye!" Thus.
"O <s>Vajra</s>, behold!" Thus.

body.text: tato mahāmaṇḍale tāvat paśyed yāvad bhagavantaṃ śākyamuniṃ / punaḥ sattvavajrīṃ baddhvā hṛdaye muñcet / vajrādhiṣṭitakalaśād udakābhiṣekaṃ vajramuṣṭyā dadyāt /
body.translated_text: Then one should gaze upon the great <s>maṇḍala</s> until one sees <s>Bhagavān</s> <s>Śākyamuni</s>. Again, having formed the <s>sattvavajrī</s> and released it at the heart, one should give the water-<s>abhiṣeka</s> (consecration) from the <s>vajra</s>-empowered vessel with the <s>vajramuṣṭi</s> (vajra-fist).
"Oṃ <s>Sarvavid</s>, consecrate me with the <s>vajra</s>!" Thus.
Again, one should consecrate with the <s>mudrā</s> of <s>Vajradhātvīśvarī</s> and the others —

body.text:
oṃ sarvavid vajradhātvīśvari huṃ abhiṣiñca mām /
oṃ sarvavid vajravajriṇi huṃ abhiṣiñca mām /
oṃ sarvavid ratnavajriṇi huṃ abhiṣiñca mām /
oṃ sarvavid dharmavajriṇi huṃ abhiṣiñca mām /
oṃ sarvavit karmavajriṇi huṃ abhiṣiñca mām /
oṃ ṭūṃ ṭūṃ ṭūṃ vajra tuṣya hoḥ /
body.translated_text:
"Oṃ <s>Sarvavid</s> <s>Vajradhātvīśvarī</s> Hūṃ, consecrate me!
Oṃ <s>Sarvavid</s> <s>Vajravajriṇī</s> Hūṃ, consecrate me!
Oṃ <s>Sarvavid</s> <s>Ratnavajriṇī</s> Hūṃ, consecrate me!
Oṃ <s>Sarvavid</s> <s>Dharmavajriṇī</s> Hūṃ, consecrate me!
Oṃ <s>Sarvavid</s> <s>Karmavajriṇī</s> Hūṃ, consecrate me!
Oṃ Ṭūṃ Ṭūṃ Ṭūṃ <s>Vajra</s> Tuṣya Hoḥ!"

body.text: dvyakṣarakavacena kavacayitvā / tataḥ svavajrābhiṣekaṃ gṛhṇīyāt / adyābhiṣiktas tvam asi buddhair vajrābhiṣekataḥ //
body.translated_text: Having armored oneself with the two-syllable armor — then one should receive one's own <s>vajra-abhiṣeka</s> (vajra-consecration): "Today you are consecrated by the <s>Buddhas</s> through the <s>vajra-abhiṣeka</s>!"
"This is the state of all buddhahood — accept it for the perfect accomplishment of the <s>vajra</s>!"

body.text: oṃ vajrādhipati tvām abhiṣiñcāmi tiṣṭha vajrasamayas tvaṃ vajranāmābhiṣekataḥ /
body.translated_text: "Oṃ, O Lord of the <s>Vajra</s>, I consecrate you! Remain! You are the <s>vajra-samaya</s>! By the consecration of the <s>vajra</s>-name —"
"Oṃ <s>Vajrasattva</s>, I consecrate you!"
"This state of all buddhahood rests in the hand of <s>Vajrasattva</s>!"
"You too must always maintain the firm vow of <s>Vajrapāṇi</s>!"

body.text: oṃ sarvatathāgatasiddhivajrasamaya tiṣṭhaiṣa tvāṃ dhārayāmi vajrasattva hi hi hi hi huṃ / iti /
body.translated_text: "Oṃ, O <s>Vajra-samaya</s> of the accomplishment of all <s>Tathāgatas</s>, remain! I shall uphold you, O <s>Vajrasattva</s>! Hi Hi Hi Hi Hūṃ!" Thus.
"Oṃ <s>Sarvavid</s>, at the time of the <s>vajra</s>-empowerment pledge, Hūṃ!" This is the mantra of self-empowerment.

body.text: vajramuṣṭidvayaṃ baddhvāṅguṣṭhamadhyamākaniṣṭhordhvaṃ sthitvā mukhe śliṣyet tarjanyanāmikāsattvaparyaṅkaṃ kṛtvā / vajramudrā / hṛtkaṇṭhalalāṭa ūrṇābhrūmadhye nāsikākarṇakaṭijānupādadvaye jaṃghāyāṃ cakṣurdvaye guhye 'dhiṣṭhāṇaṃ tu kārayet /
body.translated_text: Having formed both <s>vajramuṣṭis</s> (vajra-fists), with the thumbs, middle fingers, and little fingers standing upward, one should press them to the mouth; having made a <s>sattvaparyaṅka</s> (cross-legged posture) with the index and ring fingers — this is the <s>vajra-mudrā</s>. One should perform the empowerment at the heart, throat, forehead, between the <s>ūrṇā</s>-eyebrows, nose, ears, waist, knees, both feet, shanks, both eyes, and the secret place.

body.text:
tataḥ svakāyasamaya akāreṇa candramaṇḍalam / sarvabījasamutpannacihnāhaṃkāraṃ mantram udvahan /
oṃ sarvavid jaḥ huṃ vaṃ hoḥ samayas tvaṃ samaya hoḥ /
oṃ mune mune mahāmunaye svāhā / trir uccārayet sāmānyam api /
tataḥ svakāye vajrasamājamudrāṃ baddhvā /
body.translated_text: Then on one's own body, with the syllable A, [visualize] a moon-disc. Bearing the mantra of self-identity born from all seed-syllables: oṃ sarvavid jaḥ huṃ vaṃ hoḥ samayas tvaṃ samaya hoḥ / oṃ mune mune mahāmunaye svāhā. Recite three times, also the common [mantra]. Then, having formed the <s>vajrasamāja-mudrā</s> (vajra-assembly seal) on one's own body,

children.translated_text: Activate [it by reciting] jaḥ huṃ vaṃ hoḥ.
Drawing [the deities] to their respective places, causing them to enter, binding them, and subjugating them.
In one's own heart, through the yoga of the HŪṂ syllable, [visualize] the five-pronged <s>vajra</s>.

body.translated_text: I shall now explain the <s>samaya</s> (pledge) through the <s>mudrā</s> of <s>Śākyasiṃha</s>.
Situated at the foremost <s>samādhi</s>, it is called the <s>mudrā-samaya</s> (seal-pledge).
Having firmly bound the <s>vajrabandha</s> (vajra-bond), the middle fingers are joined at the mouth.

children.translated_text: The <s>vajroṣṇīṣa-mudrā</s> (vajra-crown-protuberance seal).

children.text: saiva madhyamā ratnaṃ tu padmākāraṃ tu madhyamā //
children.translated_text: That same [with] the middle finger [becomes] the <s>ratna</s> (jewel); with the <s>padma</s> (lotus) form, the middle finger.

body.text: saiva madhyamā vajraṃ tu śeṣā jvālāṃgulīkṛtā //
body.translated_text: That same [with] the middle finger [becomes] the <s>vajra</s>; the rest are made with flame-fingers.
That same finger made flame-shaped, with the radiance of the <s>uṣṇīṣa-mudrā</s>.
That same [with] the ring finger; release the two little fingers.

body.text: tarjanī padmapattraṃ tu madhyamā vajraṃ utthitā //
body.translated_text: The index finger is the lotus petal; the middle finger rises as the <s>vajra</s>.
That same, standing in front, forms the <s>vajrapañjara</s> (vajra-enclosure).
At the heart, with joined thumbs, [form] the well-extended garland [mudrā].
With the tips of the joined hands raised upward, cupped above the head of the dancer.
From the lower offering of the <s>vajrabandha</s>, with the joined hands offering upward.
Pressing the joined thumbs, well-extended for anointing.
Having formed the double <s>vajramuṣṭi</s> (vajra-fist), [with] index, thumb, and middle fingers,
Each should be held facing the other.
Curving one index finger, the two thumbs are tied in a knot.

body.text:
aṃguṣṭhāgrakaṭibandhā vajramuṣṭyagrasaṃhitā // iti /
dharmamudrāṃ bhāvayet kaṇṭhe padmendumaṇḍale //
body.translated_text: The thumb-tips bound at the waist, joined at the top of the <s>vajramuṣṭi</s>. Thus: one should visualize the <s>dharma-mudrā</s> (dharma-seal) at the throat on the <s>padmendu-maṇḍala</s> (lotus-moon disc).
First, through the offering-mantra, the <s>dharma-mudrā</s> is performed.
The <s>karma-mudrā</s> (action-seal): at the heart, a <s>viśvavajra</s> (crossed vajra).
The <s>dharmacakra</s> (dharma-wheel), through the <s>mudrā</s> of <s>Śākyarāja</s> as described.
<s>Bhūsparśa</s> (earth-touching), <s>varada</s> (boon-granting), <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation), <s>abhaya</s> (fearlessness), and so forth in order.
Through the <s>mudrā</s> of <s>Tejoṣṇīṣa</s>, situated at the foremost <s>samādhi</s>.
The right arm as a staff, and in the left at the heart, wielding a sword.
Releasing the left index finger, extend [it] with the right.
Closing both hands, hold in an umbrella-shape.
The procedure of the <s>karma-mudrā</s>, for those who are the newly-awakened <s>Buddhas</s>.
Through the application of <s>vajragarva</s> (vajra-pride), bow with shaking devotion.
The garland-binding raised upward at the mouth, turned while dancing.
Through the application of <s>vajramuṣṭi</s>, offer incense and the rest likewise.
With the index-finger hook-binding, the great hook at the little finger.
Press at the forearms and back with the tips of the knot-bindings.
Now I shall explain [the mudrās] of the great-souled <s>Bodhisattvas</s>.
Through the sequence of <s>karma-mudrās</s>, in proper order and characteristics.
Having formed the double <s>vajramuṣṭi</s>, close both together.
Curving index and middle fingers, hold in the shape of a flower.

children.translated_text: The <s>mudrā</s> of <s>Maitreya</s>.
Place the left fist at the waist, the right [fist] at the side of the arm.

body.translated_text: Release the index and middle fingers, hold in the shape of an eye.

children.translated_text: Of <s>Amoghadarśin</s>.
Having formed the double <s>vajramuṣṭi</s>, extend the index fingers.

body.translated_text: With the left, hold a hook—of <s>Sarvāpāyajaha</s>.
Place the left fist at the waist; the right has the form of a staff.
Hold it upward—of <s>Sarvaśokatamas</s>.
The left fist is positioned in the sky, in the form of an elephant's trunk.
Hold it in the right hand—through the <s>mudrā</s> of <s>Gandhahastin</s>.
Place the left fist at the waist; the right in the form of a sword.

children.translated_text: Of <s>Śūraṃgama</s>.

children.text: vāmamuṣṭiṃ hṛdi dhārya dakṣiṇaṃ ūrdhvaṃ bhrāmayet //
children.translated_text: Hold the left fist at the heart; rotate the right upward.
Of <s>Gaganagañja</s>.
Having formed the double <s>vajramuṣṭi</s>, hold with the right.

body.translated_text: In the form of holding a banner—through the <s>mudrā</s> of <s>Jñānaketu</s>.
Hold with both hands in the shape of a water vessel.
Of <s>Amṛtaprabha</s>.
With the left fist resting on the thigh, the right fist at the side,
Extend the little finger and thumb, in the form of a crescent moon.

children.translated_text: Of <s>Candraprabha</s>.
At the heart region, open both hands in the form of a lotus.

body.translated_text: With faces directed toward each other—through the <s>mudrā</s> of <s>Bhadrapāla</s>.
Having formed the double <s>vajramuṣṭi</s>, hold in the form of an armor.
Hold at the two breasts—through the <s>mudrā</s> of <s>Jālinīprabha</s>.
The left fist placed at the waist, the right situated at the heart.
Release the middle finger—through the <s>mudrā</s> of <s>Vajragarbha</s>.
The left fist placed at the heart, the right in the <s>varada</s> (boon-granting) form.

children.translated_text: The <s>mudrā</s> of <s>Akṣayamati</s>.

children.text: vāme nābhasthitā muṣṭir dakṣiṇe choṭikāṃ dadan //
children.translated_text: The left fist positioned in the sky, the right giving a finger-snap.
Of <s>Pratibhānakūṭa</s>.
Hold the left fist at the waist; the right is a jewel-fist.
Of <s>Samantabhadra</s>.
Through the method without emblems, the <s>karma-mudrā</s> is thus stated.

body.translated_text: At the heart, hold the <s>vajra</s> in the form of five prongs.
As held during the offerings, for those bearing <s>mudrās</s> and weapons.
Becoming the bearer of <s>vajra</s> and <s>ghaṇṭā</s> (bell), hold the <s>vajra</s> at the heart.
This should be known as the <s>mahāmudrā</s> (great seal) of the great-souled <s>Bodhisattvas</s>.
As grasped during the offerings, for those bearing <s>mudrā</s>-weapons.

body.text: yāṃ yāṃ mudrāṃ tu badhnīyād yasya yasya mahātmanaḥ //
body.translated_text: Whatever <s>mudrā</s> one binds, for whichever great-souled one,

body.text: japan tu hṛdayārthena bhāvayet tu svam ātmānam //
body.translated_text: Reciting with the meaning of the <s>hṛdaya</s> (heart-mantra), one should visualize oneself.
The four <s>mudrās</s> should be performed to seal all deities completely.
Endowed with the qualities of omniscience, for the sake of benefiting all beings,
Having purified all evil destinies, <s>bodhi</s> (enlightenment) is attained for beings.
Now I shall proclaim the mantra in the <s>Sarvadurgati-maṇḍala</s> (maṇḍala of all evil destinies).
Through the application of <s>mudrā</s> and <s>mantra</s>, one becomes capable of all tasks.
Having performed the <s>vajra-nṛtya</s> (vajra-dance) in succession, it is recited with mantras.
Oṃ, homage to the King of Purification of All Evil Destinies,
the <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, <s>Samyaksaṃbuddha</s>. The formula is:
Oṃ śodhane śodhane sarvapāpaviśodhane śuddhe,
viśuddhe sarvakarmāvaraṇaviśuddhe svāhā.

body.text: vāmavajramuṣṭyā vajraghaṇṭām ādāya dakṣiṇahastena vajraṃsagarvam ullalayan evaṃ vadet / vajravācāṭakki huṃ jaḥ jaḥ jaḥ / svahṛdy utkarṣaṇayogena dhārayet / ṭakki jaḥ hoḥ iti vadet /
body.translated_text: Taking the <s>vajraghaṇṭā</s> (vajra-bell) with the left <s>vajramuṣṭi</s>, and raising the <s>vajra</s> with pride in the right hand, speak thus: vajravācāṭakki huṃ jaḥ jaḥ jaḥ. Hold it at one's own heart through the yoga of drawing upward. Say: ṭakki jaḥ hoḥ.

body.text: tadanuśatākṣareṇadṛḍhīkṛtya / etena daśabhūmīśvarabodhisattvasadṛśo bhavati / tān dṛṣṭvā sarvapūjāṃ prapūjayet /
body.translated_text: Then, having made [it] firm with the hundred-syllable [mantra]—by this one becomes equal to a <s>Bodhisattva</s> Lord of the Ten Stages. Having seen them, one should make all offerings.

children.translated_text: Then one should worship with all those praises.
Homage to you, <s>Śākyasiṃha</s> (Lion of the Śākyas), turner of the <s>Dharmacakra</s> (Dharma-wheel).

body.translated_text: May you purify the entire triple world and all evil destinies.
Homage to you, <s>Vajroṣṇīṣa</s>, from the intrinsic nature of the <s>dharmadhātu</s>.
For the benefit of all beings, you who reveal the truth of the self.
Homage to you, <s>Ratnoṣṇīṣa</s>, through the cultivation of the truth of equality.
The entire triple world stands [in awe]; you who bestow <s>abhiṣeka</s> (consecration).
Homage to you, <s>Padmoṣṇīṣa</s>, you who examine [things'] intrinsic nature.
You comfort beings with showers of the nectar of <s>Dharma</s>.
Homage to you, <s>Viśvoṣṇīṣa</s>, you who practice according to intrinsic nature.
You who perform all deeds for the cessation of suffering of these beings.
Homage to you, <s>Tejoṣṇīṣa</s>, you who illuminate the triple realm.
Having truly seen beings in evil destinies, you will act [to save them].
Homage to you, <s>Dhvajoṣṇīṣa</s>, bearer of the <s>cintāmaṇi</s> (wish-fulfilling jewel) banner.
Through generosity, may you fulfill all wishes of all beings.
Homage to you, <s>Tīkṣṇoṣṇīṣa</s>, cutter of <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions) and <s>upakleśas</s> (secondary afflictions).
Having shattered the forces of the four <s>Māras</s>, <s>bodhi</s> (enlightenment) is attained for beings.
Homage to you, <s>Chatroṣṇīṣa</s>, adorned with the white parasol.
The entire triple world attains the sovereignty of <s>Dharma</s>.

body.text: lāsyā mālā tathā gītā nṛtyā devyaś catuṣṭayāḥ //
body.translated_text: <s>Lāsyā</s>, <s>Mālā</s>, and <s>Gītā</s>, <s>Nṛtyā</s>—the four goddesses.

body.text: puṣpā dhūpā ca dīpā ca gandhā devī namo 'stu te //
body.translated_text: <s>Puṣpā</s>, <s>Dhūpā</s>, and <s>Dīpā</s>, and <s>Gandhā</s>—goddesses, homage to you.
Standing at the center of the doors: <s>Āveśa</s>, <s>Aṃkuśa</s>, <s>Pāśa</s>, <s>Sphoṭaka</s>.
Born from the cultivation of faith and the rest, door-guardians, homage to you.
Those who stand at the railing and the sides of the four doorways,

body.text: muditādau daśe sthitvā bodhisattvā namo 'stu te //
body.translated_text: Standing in the ten [stages] beginning with <s>Muditā</s> (Joy), <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, homage to you.
<s>Brahmā</s> and <s>Indra</s>, <s>Rudra</s>, <s>Candra</s>, and others, world-protectors of the four directions,
<s>Agni</s>, <s>Rākṣasa</s>, <s>Vāyu</s>—lords of beings, homage to you.
Having praised with this king of praises before the <s>maṇḍala</s>,
The <s>mantrī</s> (mantra-holder) bearing <s>vajra</s> and <s>ghaṇṭā</s> should recite this hymn.
Afterwards, on one's own body, one should visualize the self-<s>maṇḍala</s>.
Thus visualizing, the <s>maṇḍala</s> from the primordial yoga.

body.text:
ādiyoganāmasamādhiḥ /
tato maṇḍalarājāgrīnāma pravakṣyāmi /
oṃ akāro mukhaṃ sarvadharmāṇām ādyanutpannatvāt / tadarthādhimokṣato daśadikṣarvalokadhātuṣoḍaśaśūnyatām adhimucya śūnyatāhaṃkāram ātmānaṃ paśyet /
body.translated_text: The <s>samādhi</s> called <s>Ādiyoga</s> (Primordial Yoga). Now I shall explain the Foremost of <s>Maṇḍala</s>-Kings. Oṃ, the syllable A is the face of all <s>dharmas</s> because they are primordially unarisen. Through aspiration for that meaning, contemplating the sixteen <s>śūnyatās</s> (emptinesses) across all world-realms in the ten directions, one should see oneself as the identity of <s>śūnyatā</s>.

body.text: tato huṃkāreṇa niṣpannavajreṇa vāyumaṇḍalaṃ tasyopari raṃkāreṇāgnimaṇḍalaṃ tasyopari vaṃkāreṇa mahodadhiṃ tasyopari kaṃkāreṇa kāñcanamaṇḍalaṃ tadmadhye huṃ suṃ huṃ iti / tena sumeruṃ caturasraṃ ratnamayaṃ sarvaratnavibhūṣitaṃ niṣpādya / oṃ vajra dṛḍhetyādinā vajrabandhenādhitiṣṭhet / tasyopari vajrahetukarmamudrayā bhūṃkārasitaniṣpannavajramaṇiratnaśikharakūṭāgāram /
body.translated_text: Then, with the <s>vajra</s> arisen from HŪṂ, [visualize] the wind-<s>maṇḍala</s>; above that, with RAṂ, the fire-<s>maṇḍala</s>; above that, with VAṂ, the great ocean; above that, with KAṂ, the golden ground. In the middle of that, [with] HŪṂ SUṂ HŪṂ, having constructed <s>Sumeru</s>—four-sided, made of jewels, adorned with all precious gems—one should consecrate [it] with the <s>vajrabandha</s> [saying] 'Oṃ vajra dṛḍha' and so forth. Above that, with the <s>vajrahetu-karma-mudrā</s>, [arises] from the syllable BHŪṂ on a white [base] the jewel-peaked mansion with a <s>vajra</s>-gem pinnacle.
Four-sided, with four doors, adorned with four <s>toraṇas</s> (gateways).
At all four corners and at the junctures of the door-extensions.
Marked with moon, sun, and <s>vajra</s>, fashioned with necklaces and half-necklaces.
Endowed with four cords, adorned with cloth-garlands and festoons.

body.text: abhyantaramaṇḍalam aṣṭāracakraṃ vajrāvalīparivṛtam / tasya nābhopari siṃhāsanaṃ tasyopari candramaṇḍalaṃ / cakrāṣṭāramadhyeṣu candramaṇḍalaṃ devatāsthānam /
body.translated_text: The inner <s>maṇḍala</s> has an eight-spoked wheel surrounded by a <s>vajra</s>-fence. Above its hub, a lion-throne; above that, a moon-disc. In the middle of the eight spokes of the wheel, moon-discs—the seats of the deities.

body.text: bāhyamaṇḍalasya devatāsthānaṃ paṭikāyām aṣṭāviṃśaticandramaṇḍalaṃ paśyet / siṃhāsanopari candramaṇḍale / akārādikakārādyakṣaraprajñopāyasvarūpaṃ dravībhūtam ākāśaspharaṇaka samādhisamāpannaṃ bodhicittasvarūpeṇa sattvārthahetusaṃpannamantrarūpaṃ bhavati /
body.translated_text: [Continued from above.]
Oṃ mune mune mahāmunaye svāhā.

body.text:
anena mantreṇa śrīśākyasiṃharājaniṣpanno bhavati / sarvanīvāraṇaṃ nāma samādhisamāpannaḥ /
tatas samādhisamāpanno buddho bhagavān tasya mudrāmantraṃ udāharet /
body.translated_text: Through this mantra, the glorious <s>Śākyasiṃharāja</s> (Lion-King of the Śākyas) arises. He has entered the <s>samādhi</s> called <s>Sarvanīvāraṇa</s> (Removal of All Obscurations). Then the <s>Buddha Bhagavān</s>, having entered <s>samādhi</s>, recites the <s>mudrā</s>-<s>mantra</s>.
Having formed the double <s>vajramuṣṭi</s>, open [the fingers] in sequence.
This is the <s>mudrā</s> of the <s>dharmacakra</s> (dharma-wheel), cutter of all <s>saṃsāra</s>.
'Tadyathā'—this is an illustration:
Just as bees and others become trapped on lotuses,
So, through the opening of the lotus, those trapped ones are freed from suffering.
Similarly, those trapped in the <s>saṃsāra</s> of suffering, caught in the three realms of existence,
Thus the trapped ones are liberated through the compassionate nature of <s>Śākyasiṃha</s>.

body.text: tataś śākyamuner hṛdaye 'kāreṇa candramaṇḍalam / tataś candramaṇḍale sarvāsāṃ mantrāṇi niṣpādyante / vajroṣṇīṣam ārabhya yāvad vajrāveśaparyantaṃ bhāvayet / tato mantrāṇi bhavanti /
body.translated_text: Then, in the heart of <s>Śākyamuni</s>, with the syllable A, [arises] a moon-disc. Then on the moon-disc, the mantras of all [deities] are produced. Beginning with <s>Vajroṣṇīṣa</s> up to <s>Vajrāveśa</s>, one should visualize [them]. Then the mantras arise.

body.text: oṃ namas sarvadurgatipariśodhanarājāya tathāgatāyārhate samyaksaṃbuddhāya / tadyathā /
body.translated_text: Oṃ, homage to the King of Purification of All Evil Destinies, the <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, <s>Samyaksaṃbuddha</s>. The formula is:

body.text: oṃ śodhane śodhane sarvapāpaviśodhane śuddhe viśuddhe sarvakarmāvaraṇaviśuddhe svāhā / idaṃ mantram udāharet /
body.translated_text: Oṃ śodhane śodhane sarvapāpaviśodhane śuddhe viśuddhe sarvakarmāvaraṇaviśuddhe svāhā. Recite this mantra.

children.translated_text: Now I shall declare in sequence, step by step:
<s>Oṃ vajra huṃ phaṭ</s>!
