Issuing forth through the mouth-door, going out as five-rayed [light],

body.translated_text: Illuminating all beings in the ten directions everywhere,
It shall make an end of suffering; then returning, those rays
Enter into the heart.
Merging the two—<s>mantra</s> and rays—the completed form arises.
On the spoke of the inner <s>maṇḍala</s>, in the eastern direction, upon a lotus and moon[-disc],
<s>Vajroṣṇīṣa Tathāgata</s>, descending from the heart, should be seated
For the benefit [of all beings].
Of white color, with divine radiance, established in the <s>bhūsparśa-mudrā</s> (earth-touching gesture),
Thus, by the previously described method of emanation and withdrawal of rays in all directions,
Through the yoga of emanation and withdrawal, the merging of <s>mantra</s> and rays,
Descending from the heart where the image-generation is complete,
He should be seated in his proper place, well-established on the southern spokes.
<s>Oṃ ratnottama traṃ</s>—he should be emitted.
Upon a moon in the center of a lotus, <s>Ratnoṣṇīṣa Tathāgata</s>,
Descending from the heart, adorned with the marks of a <s>Buddha</s>,
Of blue color by nature, and his <s>mudrā</s> is that of the boon-granting [gesture],
He bestows <s>abhiṣeka</s> (consecration) upon all beings in the entire three realms without remainder.
As before, by the method of emanation and withdrawal and the sequence of image-generation,
<s>Oṃ padmottama hrīḥ</s>—he should be emitted.
Then upon the western spoke, on a moon-disc above a lotus,
Born from the ray-<s>bīja</s> (seed-syllable), <s>Padmoṣṇīṣa Tathāgata</s>,
Having emerged from the heart, the Instructor should be seated.
Of ruby-lotus radiance and divine splendor, established in the <s>dhyāna-mudrā</s> (meditation gesture),
<s>Oṃ viśvottama aḥ</s>—he should be emitted.
On the northern spoke, upon a moon-disc on a lotus,
Descending from the heart, the <s>Buddha</s> <s>Viśvoṣṇīṣa Tathāgata</s>,
Of green color with blazing radiance, and his <s>mudrā</s> is the <s>abhaya</s> (fearlessness)-granting one,
The <s>Buddha</s> who performs all activities shall lift beings out of <s>saṃsāra</s>.
With the syllable <s>Oṃ</s>, the <s>Buddha</s> <s>Tejoṣṇīṣa Tathāgata</s> should be emitted,
Positioned on the southeast spoke, properly upon a moon-disc on a lotus,
Grasping the sun in his right [hand], the left hand resting at the hip,
Of cool reddish color, he illuminates the three realms.
Born from the seed-syllable <s>Huṃ</s>, <s>Dhvajoṣṇīṣa Tathāgata</s>,
Should be emitted, descending from the heart, seated on the southwest spoke,
Upon a moon-image on a lotus, of dark-red color,
Holding a <s>cintāmaṇi</s> (wish-fulfilling jewel) banner, he purifies the avarice of beings.
Born from the seed-syllable <s>Dhīḥ</s>, <s>Tīkṣṇoṣṇīṣa Tathāgata</s>,
Cutting through <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions) and secondary afflictions, should be emitted on the northwest spoke,
Seated upon a lotus and moon, his <s>mudrā</s>: a sword in the right [hand],
His body the color of the sky, holding a book in the left [hand].
Born from the seed-syllable <s>Krīṃ</s>, <s>Chatroṣṇīṣa Tathāgata</s>,

body.text: dharmasvāmī ca sattvānām īśānāre ca utsṛjet //
body.translated_text: Lord of <s>Dharma</s> for all beings, should be emitted on the northeast spoke,
Of jasmine-moon color, his <s>mudrā</s> is holding a parasol.
All of them are seated upon universal lotuses, on moon-discs.
<s>Huṃ Trāṃ Hrīḥ Aḥ</s>.

body.text: tena mantreṇa uccārya hṛdayād utsṛjanti ca //
body.translated_text: Uttering that <s>mantra</s>, they are emitted from the heart,
At the four corner positions, upon moon-discs on lotuses,
The four goddesses beginning with <s>Lāsyā</s>, bearing the colors of their families:
White, yellow, red, and multicolored.
Their <s>mudrās</s> are prescribed as stated.

body.text: tenaiva mantram uccārya utsṛjed hṛdayād api //
body.translated_text: Uttering that very <s>mantra</s>, they are emitted from the heart as well.
The four goddesses beginning with <s>Dhūpā</s>, upon moon-discs on lotuses,
At all four corners, in the sequence of colors and families.

body.text: oṃ sarvasaṃskārapariśuddhe dharmate gaganasamudgate svabhāvaviśuddhe mahānayaparivāre svāhā /
body.translated_text: <s>Oṃ sarvasaṃskārapariśuddhe dharmate gaganasamudgate svabhāvaviśuddhe mahānayaparivāre svāhā</s>.
With this <s>mantra</s>, they should be emitted, stationed on both sides of the eastern gate.
The group of four beginning with <s>Maitreya</s>, upon moon-discs on lotuses,
All in <s>sattvaparyaṅka</s> (cross-legged) posture, in the sequence of <s>mudrās</s> and colors:
Of yellow color with divine radiance, holding a <s>nāgapuṣpa</s> (serpent-flower) in the right [hand],
Grasping a water-vessel in the left, purified by the mind of <s>maitrī</s> (loving-kindness).
The second is <s>Amoghadarśin</s>, blazing with yellow radiance,
Left fist resting at the hip, holding a lotus with an eye in the right.
The third <s>Bodhisattva</s>, named <s>Apāyajaha</s> (Remover of Evil Destinies),
Blazing with white radiance, his <s>mudrā</s> is holding a hook.
The fourth is <s>Sarvaśokatamo-nirghātanamati</s> (Mind that Strikes Down All Sorrow and Darkness),
Of mixed white-yellow color, his <s>mudrā</s> is holding a staff,
Left fist resting at the hip, established in <s>sattvaparyaṅka</s> posture.
Four <s>Bodhisattvas</s> are established at the southern gate:

body.text: prathamo gandhahastī ca sitaśyāmaś ca varṇakaḥ //
body.translated_text: The first is <s>Gandhahastī</s> (Elephant of Fragrance), of white-dark color,
His <s>mudrā</s>: in the right hand, a conch filled with fragrance,
Left hand resting at the hip, he purifies all obscurations.
The second, named <s>Śūraṃgama</s> (Heroic March), liberator from all afflictions,
Of crystal-like radiance with divine splendor, his <s>mudrā</s> is holding a sword,
Left hand resting at the hip, he pacifies the suffering of beings.
The third is <s>Gaganagañja</s> (Treasury of Space), adorned with all ornaments,
Of mixed white-yellow color, free from all obscurations,
His <s>mudrā</s>: in the right hand, a <s>Dharma</s>-treasury on a lotus,
Left hand resting at the hip, he holds the wealth of all space.
The fourth is <s>Jñānaketu</s> (Banner of Wisdom), fulfiller of all hopes,
Resembling blue in color, bearing a <s>cintāmaṇi</s> (wish-fulfilling jewel) banner,
Left fist resting at the hip, he liberates from the suffering of poverty.
Seated at the western gate, upon a moon-disc on a lotus:
The first is <s>Amṛtaprabha</s> (Radiance of Immortality), resplendent with moon-color,
Holding a nectar-vessel, with a crown, [and] a jewel in [his other] hand,
Left fist resting at the hip, he bestows long life extensively.
The second, named <s>Candraprabha</s> (Moon-Radiance), destroyer of the darkness of ignorance,
Of white color with a divine body, his <s>mudrā</s> in the right hand
Is a moon-image on a lotus; left fist resting at the hip.
The third is <s>Bhadrapāla</s>, of white-red color,
Illuminator of all <s>dharmas</s>, his <s>mudrā</s> in the right hand
Is holding a blazing jewel; left fist resting at the hip.
The fourth <s>Bodhisattva</s>, known as <s>Jālinīprabha</s> (Net-Radiance),
Of red color with divine radiance, holding a <s>vajra</s>-cage.
The first son of the <s>Buddha</s>, named <s>Vajragarbha</s> (Vajra-Essence),
Of combined white-blue color, his <s>mudrā</s> in the right hand
Is an <s>utpala</s> (blue lotus) conjoined with a <s>vajra</s>; left fist resting at the hip.

body.text: dvitīyo akṣayo nāma matir anteṣu saṃsthitaḥ //
body.translated_text: The second, named <s>Akṣaya</s> (Inexhaustible), his mind established at the limits,
Resembling jasmine-moon color, his <s>mudrā</s> with both hands
Is holding a wisdom-vessel, he nourishes all beings.
The third son of the <s>Buddha</s>, known as <s>Pratibhākūṭa</s> (Peak of Eloquence),
Blazing with red radiance, his <s>mudrā</s> in the right hand
Is a jewel-peak on a lotus; left fist resting at the hip.
The fourth <s>Bodhisattva</s>, named <s>Samantabhadra</s>,
Resembling golden color, his <s>mudrā</s> in the right hand
Is a divine jewel-spray; left fist resting at the hip.
Thus endowed with these forms, the <s>Bodhisattvas</s> whose nature is compassion.
The <s>samādhi</s> called '<s>Maṇḍalarājāgrī</s>' (Supreme King of the <s>Maṇḍala</s>).

body.text:
oṃ mune mune mahāmunaye svāhā /
oṃ namas sarvadurgatipariśodhanarājāya tathāgatāyārhate samyaksaṃbuddhāya l tadyathā /
body.translated_text: <s>Oṃ mune mune mahāmunaye svāhā</s>. <s>Oṃ</s>, homage to the King of the Purification of All Evil Destinies, the <s>Tathāgata</s>, the <s>Arhat</s>, the Perfectly Awakened One. That is to say:

body.text: oṃ śodhane śodhane sarvapāpaviśodhane śuddhe viśuddhe sarvakarmāvaraṇaviśuddhe svāhā /
body.translated_text: <s>Oṃ śodhane śodhane sarvapāpaviśodhane śuddhe viśuddhe sarvakarmāvaraṇaviśuddhe svāhā</s>.

body.text: anena mantreṇa śrīśākyasiṃharājapramukhasaptatriṃśaddevatāparipūrṇaṃ bhāvayet / tataḥ paścād jñānamaṇḍalam ākarṣayet /
body.translated_text: By this <s>mantra</s>, one should visualize [the <s>maṇḍala</s>] complete with the thirty-seven deities headed by the glorious <s>Śākyasiṃha</s> King. Then afterward, one should attract the wisdom-<s>maṇḍala</s>.
Having performed the opening of the gates, endowed with <s>mantra</s> and <s>mudrā</s>,
Binding both [hands in] <s>vajra</s>-fists, one should extend the two index fingers,
Interlocking the little fingers—with the gate-opening <s>mudrā</s>,
<s>Oṃ sarvavid dvāram udghāṭaya huṃ</s>!

body.text:
dvārodghāṭanamantramudrayā dvāram udghāṭayet /
vajracakramudrayā maṇḍalaṃ parikalpayet /
body.translated_text: With the gate-opening <s>mantra</s> and <s>mudrā</s>, one should open the gate. With the <s>vajracakra-mudrā</s>, one should consecrate the <s>maṇḍala</s>.
<s>Oṃ sarvavid vajracakre huṃ</s>!
With the <s>vajra</s>-binding of both arms, in the releasing of the <s>vajra</s>-snap,
The glorious <s>Śākyarāja</s>-yoga-self should gather all <s>Buddhas</s>.
With the snap-clap of the left, it is accomplished with an even clap,

body.text: dakṣiṇena tu tāloktaṃ saṃnipātāv ubhāv api //
body.translated_text: The right is said [to be used] with a clap; both are assemblages.

body.text: oṃ vajrasamāja jaḥ huṃ vaṃ hoḥ /
body.translated_text: <s>Oṃ vajrasamāja jaḥ huṃ vaṃ hoḥ</s>!
By the mere issuing of this command, with the retinue and the assembly of the <s>cakra</s>,
All <s>Buddhas</s> come together—what need to speak of others?

body.text: tato 'grata ākāśadeśe maṇḍalacakraṃ dṛṣṭvā vajrayakṣamantreṇa / japtārghabhājane sthitagandhavāriṇā saṃprokṣyācamanaṃ dadyāt / tato 'rghamudrayārghaṃ dadyāt / tataḥ pādyamudrayā pādyaṃ dadyāt / tataḥ /
body.translated_text: Then, having seen the <s>maṇḍala-cakra</s> in the space before, with the <s>vajrayakṣa-mantra</s>, one should sprinkle with scented water placed in a vessel consecrated by recitation, and offer mouth-rinsing water. Then with the <s>argha-mudrā</s> one should offer <s>argha</s> (welcome-water). Then with the <s>pādya-mudrā</s> one should offer foot-washing water. Then:

body.text: vajrapuṣpe huṃ / vajradhūpe huṃ / vajradīpe huṃ / vajragandhe huṃ /
body.translated_text: <s>Vajrapuṣpe huṃ</s>! <s>Vajradhūpe huṃ</s>! <s>Vajradīpe huṃ</s>! <s>Vajragandhe huṃ</s>!
With the <s>vajrayakṣa-mantra</s>, having driven away the obstructors, one should cause [the deities] to enter the <s>maṇḍalas</s>.
Then the four <s>mudrās</s>:

body.text: prathamaṃ pūrvoktavidhimudrayā samayamudrā nibandhayet / tataḥ pūrvoktamantreṇa dharmamudrā vidhīyate / tataḥ karmamudrāmantreṇa karmamudrāṃ badhmyāt / tato mahāmudrāmantreṇa mahāmudrāṃ badhnīyāt /
body.translated_text: First, with the previously described ritual <s>mudrā</s>, one should bind the <s>samaya-mudrā</s> (pledge seal). Then with the previously stated <s>mantra</s>, the <s>dharma-mudrā</s> is performed. Then with the <s>karma-mudrā mantra</s>, one should bind the <s>karma-mudrā</s> (action seal). Then with the <s>mahāmudrā mantra</s>, one should bind the <s>mahāmudrā</s> (great seal).

body.text: tato vajroṣṇīṣāditathāgataiḥ sattvavajrīratnavajrīdharmavajrīkarmavajrīṃ sphārayitvā samāṇḍaleyadevatāśrīśākyarājapramukhavajrāveśaparyantam abhiṣekaṃ dadyāt / pañcābhiṣekādhipatMaśaparyantaṃ dadyāt / abhiṣekānantaram /
body.translated_text: Then, by <s>Vajroṣṇīṣa</s> and the other <s>Tathāgatas</s>, having emanated the <s>Sattvavajrī</s>, <s>Ratnavajrī</s>, <s>Dharmavajrī</s>, and <s>Karmavajrī</s>, one should bestow the <s>abhiṣeka</s> (consecration) up to the <s>vajra</s>-empowerment, upon all the <s>maṇḍala</s> deities headed by the glorious <s>Śākyarāja</s>. One should bestow up to the five <s>abhiṣekas</s> with their presiding lords. After the <s>abhiṣeka</s>:

body.text:
oṃ sarvatathāgatadhūpapūjāmeghasamudraspharaṇasamaye huṃ /
oṃ sarvatathāgatapuṣpapūjāmeghasamudraspharaṇasamaye huṃ /
oṃ sarvatathāgatadīpapūjāmeghasamudraspharaṇasamaye huṃ /
oṃ sarvatathāgatagandhapūjāmeghasamudraspharaṇasamaye huṃ /
tato lāsyādicatuṣṭayena pūjayet /
vajram ullālayan vajravācāśatākṣarapūrvavat stutiṃ kuryāt / tataḥ /
body.translated_text: <s>Oṃ sarvatathāgatadhūpapūjāmeghasamudraspharaṇasamaye huṃ</s>! <s>Oṃ sarvatathāgatapuṣpapūjāmeghasamudraspharaṇasamaye huṃ</s>! <s>Oṃ sarvatathāgatadīpapūjāmeghasamudraspharaṇasamaye huṃ</s>! <s>Oṃ sarvatathāgatagandhapūjāmeghasamudraspharaṇasamaye huṃ</s>! Then one should make offerings with the group of four beginning with <s>Lāsyā</s>. Brandishing the <s>vajra</s>, one should make praises with the hundred-syllable <s>vajra</s>-speech as before. Then:

children.translated_text: Those whose nature is the unequaled, immovable, incomparable, essential <s>Dharma</s>,
Whose nature is compassion, who remove suffering in the world,
Bestowers of the attainment of all good qualities universally,

body.translated_text: Whose nature is the unequaled, immovable, incomparable, supreme, foremost <s>Dharma</s>,
Gone like space, they are not found [to have inherent existence],
Not even a mote of a particle of a quality-atom in the boundless,
In those who bestow the supreme attainment of the clear being-realm,
In those of unequaled, universal attainments beyond comparison,
Constantly pure, arisen from the force of compassion,
The fulfillment of aspirations, the nature of non-cessation,
Universally devoted to accomplishing the welfare of the world,
Constantly shines forth—[such is the nature] of those whose essence is great compassion.
The conduct of the compassion-journey does not go to cessation;
It goes, bestowing the supreme attainment of the three worlds.
Gone to perfect completion in the immeasurable and boundless,
Even in those gone to good destinies—ah, what good <s>Dharma</s>!
May they, the bestowers of the supreme pledge-attainment, grant [it] to me!
The state of boon-granting has always gone to the state of good destiny,
Bestowing the supreme attainment of the entire three worlds,
Gone through the three times as <s>Sugatas</s>, unobstructed.

body.text: sarvatra jihvāśatamukhena stotropahāram adhimucya vajraghaṇṭādharaḥ stutiṃ karyāt /
body.translated_text: Everywhere, with a hundred mouths and tongues, having delighted in the offering of praise, holding a <s>vajra-ghaṇṭā</s> (vajra-bell), one should make praises.

body.text: tato daśasu dikṣu sarvatathāgatabodhisattvebhyo laukikalokottarabāhyadevatābhyaś ca sarvapūjābhir balividhim upakaraṇena sahitaṃ baliṃ dadyāt /
body.translated_text: Then, to all <s>Tathāgatas</s> and <s>Bodhisattvas</s> in the ten directions, and to the worldly and supramundane external deities, one should offer <s>bali</s> (offering) together with all offerings and implements.
One should recite extensively.
At the beginning, with the snap-sound and other [gestures], one should attract the hosts of evil [beings],
With the <s>Trailokyavijaya-mudrā</s> (Three-World-Victory seal), accompanied by the three syllables and so forth,
The entirety of the world-realms [consisting of] all evil destiny attainments,
Attraction, lifting up, binding, and destruction.
Four well-arranged <s>mantras</s>:

children.translated_text: With the striking mantras and the like, striking with white mustard seeds,
the bones should be washed, together with white cloth.

body.text:
oṃ śodhana ityādimantreṇa udakena kṣālayet trayabhavanamalaṃ /
oṃ kaṃkaṇītyādimantreṇa kṣalayet pañcagavyena /
oṃ ratne ratna ityādimantreṇa kṣālayet sarvagandhataḥ /
oṃ amoghāvaraṇetyādimantreṇa kṣālayet kṣīragāvitaḥ /
oṃ amṛte amṛta ityādimantreṇa kṣālayet madyam uttamam /
oṃ puṇye puṇya ityādimantreṇodakena kṣālayet antarāntataḥ /
body.translated_text:
With the <s>mantra</s> beginning '<s>Oṃ śodhana</s>' etc., one should wash with water the impurity of the three realms of existence.
With the <s>mantra</s> beginning '<s>Oṃ kaṃkaṇī</s>' etc., one should wash with the five cow-products (<s>pañcagavya</s>).
With the <s>mantra</s> beginning '<s>Oṃ ratne ratna</s>' etc., one should wash with all fragrances.
With the <s>mantra</s> beginning '<s>Oṃ amoghāvaraṇa</s>' etc., one should wash with cow's milk.
With the <s>mantra</s> beginning '<s>Oṃ amṛte amṛta</s>' etc., one should wash with the finest liquor.
With the <s>mantra</s> beginning '<s>Oṃ puṇye puṇya</s>' etc., one should wash with water thoroughly inside and out.

body.text: punar maṃgalagāthāṃ pāṭhayed abhiṣiñcet / mārgaśodhanaṃ kartavyaṃ / dhūpādideyāś caturvidhamantrāḥ /
body.translated_text: Furthermore, one should recite the auspicious verse and perform the consecration (<s>abhiṣeka</s>). The path-purification should be performed. The four types of <s>mantras</s> for incense and other [offerings] should be given.

body.text: hastamātram idaṃ kuṇḍaṃ kartavyaṃ homayet tataḥ //
body.translated_text: A fire-pit (<s>kuṇḍa</s>) one cubit in size should be made; then one should perform the fire offering (<s>homa</s>).
Recollecting that being situated in the evil destinies,
one of virtuous disposition should perform the fire offering for the pacification of obstructions caused by sin.
With ghee, milk, honey, and parched grain mixed with mustard seeds,
sesame, rice, unhusked rice, and the like—two handfuls upon the fuel-sticks.

body.text: anyāny api tu karmāṇi yathā pūrvaṃ tathā kuryāt //
body.translated_text: And other ritual actions too should be performed as before.

body.text: tena saṃpadyate kṣipraṃ sattvānāṃ ca sukhāvaham // iti /
body.translated_text: By that, there quickly comes about what brings happiness to beings. Thus:
The <s>samādhi</s> called <s>Karmarājāgrī</s> (Supreme King of Ritual Action).

body.text: tasmiṃś ca sattve kṛte sati / tatas te nārakaduḥkhād vimuktāḥ santas tuṣiteṣu sarvasattvahitakāriṇaḥ / sugatavad utpannāḥ / tata indreṇa sahitamahāyaśaso devā nṛtyanto 'nantaiḥ pūjāmeghair iha janmani tathāgatapūjārthaṃ puraskṛtya devagaṇā utpātitabodhicittā divyanānāvidhapuṣpadhūpadīpagandhachatradhvajapatākādibhir anekākārābhiś ca śobhitam / vastraratnavarṣādibhiś ca paripūritaṃ kurvanti sma nandanavanam / tato mahāścaryaṃ bhūtam /
body.translated_text: And when this has been performed for that being, then those [beings], having been liberated from the suffering of hell, being in the <s>Tuṣita</s> heaven, become benefactors of all beings—born like <s>Sugatas</s> (Buddhas). Then the gods of great glory, together with <s>Indra</s>, dancing, with boundless clouds of offerings, for the purpose of worshipping the <s>Tathāgata</s> in this very birth, placing the hosts of gods at the fore, their <s>bodhicitta</s> (aspiration to awakening) aroused, with divine flowers of various kinds, incense, lamps, fragrances, parasols, banners, pennants, and many other kinds of adornments, and with showers of cloth-jewels and the like, they made the <s>Nandavana</s> resplendent and complete. Then a great wonder occurred.

body.text:
II
atha bhagavān vajrapāṇir bodhisattvo bhagavato 'dhiṣṭhānena mantrakalparājottarakalpam abhāṣata / vīrāsanād utthāya praharṣan vajram ullalayan śākyādhipaṃ nandan munīśvaraṃ praṇamya sarvāvaraṇaviśodhanavajraṃ nāma samādhiṃ samāpadyedaṃ durgatipariśodhanaṃ nāma hṛdayaṃ svahṛdayād niścacāra /
body.translated_text:
II.
Then the <s>Bhagavān</s> <s>Vajrapāṇi</s> <s>Bodhisattva</s>, through the empowerment of the <s>Bhagavān</s>, spoke the supreme supplementary ritual (<s>uttarakalpa</s>) of the <s>mantra</s> ritual king. Rising from the hero's seat (<s>vīrāsana</s>), rejoicing, brandishing the <s>vajra</s>, having bowed to the Lord of the <s>Śākyas</s>, delighting <s>Munīśvara</s> (Lord of Sages), and having entered the <s>samādhi</s> called <s>Sarvāvaraṇaviśodhanavajra</s> (Vajra that Purifies All Obstructions), this heart [<s>dhāraṇī</s>] called 'Purification of Evil Destinies' issued forth from his own heart:

body.text:
oṃ sarvapāpadahanavajra huṃ phaṭ /
oṃ sarvāpāyaviśodhanavajra huṃ phaṭ /
oṃ sarvakarmāvaraṇāni bhasmīkuru huṃ phaṭ /
oṃ bhruṃ vināśayāvaraṇāni huṃ phaṭ /
oṃ druṃ viśodhayāvaraṇāni huṃ phaṭ /
oṃ jvala jvala dhaka dhaka hana hanāvaraṇāni huṃ phaṭ /
oṃ sruṃ sara sara prasara prasarāvaraṇāni huṃ phaṭ /
oṃ huṃ hara hara sarvāvaraṇāni huṃ phaṭ /
oṃ huṃ phaṭ sarvāvaraṇāni sphoṭaya huṃ phaṭ /
oṃ bhṛta bhṛta sarvāvaraṇāni huṃ phaṭ /
oṃ traṭa traṭa sarvāvaraṇāni huṃ phaṭ /
oṃ chinda chinda vidrava vidrava sarvāvaraṇāni huṃ phaṭ /
oṃ daha daha sarvanarakagatihetuṃ huṃ phaṭ /
oṃ paca paca sarvapretagatihetuṃ huṃ phaṭ /
oṃ matha matha sarvatiryaggatihetuṃ huṃ phaṭ /
body.translated_text:
<s>Oṃ sarva-pāpa-dahana-vajra huṃ phaṭ</s>.
<s>Oṃ sarvāpāya-viśodhana-vajra huṃ phaṭ</s>.
<s>Oṃ sarva-karmāvaraṇāni bhasmīkuru huṃ phaṭ</s>.
<s>Oṃ bhruṃ vināśayāvaraṇāni huṃ phaṭ</s>.
<s>Oṃ druṃ viśodhayāvaraṇāni huṃ phaṭ</s>.
<s>Oṃ jvala jvala dhaka dhaka hana hanāvaraṇāni huṃ phaṭ</s>.
<s>Oṃ sruṃ sara sara prasara prasarāvaraṇāni huṃ phaṭ</s>.
<s>Oṃ huṃ hara hara sarvāvaraṇāni huṃ phaṭ</s>.
<s>Oṃ huṃ phaṭ sarvāvaraṇāni sphoṭaya huṃ phaṭ</s>.
<s>Oṃ bhṛta bhṛta sarvāvaraṇāni huṃ phaṭ</s>.
<s>Oṃ traṭa traṭa sarvāvaraṇāni huṃ phaṭ</s>.
<s>Oṃ chinda chinda vidrava vidrava sarvāvaraṇāni huṃ phaṭ</s>.
<s>Oṃ daha daha sarva-naraka-gati-hetuṃ huṃ phaṭ</s>.
<s>Oṃ paca paca sarva-preta-gati-hetuṃ huṃ phaṭ</s>.
<s>Oṃ matha matha sarva-tiryag-gati-hetuṃ huṃ phaṭ</s>.
Then he spoke their implements [<s>mantras</s>]:

body.text:
oṃ sarvapāpaviśodhani dhama dhama dhūpaya huṃ phaṭ /
oṃ sarvadurgativiśodhani puṣpavilokini huṃ phaṭ /
oṃ sarvāpāyaviśodhani jñānālokakari huṃ phaṭ /
oṃ sarvāpāyagatināśani gandha huṃ phaṭ /
oṃ narakagatyākarṣaṇi huṃ phaṭ /
oṃ sarvanarakagatyuddharaṇi huṃ phaṭ /
oṃ sarvāpāyabandhanavimocani huṃ phaṭ /
oṃ sarvāpāyagatigahanavināśani huṃ phaṭ /
body.translated_text:
<s>Oṃ sarva-pāpa-viśodhani dhama dhama dhūpaya huṃ phaṭ</s>.
<s>Oṃ sarva-durgati-viśodhani puṣpa-vilokini huṃ phaṭ</s>.
<s>Oṃ sarvāpāya-viśodhani jñānāloka-kari huṃ phaṭ</s>.
<s>Oṃ sarvāpāya-gati-nāśani gandha huṃ phaṭ</s>.
<s>Oṃ naraka-gaty-ākarṣaṇi huṃ phaṭ</s>.
<s>Oṃ sarva-naraka-gaty-uddharaṇi huṃ phaṭ</s>.
<s>Oṃ sarvāpāya-bandhana-vimocani huṃ phaṭ</s>.
<s>Oṃ sarvāpāya-gati-gahana-vināśani huṃ phaṭ</s>.

children.translated_text: Then he spoke [the instructions for] the <s>maṇḍala</s>:

children.text: cakrāntaraṃ tu maṇḍalam aṣṭāraiś ca subhūṣitam //
children.translated_text: The <s>maṇḍala</s> within the wheel, beautifully adorned with eight spokes,

body.translated_text: equipped with a hub and rim, with an inner enclosure,
having drawn [the outline], one should depict in the hub the <s>Śākyādhipendra Muni</s> (Supreme Lord of the Śākyas, the Sage).
Then in front of the hero, one should draw <s>Vajrapāṇi</s> of great strength.
Behind, one should draw the <s>Cakravartin</s> (Universal Sovereign).

body.text: dakṣiṇe jayoṣṇīṣaṃ ca vāmato vijayaṃ likhet //
body.translated_text: On the right, <s>Jayoṣṇīṣa</s>; and on the left, one should draw <s>Vijaya</s>.
<s>Tejorāśi</s> (Mass of Splendor) in the southeast; <s>Sitātapatra</s> (White Parasol) in the northeast.

body.text: vikiriṇaṃś caiva vāyavyāṃ nairṛtyāṃ vidhvaṃsakaṃ likhet//
body.translated_text: <s>Vikiriṇa</s> (Scatterer) in the northwest; in the southwest, one should draw <s>Vidhvaṃsaka</s> (Destroyer).
Then one should draw the outer [enclosure]:
Square, with four gates, adorned with four <s>toraṇas</s> (gateways).
The hero's hook (<s>aṅkuśa</s>), noose (<s>pāśa</s>), chain (<s>sphoṭa</s>), and bell (<s>ghaṇṭā</s>) should be placed [at the gates].
In all corners, flowers and the like should be drawn.
Then one should anoint one's own body with garlands, perfume, fragrance, and the like.

body.text: tathaiva vajrācāryaḥ praviśet / jaḥ huṃ vaṃ hoḥ / bhagavan ehi mahākaruṇika dṛśya hoḥ / iti / sarvadevān ākarṣayet / tathaiva praveśyābhiṣiktāḥ sarvadurgatibhyo vimuktāḥ svargalokottarabhūmiṣūdpadyante / sarvasiddhayo 'pi siddhyanti / samyaksaṃbodhiś cāvaśyaṃ prāpyate / pūrvavat sarvakarmāṃ kurvanti / sarvatrāpratihatā bhavanti / unmārjanena sarvajvaragrahādīn mokṣayanti / vajrapāṇir huṃkāreṇa sarvakarmāṇi karoti / anyakalpavidhināpi sarvasādhako bhavati / devanāgayakṣagandharvāsurarākṣasādīnāṃ durgativaśībhūtānāṃ sarvapratibimbādikam abhilikhya japahomābhiṣekaiḥ sarvadurgatibhyo muktir bhavati / atha bhagavān vajradharaḥ siṃhāvalokitena bhagavato mukham avalokya praṇamyaitad avocat / bhagavan paramamudrālakṣaṇam uttamam ābhāṣe karuṇāvedanāvaśagacittena sarvajinā adhiṣṭhānaṃ kurvanti /
body.translated_text: Likewise, the <s>vajrācārya</s> (vajra master) should enter [the maṇḍala]. '<s>Jaḥ huṃ vaṃ hoḥ</s>.' '<s>Bhagavān</s>, come, O greatly compassionate one! Behold! <s>Hoḥ</s>!' Thus one should summon all the deities. Likewise, those who are introduced and consecrated are liberated from all evil destinies and are born in the supramundane stages of heaven. All <s>siddhis</s> (spiritual accomplishments) are also attained. And supreme, perfect awakening is certainly obtained. As before, they perform all ritual actions. They become unobstructed everywhere. By the cleansing rite, they liberate [beings] from all fevers, seizures by spirits, and the like. <s>Vajrapāṇi</s>, with the syllable <s>Huṃ</s>, accomplishes all ritual actions. By the procedure of other <s>kalpas</s> (ritual manuals) as well, one becomes an accomplisher of all [goals]. For gods, <s>nāgas</s>, <s>yakṣas</s>, <s>gandharvas</s>, <s>asuras</s>, <s>rākṣasas</s>, and others who have fallen under the power of evil destinies, by drawing their images and the like and [performing] recitation, fire offering, and consecration, liberation from all evil destinies is achieved. Then the <s>Bhagavān Vajradhara</s>, with a lion's gaze, looked upon the face of the <s>Bhagavān</s>, bowed down, and said: '<s>Bhagavān</s>, I shall speak the supreme characteristic of the ultimate <s>mudrā</s> (seal/gesture). With a mind overcome by compassion, all the Victorious Ones bestow their empowerment.'

body.text: samādhistho lalā@ṭe 'ñjaliṃ kṛtvā praṇamet / buddhānāṃ praṇāmamudrā / yogavit kaṇṭhapradeśe 'ñjaliṃ mukulitapadmākṛtiṃ kuryāt / padmakule padmamudrā / hṛdi vajrāñjaliṃ kṛtvā madhyamāṃgulīsūcīyojayati / vajrakule samayamudrā / vāmahastam uttānam utsaṃge sthāpayitvā tasyopari dakṣiṇaṃ vyavasthāpyāṃguṣṭhadvayaṃ yojayitvā śāntaṃ dṛṣṭvā nirīkṣayet / iyaṃ tathāgatakule samādhimudrā samayaḥ /
body.translated_text: Abiding in <s>samādhi</s>, one should make <s>añjali</s> (palms joined) at the forehead and bow. This is the <s>praṇāma-mudrā</s> (gesture of homage) of the Buddhas. The knower of <s>yoga</s> should make <s>añjali</s> at the throat in the form of a closed lotus bud. In the <s>Padmakula</s> (Lotus Family), this is the <s>padma-mudrā</s> (lotus gesture). Making <s>vajrāñjali</s> (vajra-joined palms) at the heart, one joins the middle fingers like needles. In the <s>Vajrakula</s> (Vajra Family), this is the <s>samaya-mudrā</s> (pledge gesture). Placing the left hand palm-upward in the lap, setting the right hand upon it, and joining the two thumbs—gazing with peaceful eyes—this is the <s>samādhi-mudrā</s> (meditation gesture), the <s>samaya</s> (pledge) of the <s>Tathāgatakula</s> (Tathāgata Family).

body.text: tām eva parivartyānyonyaṃ yojayitvā kaniṣṭhāṃguṣṭhakāni śṛṃkhalākārāṇi baddhvā hṛdi sthāpayet / iyaṃ vajrakule samayamudrā / pūrṇāñjaliṃ kṛtvā kanyasāṃguṣṭhau sūciṃ dhārayec cheṣān prasārayet / iyaṃ padmakule padmamudrā /
body.translated_text: Turning that [gesture] and interlocking [the fingers], binding the little fingers and thumbs in a chain-like form, one should place it at the heart. This is the <s>samaya-mudrā</s> of the <s>Vajrakula</s>. Making full <s>añjali</s>, holding the little fingers and thumbs pointed upward like needles, and extending the rest—this is the <s>padma-mudrā</s> of the <s>Padmakula</s>.

body.text: vajrabandhaṃ dṛḍhīkṛtya madhyamāṃguliṃ vajrasūcīkṛtya kanyasāṃguṣṭhau prasārayet / iyaṃ vajrapāṇer vajramudrā / tasyā eva kaniṣṭhāṃguṣṭhadvayaṃ tathaiva kṛtvā tarjanyanāmike padmapatrākāraiḥ kuryāt / iyaṃ sarvadurgatipariśodhanarājasya sarvaśodhanamudrā / tasyā eva tarjanyanāmike ratnākāraṃ kuryāt / iyam abhiṣekamudrā / kanyasāṃguṣṭhau pṛthak pṛthag yojayitvā śeṣāḥ prasāritāḥ / sarvaprasahanamudrā /
body.translated_text: Making the <s>vajrabandha</s> (vajra bond) firm, forming the middle fingers into a vajra-needle, and extending the little fingers and thumbs—this is the <s>vajra-mudrā</s> of <s>Vajrapāṇi</s>. Of that same [mudrā], making the two little fingers and thumbs likewise, and forming the index and ring fingers into lotus-petal shapes—this is the <s>sarvaśodhana-mudrā</s> (all-purifying gesture) of <s>Sarvadurgatipariśodhana-rāja</s>. Of that same [mudrā], forming the index and ring fingers into a jewel shape—this is the <s>abhiṣeka-mudrā</s> (consecration gesture). Joining the little fingers and thumbs separately and extending the rest—this is the <s>sarvaprasahana-mudrā</s> (all-subduing gesture).

body.text:
vāmahastas tathaiva parivartitaḥ sarvakarmikamudrā /
añjaler ūrdhvakṣepād dhūpamudrā /
tasyā evādhaḥkṣepāt puṣpamudrā /
saiva śaṃkhākāro gandhamudrā /
etām eva prasāritāṃ dhārayed balimudrā /
tasyā eva madhyamādvayād antaram arpaṇamudrā /
vajrabandhamadhyamādvayaṃ madhye parvabhaṃgaṃ kṛtvā sarvāṃgulīḥ prasārayed vikīriṇamudrā /
tasyā eva kanyasādvayāṃguṣṭhadvayam ākṛṣṭaṃ vidhvaṃsanamudrā /
saivāñjaliḥ prabhākāras tejorāśimudrā /
tām evoṣṇīṣasthāne bhrāmayet sitātapatramudrā /
vajrabandhe kanyasāṃguṣṭhadvayaṃ śṛṃkhalākāreṇa baddhvordhvaṃ bhrāmayet / cakramudrā /
body.translated_text:
The left hand likewise reversed—the <s>sarvakarmika-mudrā</s> (all-action gesture).
Throwing upward from the <s>añjali</s>—the <s>dhūpa-mudrā</s> (incense gesture).
Of that same, throwing downward—the <s>puṣpa-mudrā</s> (flower gesture).
That same in conch-shell shape—the <s>gandha-mudrā</s> (perfume gesture).
Holding that same extended—the <s>bali-mudrā</s> (offering gesture).
Of that same, the gap between the two middle [fingers]—the <s>arpaṇa-mudrā</s> (bestowal gesture).
In the <s>vajrabandha</s>, bending the two middle fingers in the center at the joints and extending all fingers—the <s>vikīriṇa-mudrā</s> (scattering gesture).
Of that same, drawing in the two little fingers and two thumbs—the <s>vidhvaṃsana-mudrā</s> (destroying gesture).
That same <s>añjali</s> in radiant form—the <s>tejorāśi-mudrā</s> (splendor-mass gesture).
Rotating that same at the <s>uṣṇīṣa</s> (crown of the head)—the <s>sitātapatra-mudrā</s> (white parasol gesture).
In the <s>vajrabandha</s>, binding the two little fingers and thumbs in chain-form and rotating upward—the <s>cakra-mudrā</s> (wheel gesture).

body.text:
vajrabandhe madhyame vajrākāreṇa tarjanyo ratnākārau kṛtvā śeṣāḥ prabhākārā jayoṣṇīṣamudrā /
tathaiva tarjanīdvayaṃ vajrīkṛtya śeṣāṃgulyo baddhvā vajrākārāh kuryād vijayāsya /
dakṣiṇena varadā vāmenābhayadā tathāgatī /
vajrabandhe tarjanīdvayaṃ vajrākāraṃ kuryād vajramudrā /
etasyā evāṃguladakṣiṇatarjanyākṛṣṭāṃkuśī /
saiva ropākārā śaraḥ / saivāgrāṃguṣṭhā sthāpitā sādhumateḥ /
saiva madhye bhagnā ratnam /
tasyā evāṃgulayaḥ prabhākārās tejaḥ /
tām evoṣṇīṣe sthāpayet ketumudrā /
tām evāgrataḥ sthāpayed vāśamudrā /
saiva padmākārā padmā /
saivāgrākṛṣṭā khaḍgaḥ /
tām eva valayākārāṃ kuryāc cakram /
tām eva padmapatrākārāṃ jihvā /
saivāgraprasāritā viśvā /
saiva suprasāritā rakṣā /
saivāgrataḥ kuṃcitā yakṣā /
saivākuṃcitā bandham /
tasyā eva tarjanīdvayaṃ kuṃcitam aṃkuśam /
saivāgragrastā pāśaḥ /
saivānyonyaṃ granthitā sphoṭaḥ /
tām eva cālayed toṣā /
body.translated_text:
In the <s>vajrabandha</s>, with the middle fingers in vajra form and the index fingers in jewel form, and the rest in radiant form—the <s>jayoṣṇīṣa-mudrā</s>.
Likewise, making the two index fingers into vajra form and binding the remaining fingers in vajra shapes—this is [the mudrā] of <s>Vijaya</s>.
With the right [hand] in the gesture of granting (<s>varadā</s>) and the left in the gesture of fearlessness (<s>abhayā</s>)—that of the <s>Tathāgatī</s>.
In the <s>vajrabandha</s>, making the two index fingers into vajra form—the <s>vajra-mudrā</s>.
Of that same, the right index finger drawn [back]—the hook (<s>aṅkuśī</s>).
That same in arrow form—the arrow (<s>śara</s>). That same with the tips of the thumbs placed—[the mudrā] of <s>Sādhumati</s>.
That same bent in the middle—the jewel (<s>ratna</s>).
Of that same, the fingers in radiant form—splendor (<s>tejas</s>).
Placing that same at the <s>uṣṇīṣa</s>—the banner (<s>ketu</s>) gesture.
Placing that same in front—the speech (<s>vāśa</s>) gesture.
That same in lotus form—the lotus (<s>padmā</s>).
That same with the tip drawn—the sword (<s>khaḍga</s>).
Making that same in bracelet form—the wheel (<s>cakra</s>).
Making that same in lotus-petal form—the tongue (<s>jihvā</s>).
That same with the tip extended—the universal (<s>viśvā</s>).
That same well-extended—the protection (<s>rakṣā</s>).
That same with the tip curved—the <s>yakṣā</s>.
That same curved—the bond (<s>bandha</s>).
Of that same, the two index fingers curved—the hook (<s>aṅkuśa</s>).
That same with the tip grasped—the noose (<s>pāśa</s>).
That same mutually knotted—the chain (<s>sphoṭa</s>).
Shaking that same—the bell (<s>toṣā</s>).

body.text: atha khalu bhagavān vajrapāṇis taṃ śakrabrahmāpramukhaṃ mahāparṣadmaṇḍalam avalokya sādhukāraiḥ saṃtoṣya sādhu sādhu śakrapramukhā devaputrā yad yuṣmākam īdṛśaṃ pratibhānaṃ sajātaṃ tat sādhu pratipadyadhvaṃ deśayāmi /
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bhagavān Vajrapāṇi</s>, surveying the great assembly circle headed by <s>Śakra</s> and <s>Brahmā</s>, having pleased them with acclaim, said: 'Excellent, excellent, O <s>devaputras</s> led by <s>Śakra</s>! Since such inspiration has arisen in you, that is excellent. Apply yourselves! I shall teach.'

body.text: atha khalu bhagavān vajrapāṇiḥ sarvāmitāyusspharaṇasaṃbhavavajraṃ nāma samādhiṃ samāpadyāparimitāyuḥpuṇyajñānasaṃbhāravardhanaṃ nāma sarvatathāgatahṛdayaṃ svahṛdayād niścacāra /
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bhagavān Vajrapāṇi</s>, having entered the <s>samādhi</s> called <s>Sarvāmitāyusspharaṇasaṃbhavavajra</s> (Vajra Born from the Radiance of All Immeasurable Life), uttered from his own heart the heart [<s>dhāraṇī</s>] of all <s>Tathāgatas</s> called <s>Aparimitāyuḥpuṇyajñānasaṃbhāravardhana</s> (Increase of the Accumulation of Immeasurable Life, Merit, and Wisdom):
<s>Oṃ puṇye puṇye mahāpuṇye 'parimitapuṇye 'parimitāyuḥ-puṇya-jñāna-saṃbhāropacaya-kāriṇi svāhā</s>

body.text: asyāṃ sarvatathāgatahṛdayadhāraṇyāṃ bhāṣitamātrāyāṃ sarvāpāyāḥ praśāntā mocitaś cātmā sarve narakapretatiryaggatipannāḥ sattvāḥ prajānanti /
body.translated_text: Immediately upon the utterance of this heart-<s>dhāraṇī</s> of all <s>Tathāgatas</s>, all evil destinies were pacified, and the self was liberated; all beings fallen into the realms of hell, hungry ghosts, and animals came to understand.

body.text: sarve ca lokadhātavo 'vabhāsitā avabhāsya ca dvādaśakāraṃ buddhakṛtyaṃ kṛtvā tasmin eva sarvatathāgatahṛdayadharmākṣare praviṣṭāny abhūvan /
body.translated_text: And all world-realms were illuminated, and having illuminated them and performed the twelve-fold Buddha activity, [the rays] entered into that very syllable of the Dharma of the heart of all <s>Tathāgatas</s>.

body.text: atha khalu bhagavān punar apy amitāyurvajraprabhākarīṃ nāma samādhiṃ samāpadyemaṃ sarvatathāgatāyurvajraṃ nāma hṛdayadhāraṇīm abhāṣata /
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bhagavān</s> again, having entered the <s>samādhi</s> called <s>Amitāyurvajraprabhākarī</s> (Producing the Radiance of the Vajra of Immeasurable Life), spoke this heart-<s>dhāraṇī</s> called <s>Sarvatathāgatāyurvajra</s> (Vajra of the Life of All Tathāgatas):
<s>Oṃ amṛte 'mṛte 'mṛtodbhave 'mṛtasaṃbhave 'mṛta-vikrānta-gāmini sarva-kleśa-kṣayaṃkari svāhā</s>

body.text: athāsyāṃ bhāṣitamātrāyāṃ tathaiva sarvasattvānāṃ sarvaduḥkhāni praśāntāni /
body.translated_text: And immediately upon its utterance, likewise all sufferings of all beings were pacified.

body.text: atha bhagavān punar apy amoghāvaraṇavināśanīṃ nāma samādhiṃ samāpadyemaṃ sarvatathāgatāvaraṇatroṭanaṃ nāma hṛdayadhāraṇīṃ svahṛdayād niścacāra /
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bhagavān</s> again, having entered the <s>samādhi</s> called <s>Amoghāvaraṇavināśanī</s> (Destroyer of Infallible Obstructions), uttered from his own heart this heart-<s>dhāraṇī</s> called <s>Sarvatathāgatāvaraṇatroṭana</s> (Shattering of All Tathāgata Obstructions):

body.text: oṃ kaṃkaṇi kaṃkaṇi rocani rocani troṭani troṭani pratihana pratihana sarvakarmaparaṃparāṇi sarvasattvānāṃ svāhā /
body.translated_text: <s>Oṃ kaṃkaṇi kaṃkaṇi rocani rocani troṭani troṭani pratihana pratihana sarva-karma-paraṃparāṇi sarva-sattvānāṃ svāhā</s>
Immediately upon its utterance, likewise everything came to pass.

body.text: atha khalu bhagavān punar api sarvāvaraṇavimalaviśuddhivajraṃ nāma samādhiṃ samāpadyemāṃ sarvatathāgatāśeṣāvaraṇavināśanīṃ nāma hṛdayadhāraṇīṃ svahṛdayād niścacāra /
body.translated_text: Then <s>Bhagavān</s> again entered the <s>samādhi</s> called <s>Sarvāvaraṇavimalaviśuddhivajra</s> (Vajra of Stainless Purification of All Obscurations) and uttered from his heart this <s>hṛdaya-dhāraṇī</s> (heart-spell) called the Destroyer of All Residual Obscurations of All <s>Tathāgatas</s>:

body.text: oṃ ratne ratne mahāratne ratnasaṃbhave ratnakiraṇe ratnamālāviśuddhe śodhaya sarvapāpaṃ huṃ phaṭ /
body.translated_text: "Oṃ Ratne Ratne Mahāratne Ratnasaṃbhave Ratnakiraṇe Ratnamālāviśuddhe, purify all sins, Hūṃ Phaṭ!"

body.text: asyāṃ bhāṣitamātrāyāṃ sarvamārabhavanāni dhvastāni vidhvaṃsitāny abhūvan /
body.translated_text: The moment this was spoken, all the abodes of <s>Māra</s> were shattered and demolished.

body.text: atha khalu bhagavān punar apy amoghāpratihatasarvāvaraṇavidhvaṃsanināmasamādhiṃ samāpadyemāṃ sarvatathāgatahṛdayadhāraṇīṃ svahṛdayād niścacāra /
body.translated_text: Then <s>Bhagavān</s> again entered the <s>samādhi</s> called <s>Amoghāpratihatasarvāvaraṇavidhvaṃsanī</s> (Infallible, Unobstructed Destroyer of All Obscurations) and uttered from his heart this <s>hṛdaya-dhāraṇī</s> of all <s>Tathāgatas</s>:

body.text: om amoghāpratihatasarvāvaraṇavināśani hara hara huṃ phaṭ /
body.translated_text: "Oṃ Amoghāpratihatāsarvāvaraṇavināśani, destroy, destroy, Hūṃ Phaṭ!"

body.text:
asyāṃ bhāṣitamātrāyāṃ sarvopamalokadhātuḥ kampitaḥ prakampitaḥ saṃprakampitaś calitaḥ pracalitaḥ saṃpracalitaḥ kṣubhitaḥ prakṣubhitaḥ saṃprakṣubhitaḥ /
anekāny āścaryādbhutāni loke saṃdṛśyante sma /
tathaiṣāṃ maṇḍalaṃ bhavati /
body.translated_text:
The moment this was spoken, the entire world-system with its surroundings trembled, shook greatly, and shook exceedingly; quaked, quaked greatly, and quaked exceedingly; was agitated, greatly agitated, and exceedingly agitated.
Many marvels and wonders were seen in the world.
And thus is their <s>maṇḍala</s>:
Four-cornered, with four gates, endowed with four sides,
Furnished with four <s>toraṇas</s> (archways), equipped with rim and projections,
Within it one should draw the supreme wheel-<s>maṇḍala</s>,
Endowed with four spokes and a supreme hub-circle,

body.text: tasya madhye likhed nāthaṃ vajrapāṇiṃ mahābalam //
body.translated_text: In its center one should draw the protector <s>Vajrapāṇi</s> of great strength,
Holding <s>vajra</s> and <s>ghaṇṭā</s> (bell), gentle, with a face smiling like the full moon,
In the middle portions of the eastern spoke one should draw the lord <s>Akṣobhya</s>,
To the south one should draw <s>Ratna</s> (Ratnasaṃbhava), to the west the supreme lotus one (<s>Amitābha</s>),
To the north one should draw the hero called <s>Amogha</s> (Amoghasiddhi) of great strength,
One should draw all the <s>Tathāgatas</s> in the splendor of <s>Cakravartins</s>,
Resembling moon-discs, adorned with all ornaments,
With hands in <s>varada</s> (boon-granting) and <s>abhaya</s> (fearlessness) gestures, well-seated in <s>vajraparyaṅka</s> (vajra cross-legged posture),
In all the corner sections, one should likewise draw incense-offerings and so forth,

body.text: dvārapālāś ca te lekhyāḥ kruddhāḥ krodhaparāyaṇāḥ //
body.translated_text: And the gate-guardians should be drawn, wrathful and devoted to wrath,

body.text: tataḥ praviśya svayaṃ yogī ākarṣayed mantradevatāḥ //
body.translated_text: Then the yogin, having entered himself, should draw in the mantra-deities,

body.text: jaḥ huṃ vaṃ hoḥ bhagavan vajra ehy ehi samayas tvam //
body.translated_text: "Jaḥ Hūṃ Vaṃ Hoḥ! O <s>Bhagavān</s> <s>Vajra</s>, come, come! You are the <s>samaya</s> (pledge)!"
Then, having briefly worshipped the protector who has come,
One should cause entry for the destruction of death, and the fears of the death-serpent,
"Oṃ <s>Vajrasamaye</s> Hūṃ!"
Having formed the <s>vajraterintirī</s>, one should cause the entry of one endowed with a jewel-hand,

body.text: puṣpamālānvito vāpi kṣepayed maṇḍale tu tam //
body.translated_text: Or one adorned with a flower-garland should be cast into the <s>maṇḍala</s>,
"Oṃ, accept, O <s>Vajra</s>, Hūṃ!"

body.text:
tataḥ samayaṃ deyaṃ / oṃ vajrasamaye huṃ /
tato 'nenodghāṭayed vajram / oṃ vajrahāsodghāṭaya huṃ /
tato 'nena darśayet / oṃ vajra dṛśya hoḥ /
tato 'bhiṣekam anena dadyāt /
oṃ vajrābhiṣiñca huṃ / oṃ buddhābhiṣiñca oṃ / oṃ ratnābhiṣiñca trāṃ /
oṃ padmābhiṣiñca hrīḥ / oṃ karmābhiṣiñca aḥ /
tataḥ kalaśābhiṣekaṃ dadyāt /
oṃ vajrakalaśābhiṣiñca huṃ / oṃ buddhakalaśābhiṣiñca oṃ /
oṃ ratnakalaśābhiṣḥiñca trāṃ / oṃ padmakalaśābhiṣiñca hrīḥ /
oṃ karmakalaśābhiṣiñca aḥ /
oṃ mālābhiṣiñca trāṃ / oṃ vajrapaṭāvalambanābhiṣiñca trīṃ /
oṃ buddhamudrābhiṣiñca om / oṃ vajramudrābhiṣiñca huṃ /
oṃ ratnamudrābhiṣiñca trāṃ / oṃ padmamudrābhiṣiñca hrīḥ /
oṃ karmamudrābhiṣiñca aḥ /
oṃ vajranāmābhiṣiñca oṃ huṃ trāṃ hrīḥ aḥ / oṃ karmābhiṣiñca huṃ aḥ /
oṃ vajracakrābhiṣiñca huṃ bhrūm /
oṃ vajracakrādhipatis tvām abhiṣiñca (yet) oṃ oṃ oṃ / huṃ huṃ huṃ / trāṃ trāṃ trāṃ / hrīḥ hrīḥ hrīḥ / aḥ aḥ aḥ /
oṃ vajradhāriṇy abhiṣiñca huṃ / oṃ tathāgatadhāriṇy abhiṣiñca oṃ /
oṃ ratnadhāriṇy abhiṣiñca trāṃ / oṃ padmadhāriṇy abhiṣiñca hrīḥ /
oṃ karmadhāriṇy abhiṣiñca aḥ /
oṃ sarvatathāgataguhyābhiṣiñca om / oṃ vajraguhyābhiṣiñca huṃ /
oṃ ratnaguhyābhiṣiñca trāṃ / oṃ padmaguhyabhiṣiñca hrīḥ /
oṃ karmaguhyābhiṣiñca aḥ /
oṃ prajñopāyasamāyogābhiṣiñca huṃ aḥ /
body.translated_text:
Then the <s>samaya</s> (pledge) should be given: "Oṃ <s>Vajrasamaye</s> Hūṃ!"
Then with this one should open the <s>vajra</s>: "Oṃ <s>Vajrahāsa</s>, open, Hūṃ!"
Then with this one should show: "Oṃ <s>Vajra</s>, see, Hoḥ!"
Then with this one should give the <s>abhiṣeka</s> (consecration):
"Oṃ <s>Vajra</s>, consecrate, Hūṃ! Oṃ <s>Buddha</s>, consecrate, Oṃ! Oṃ <s>Ratna</s>, consecrate, Trāṃ!
Oṃ <s>Padma</s>, consecrate, Hrīḥ! Oṃ <s>Karma</s>, consecrate, Aḥ!"
Then one should give the vessel-<s>abhiṣeka</s>:
"Oṃ <s>Vajra</s>-vessel, consecrate, Hūṃ! Oṃ <s>Buddha</s>-vessel, consecrate, Oṃ!
Oṃ <s>Ratna</s>-vessel, consecrate, Trāṃ! Oṃ <s>Padma</s>-vessel, consecrate, Hrīḥ!
Oṃ <s>Karma</s>-vessel, consecrate, Aḥ!
Oṃ garland, consecrate, Trāṃ! Oṃ <s>vajra</s>-banner-pendant, consecrate, Trīṃ!
Oṃ <s>Buddha-mudrā</s>, consecrate, Oṃ! Oṃ <s>Vajra-mudrā</s>, consecrate, Hūṃ!
Oṃ <s>Ratna-mudrā</s>, consecrate, Trāṃ! Oṃ <s>Padma-mudrā</s>, consecrate, Hrīḥ!
Oṃ <s>Karma-mudrā</s>, consecrate, Aḥ!
Oṃ <s>Vajra</s>-name, consecrate, Oṃ Hūṃ Trāṃ Hrīḥ Aḥ! Oṃ <s>Karma</s>, consecrate, Hūṃ Aḥ!
Oṃ <s>Vajracakra</s>, consecrate, Hūṃ Bhrūṃ!
Oṃ, Lord of the <s>Vajracakra</s>, consecrate you, Oṃ Oṃ Oṃ / Hūṃ Hūṃ Hūṃ / Trāṃ Trāṃ Trāṃ / Hrīḥ Hrīḥ Hrīḥ / Aḥ Aḥ Aḥ!
Oṃ <s>Vajradhāriṇī</s>, consecrate, Hūṃ! Oṃ <s>Tathāgatadhāriṇī</s>, consecrate, Oṃ!
Oṃ <s>Ratnadhāriṇī</s>, consecrate, Trāṃ! Oṃ <s>Padmadhāriṇī</s>, consecrate, Hrīḥ!
Oṃ <s>Karmadhāriṇī</s>, consecrate, Aḥ!
Oṃ, secret of all <s>Tathāgatas</s>, consecrate, Oṃ! Oṃ, <s>vajra</s>-secret, consecrate, Hūṃ!
Oṃ, <s>ratna</s>-secret, consecrate, Trāṃ! Oṃ, <s>padma</s>-secret, consecrate, Hrīḥ!
Oṃ, <s>karma</s>-secret, consecrate, Aḥ!
Oṃ, consecrate through the union of <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom) and <s>upāya</s> (means), Hūṃ Aḥ!"

body.text:
evam abhiṣiñcyāyurvardhanīṃ vidyāṃ dadyāt / oṃ vajrāyuṣi huṃ aḥ /
asyaḥ sādhanaṃ bhavati /
body.translated_text:
Having thus consecrated, one should give the life-extending <s>vidyā</s>: "Oṃ <s>Vajrāyuṣi</s> Hūṃ Aḥ!"
This is its <s>sādhana</s> (practice):

body.text: vajrāyur bhagavāñ candramaṇḍalārūḍhaś candrābhaḥ sarvābharaṇamaṇḍitaḥ / abhayahasto varadaś ca / amṛtaṃ kṣarantaṃ / tasyādhastāt sādhakaṃ prasāritāṃjalihastaṃ ūrdhvamukhaṃ bhagavantaṃ nirīkṣayantaṃ likhet / pañcopacāreṇa pūjāṃ kṛtvā tasyāgrataḥ śatasahasraṃ japet /
body.translated_text: <s>Vajrāyus</s> <s>Bhagavān</s>, mounted on a moon-disc, moon-colored, adorned with all ornaments, with one hand in <s>abhaya</s> (fearlessness) and one in <s>varada</s> (boon-granting), dripping <s>amṛta</s> (nectar). Below him one should draw the practitioner with palms joined and extended, face upward, gazing at <s>Bhagavān</s>. Having performed worship with the five offerings, one should recite before him one hundred thousand times.

body.text: tataḥ pūrṇamāsyāṃ mahatīṃ pūjāṃ kṛtvā kapilāgoghṛtaṃ nave bhāṇḍe sthāpya vāmavajreṇākramya bhagavantaṃ pradhyāyan sakalāṃ rātrīṃ japet / tato gandhaṃ vinasyati / apūrvaṃ vā gandham udvahati / ūṣmā dhūmaḥ śikhā vā niścarati / raśmyulkā pramuñcati / evam ādibhir nimittais tad ghṛtaṃ navanītaṃ tailaṃ vā / udakaṃ dadhi kṣīraṃ madyaṃ rudhiraṃ vasām asthikāṃ vā / māṃsaṃ vānyatamaṃ vā saṃprasādhya pratyūṣe rakṣādikaṃ ca kṛtvā / ātmānaṃś ca saṃśodhya pibed bhakṣayet / yathā nimittena yāvadā candrārkāyur bhavati / vajrasattvaś ceti / adhamenādhamā siddhir bhavet / nātra saṃśayaḥ / nirmittena bhavel loke nirvyādhir medhānvitaḥ / valipalitasukhātmā dṛḍhakāyaḥ śatāyuḥ / anyāny api karmāṇi śāntipuṣṭivaśādikaṃ karoty avicāreṇa jāpamātrāt / na saṃśayaḥ /
body.translated_text: Then, on the full moon, having performed a great worship, placing ghee from a tawny cow in a new vessel, stepping on the left vajra, meditating on <s>Bhagavān</s>, one should recite throughout the entire night. Then the scent vanishes, or it produces an extraordinary fragrance; warmth, smoke, or a flame emerges; rays or meteors are emitted. By such signs, that ghee, or butter, or oil, or water, yogurt, milk, liquor, blood, fat, or bone — or flesh, or any other substance — having accomplished it, at dawn having performed protection and so forth, and having purified oneself, one should drink or eat it. According to the sign, one's lifespan becomes as long as the sun and moon; and one becomes <s>Vajrasattva</s>. By the lowest, the lowest <s>siddhi</s> (accomplishment) is attained — there is no doubt in this. By the sign, one becomes in the world free from disease, endowed with intelligence, with youthful vigor free from wrinkles and gray hair, with a firm body, and a lifespan of a hundred years. Other rites too — pacification, increase, subjugation, and so forth — are accomplished without hesitation merely by recitation. There is no doubt.

body.text: atha catvāro mahārājāno bhagavantaṃ vajrapāṇiṃ praṇipatyaivam āhuḥ / vayam api bhagavan sarvasattvānām arthāya hitāya sukhāya svakasvakāni hṛdayāni bhāṣayāmaḥ / ājñāpayatu bhagavān ājñāpayatu vajradhṛk / sādhu sādhu mahārājāno deśayadhvam aham anumode / adhitiṣṭhāmi svasamayam /
body.translated_text: Then the four great kings, having bowed to <s>Bhagavān</s> <s>Vajrapāṇi</s>, spoke thus: "We too, O <s>Bhagavān</s>, shall utter our own respective <s>hṛdayas</s> (heart-mantras) for the benefit, welfare, and happiness of all beings. May <s>Bhagavān</s> command! May the <s>Vajra</s>-bearer command!" "Excellent, excellent, O great kings! Teach them — I approve! I empower your <s>samaya</s> (pledge)."

body.text: atha vaiśravaṇo mahāyakṣarājā bhagavadanujñāto 'numodito 'dhiṣṭhitas svahṛdayaṃ svahṛdayād niścacāra / oṃ vaiḥ / atha dhṛtarāṣṭras tathaiva svahṛdayam abhāṣata / oṃ dhṛḥ / atha virūḍhakaḥ kumbhāṇḍamahārājā svahṛdayam abhāṣata / oṃ viḥ / atha virūpākṣo nāgamahārājā tathaiva svahṛdayam abhāṣata / oṃ kṣaḥ /
body.translated_text: Then <s>Vaiśravaṇa</s>, the great <s>Yakṣa</s>-king, authorized, approved, and empowered by <s>Bhagavān</s>, uttered his <s>hṛdaya</s> from his heart: "Oṃ Vaiḥ!" Then <s>Dhṛtarāṣṭra</s> likewise uttered his <s>hṛdaya</s>: "Oṃ Dhṛḥ!" Then <s>Virūḍhaka</s>, the great <s>Kumbhāṇḍa</s>-king, uttered his <s>hṛdaya</s>: "Oṃ Viḥ!" Then <s>Virūpākṣa</s>, the great <s>Nāga</s>-king, likewise uttered his <s>hṛdaya</s>: "Oṃ Kṣaḥ!"
And thus is their <s>maṇḍala</s>:
Four-cornered, with four gates, adorned with five <s>maṇḍalas</s>,

body.text: tasya madhye likhed nāthaṃ vajrapāṇiṃ sagarvitam //
body.translated_text: In its center one should draw the protector <s>Vajrapāṇi</s> in his proud form,

body.text: tasya vāme pārśve tu likhed vaiśravaṇaṃ śubham //
body.translated_text: On his left side one should draw the auspicious <s>Vaiśravaṇa</s>,
Holding a mace and a mongoose, adorned with jewel ornaments,
Stout, mounted on a lion throne, golden-colored, of great splendor,
The wise one should draw him raining forth a flood of jewels from the auspicious vase and other treasures,
In front, <s>Dhṛtarāṣṭra</s>, devoted to playing the <s>vīṇā</s> (lute),
Graceful, dark-colored, adorned with all ornaments,
To the south one should draw the hero <s>Virūḍhaka</s> with sword in hand,
To the west, <s>Virūpākṣa</s>, the supreme bearer of the <s>vajra</s>-noose,
Complete with seven hoods, with reddish eyes emerging,
At all the gate-positions, likewise the gate-guardians,

body.text: tataḥ praviśet svayaṃ mantrī mudrayā cakrasaṃjñayā //
body.translated_text: Then the <s>mantrī</s> (practitioner) himself should enter with the <s>mudrā</s> called the wheel,
One should draw in <s>Bhagavān</s>, then assemble the kings,
Having drawn them in, the learned one should worship with offering-vessels according to the rite,
Then one should cause the disciples to enter, adorned with flower garlands,

body.text: rājānaṃ kṣatriyaṃ vāpi brāhmaṇādikam eva vā //
body.translated_text: Whether a king, a <s>Kṣatriya</s>, a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, or others,
The knower of mantras, with this mantra, with the <s>mudrā</s> of the <s>vajra</s>-holder —
"Oṃ <s>Vajrasamaye</s> Hūṃ!"

children.text: tataḥ puṣpaṃ ratnaṃ vā kṣepayed anena ca /
children.translated_text: Then one should cast a flower or a jewel with this:
"Oṃ Vaḥ, accept, O supreme ones!"

children.text: patati yasya rājasya so 'sya sidhyati nānyathā //
children.translated_text: Upon whichever king's [domain] it falls, that one succeeds for him, not otherwise,

body.translated_text: Then one should consecrate with four vessels placed at the corners,
The fifth, of <s>Vajrapāṇi</s>, one should consecrate with the <s>mudrā</s> itself,
Thus, by this same sequential procedure, through the consecration called the <s>maṇḍala</s>,

body.text: atha rājābhavate rājā rājā bhavate mahān //
body.translated_text: Then a king becomes a king, a king becomes great,
The glorious lord of <s>Jambudvīpa</s>, the excellent lord of the four continents,
Through the four consecrations and entry through the four gates,
"I, <s>Vajradhara</s>, the king, shall protect him as my own son,"
"We, the four great kings, shall constantly protect the ruler,"
"Together with his servants and retinue, his entire kingdom, city, and domain,"

body.text: duṣṭān tasya haniṣyāmaḥ pararāṣṭraṃ ca tasya ca //
body.translated_text: "We shall destroy his enemies and [protect] his rival kingdoms,"
"And the fear of disease and death, famine, calamity, and affliction,"

body.text: vaiśravaṇaḥ kurute puṣṭiṃ dhṛtarāṣṭras tu śāntikaṃ //
body.translated_text: "<s>Vaiśravaṇa</s> brings increase, <s>Dhṛtarāṣṭra</s> brings pacification,"
"<s>Virūḍhaka</s> shall destroy untimely death along with cattle and kinsmen,"
"<s>Virūpākṣa</s> brings safety and the destruction of famine and the like,"
"In brief, we shall fulfill all his wishes and all his desires,"

body.text: karoma vajrapāṇis tu drohaṃ yadi na niścayāt //
body.translated_text: "As shall <s>Vajrapāṇi</s>, if there is no treachery with certainty."
Then the guardians of the ten directions, having bowed to <s>Bhagavān</s>, spoke thus:
"We too, O <s>Bhagavān</s>, for the welfare and happiness of all beings,"
"Offer our own respective <s>hṛdayas</s> (heart-mantras)."

body.text: sādhu sādhu lokapālāḥ sādhu sādhu vadateti //
body.translated_text: "Excellent, excellent, O guardians of the world! Excellent, excellent — speak!" Thus.
Then <s>Īśāna</s>, lord of beings, gives his <s>hṛdaya</s>:

body.text: oṃ i / om ī / oṃ aḥ / oṃ yaḥ / oṃ ṛḥ / oṃ vaḥ / oṃ yaḥ / oṃ kuḥ / oṃ āḥ / oṃ vraḥ /
body.translated_text: "Oṃ I! Oṃ Ī! Oṃ Aḥ! Oṃ Yaḥ! Oṃ Ṛḥ! Oṃ Vaḥ! Oṃ Yaḥ! Oṃ Kuḥ! Oṃ Āḥ! Oṃ Vraḥ!"

children.translated_text: And thus is their <s>maṇḍala</s>:

children.text: maṇḍalaṃ pūrvavad likhed madhye nāthaṃ tathaiva ca //
children.translated_text: One should draw the <s>maṇḍala</s> as before, and likewise the protector in the center,

body.text: dikpālās tu svadigbhāge sthāpayet purato dvayam //
body.translated_text: The directional guardians should be placed in their own respective directions, with two in front,

body.text: ādityaṃ varāharūpan tu dvārapālās tathaiva ca //
body.translated_text: <s>Āditya</s> (the Sun) in the form of a boar, and likewise the gate-guardians,

body.text: tataś cākṛṣya tān sarvān pūjayet sarvapūjayā //
body.translated_text: Then, having drawn all of them in, one should worship with all offerings,

body.text: tataḥ praveśayet śiṣyān praviśya svayam eva tu //
body.translated_text: Then, having entered oneself, one should cause the disciples to enter,
One should consecrate with vessels empowered by the mantras of the directional guardians and others,
Then one should give the <s>hṛdaya</s> for the purpose of <s>sādhana</s> (practice), out of benevolence,
The directional guardians stationed in their own directions accomplish without hesitation,

body.text: atha te tuṣṭā evam āhuḥ / yaḥ kaścid bhagavan rājā kṣatriyo vā mūrdhny abhiṣiktaḥ / etad maṇḍalaṃ praviśyābhiṣekaṃ gṛhṇet / anyo vā śrāddhaḥ kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā / tasya vayaṃ bhagavan sarvadā sarvatra rakṣāvaraṇaguptiṃ saṃvidhāsyāmaḥ / pararāṣṭrāṇi ca vardhayiṣyāmaḥ / kālena kālaṃ varṣiṣyāmaḥ / sasyapuṣpaphalāni ca niṣpādayiṣyāmaḥ /
body.translated_text: Then, being pleased, they spoke thus: "Whatever king, O <s>Bhagavān</s>, or <s>Kṣatriya</s> who has been anointed on the head, enters this <s>maṇḍala</s> and receives the <s>abhiṣeka</s> (consecration) — or any other faithful son or daughter of good family — for that person, O <s>Bhagavān</s>, we shall always and everywhere provide protection, shelter, and guardianship. We shall increase the rival kingdoms. We shall send rain in due season. And we shall bring crops, flowers, and fruits to fruition."

body.text: atha yamo mahādharmarājā bhagavantaṃ praṇamyaivam āha /
body.translated_text: Then <s>Yama</s>, the great king of <s>Dharma</s>, having bowed to <s>Bhagavān</s>, spoke thus:

body.text: ahaṃ bhagavan tasya mahārājña āyur dadāmi / aṣṭakālamaraṇāni pratibādhayāmi /
body.translated_text: "I, O <s>Bhagavān</s>, shall grant longevity to that great king. I shall ward off the eight kinds of untimely death."

body.text: nairṛto mahārākṣasādhipatir evam āha / ahaṃ bhagavan tasya rājño rājaputrasya brāhmaṇasya kṣatriyasya vānyatareṣu vā manuṣyeṣu na vyādhipretapiśācabhayaṃ na rākṣasabhayādikaṃ nākālamṛtyubhayaṃ kariṣyāmi / sarvadā rakṣāvaraṇaguptiṃ kariṣyāmi /
body.translated_text: The great lord of <s>Rākṣasas</s>, <s>Nairṛta</s>, spoke thus: "I, O <s>Bhagavān</s>, for that king, prince, <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, <s>Kṣatriya</s>, or any other human being, shall not cause the fear of disease, <s>pretas</s> (hungry ghosts), or <s>piśācas</s> (goblins), nor the fear of <s>Rākṣasas</s> and the like, nor the fear of untimely death. I shall always provide protection, shelter, and guardianship."

body.text: atha varuṇo mahārājaivam āha / ahaṃ bhagavan tasya mahārājñaḥ sarvadā sarvatra sarvaviṣayaṃ pratipālayiṣyāmi / ārakṣāṃ ca kariṣyāmi / sasyāni ca niṣpādayiṣyāmi / nāgadoṣāni ca na prayacchāmi / viṣāśanīñ ca notsṛjāmi / sarvākālamaraṇāni ca pratibādhayāmi /
body.translated_text: Then the great king <s>Varuṇa</s> spoke thus: 'I, O Blessed One, shall protect that great king always, everywhere, and in all domains. I shall provide safeguarding. I shall bring crops to fruition. I shall not inflict the faults of <s>nāgas</s>. I shall not release poison or lightning. And I shall ward off all untimely deaths.'
Then the lord of the northwest (<s>Vāyu</s>) spoke thus:

body.text: aham api bhagavan tasya mahāsattvasya sarvadā vāyubhayaṃ notsṛjāmi / nākālavātaṃ cotsṛjāmi / sarvasasyapuṣpaphalāni ca pariniṣpādayiṣyāmi / sarvabhayañ ca pratibādhayāmi /
body.translated_text: 'I too, O Blessed One, shall never release the terror of wind upon that great being. I shall not release untimely storms. I shall bring all crops, flowers, and fruits to full ripeness. And I shall ward off all dangers.'

body.text: atha kuvero mahāyakṣarājā bhagavantaṃ namasyaivam āha / ahaṃ bhagavan tasya mahāsattvasyāṣṭāśītibhir mahāyakṣasenāpatibhiḥ sahāgatya sarvakālodyogena sarvadā sarvabhayaṃ pratibādhayāmi / sarvadhanadhānyasamṛddhiñ ca karomi / svajanaparijanadeśaviṣayabhṛtyabandhubāndhavamitraputraduhitṛbhāryādirakṣāṃ ca karomi / gogavyakharoṣṭrameṣagajavājicchāgalādirakṣaṃ karomi /
body.translated_text: Then <s>Kubera</s>, the great <s>Yakṣa</s> king, having bowed to the Blessed One, spoke thus: 'I, O Blessed One, coming together with eighty-two great <s>Yakṣa</s> generals, with effort at all times shall always ward off all dangers for that great being. I shall create prosperity of all wealth and grain. I shall provide protection for his own people, retainers, territory, domain, servants, relatives, kinsmen, friends, sons, daughters, wives, and others. I shall provide protection for cows, buffaloes, donkeys, camels, sheep, elephants, horses, goats, and others.'

body.text: atheśānaḥ sarvabhūtādhipatir bhagavantaṃ praṇipatyaivam āha / ahaṃ bhagavan tasya rājño rājaputrasya kṣatriyasya brāhmaṇasya vā / ihāmutra paritrāṇaṃ parigrahaṃ paripālanaṃ śāntiṃ svastyayanaṃ daṇḍaparihāraṃ śastraparihāraṃ viṣadūṣaṇaṃ viṣanāśanaṃ sīmābandhaṃ dharaṇībandhaṃ digbandhaṃ vajraprākāraṃ vajrakīlanaṃ vajrapañjaraṃ ca karomi / sarvakāryeṣu pratyupasthāpayāmi / kāryeṣv akāryesu nimittaṃ ca darśayāmi / svapne ca sarvaṃ śubhaṃ kathayāmi / sādhayato 'vighnena sarvasiddhiṃ ca dāsyāmi /
body.translated_text: Then <s>Īśāna</s>, the lord of all beings, having prostrated to the Blessed One, spoke thus: 'I, O Blessed One, for that king, prince, <s>kṣatriya</s>, or <s>brāhmaṇa</s>—shall provide protection here and hereafter, shelter, safeguarding, pacification, benediction, warding off of punishment, warding off of weapons, neutralization of poison, destruction of poison, boundary-binding, earth-binding, direction-binding, a <s>vajra</s>-rampart, <s>vajra</s>-staking, and a <s>vajra</s>-cage. I shall attend to all tasks. In matters proper and improper, I shall show omens. In dreams, I shall speak all that is auspicious. And to the one who practices, I shall grant all <s>siddhis</s> (accomplishments) without obstruction.'

body.text: athākāśacārī khagapatir bhagavantaṃ praṇipatyaivam āha / ahaṃ bhagavan sarvadā sarvaṃ ca pathigatasya rājño rājaputrasya rājāmātyasya brāhmaṇasya kṣatriyasya vā svayam āgatya sarvaparivāreṇa rakṣāvaraṇaguptiṃ saṃvidhāsyāmi / sarvāvaraṇaṃ prativārayāmi / sarvavyādhim apanayāmi / sarvadā cānubaddho bhavati / atha pātālādhipatir mahāvarāho bhagavantaṃ namasyaivam āha / ahaṃ bhagavantasya narādhipateś ca nṛpasutasya vā dvijāter dvijasutasya vā kṣatriyavaiśyaśūdrasya vānyatarasya śrāddhasya kulaputrasya kuladuhitur vā sarvadā sarvārthaṃ niṣpādayiṣyāmi / sarvabhayeṣu ca rakṣāṃ kariṣyāmi / anenāpi paritrāyiṣyāmi /
body.translated_text: Then the sky-traveler, lord of birds, having prostrated to the Blessed One, spoke thus: 'I, O Blessed One, shall always personally come to that king, prince, royal minister, <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, or <s>kṣatriya</s> who is traveling, and with my entire retinue shall provide protection, shielding, and guarding. I shall ward off all obstacles. I shall remove all diseases. And I shall be constantly in attendance.' Then <s>Mahāvarāha</s>, the lord of the underworld, having bowed to the Blessed One, spoke thus: 'I shall always accomplish all purposes for the Blessed One's king, prince, or twice-born, son of a twice-born, <s>kṣatriya</s>, <s>vaiśya</s>, <s>śūdra</s>, or any other faithful son of a good family or daughter of a good family. And I shall provide protection in all dangers. By this [power] too, I shall grant deliverance.'

body.text: athāṣṭau mahāgrahāḥ sanakṣatraparivārā evam āhuh / vayaṃ bhagavan saparivārāḥ svakasvakāni hṛdayāni dadāmaḥ / tad bhagavān adhitiṣṭhatu / sādhu sādhv adhitiṣṭhaṃtu mayā bhāṣadhvaṃ mahāgrahāḥ / athādityādayo mahāgrahā bhagavantaṃ namasyābhāṣanta /
body.translated_text: Then the eight great planets, surrounded by their retinues of <s>nakṣatras</s> (lunar mansions), spoke thus: 'We, O Blessed One, together with our retinues, offer our own respective heart-<s>mantras</s>. May the Blessed One please consecrate them.' 'Well done, well done! Speak them with my [blessing], O great planets!' Then <s>Āditya</s> (the Sun) and the other great planets, having bowed to the Blessed One, spoke:

body.text:
om āḥ / oṃ soḥ / oṃ aḥ / oṃ buḥ /
oṃ brḥ / oṃ śuḥ / oṃ sāḥ / oṃ rāḥ /
body.translated_text: <s>Oṃ āḥ</s>! <s>Oṃ soḥ</s>! <s>Oṃ aḥ</s>! <s>Oṃ buḥ</s>! <s>Oṃ brḥ</s>! <s>Oṃ śuḥ</s>! <s>Oṃ sāḥ</s>! <s>Oṃ rāḥ</s>!
Now, their <s>maṇḍala</s> is [as follows]:
Having drawn the Blessed <s>Vajrapāṇi</s> in the form of <s>Trailokyavijaya</s> (Conqueror of the Three Worlds) in the center,
One should draw the four great oceans all around.

body.text: śukrantu tasya purataḥ somaṃ pṛṣṭhato likhet //
body.translated_text: <s>Śukra</s> (Venus) should be drawn in front of him, and <s>Soma</s> (Moon) behind.

body.text: dakṣiṇe bṛhaspatiṃ likhed vāmataś ca budhaṃ likhet //
body.translated_text: One should draw <s>Bṛhaspati</s> (Jupiter) on the right, and <s>Budha</s> (Mercury) on the left.

body.text: agnisthāne tu cāṃgāram ādityaṃ vāyavyāṃ diśi //
body.translated_text: <s>Aṅgāraka</s> (Mars) in the place of <s>Agni</s> (southeast), and <s>Āditya</s> (Sun) in the northwestern direction.
<s>Śanaiścara</s> (Saturn) in the northeast, and <s>Rāhu</s> near the <s>Rākṣasa</s> [direction] (southwest).
The <s>nakṣatras</s> (lunar mansions) should be drawn everywhere, all around in the outer <s>maṇḍala</s>.

body.text: dvāre dvāre tathā dvārīṃ likhec ca krodhamānasam //
body.translated_text: At each gate, one should likewise draw a door-guardian with a wrathful mind.
Having entered with the <s>vajra</s>-holder [<s>mudrā</s>], one should invoke all [the deities].
With the <s>vajrāṅkuśa</s> (vajra-hook) and other [<s>mudrās</s>], one should then introduce the disciples.

body.text:
oṃ vajra hana huṃ phaṭ /
oṃ vajragrahasamaye huṃ phaṭ /
oṃ vajragraha pratīccha samaye huṃ /
body.translated_text: <s>Oṃ vajra hana huṃ phaṭ</s>! <s>Oṃ vajragrahasamaye huṃ phaṭ</s>! <s>Oṃ vajragraha pratīccha samaye huṃ</s>!
Then one should perform the <s>abhiṣeka</s> (consecration) with eight water-vessels,
Consecrated by the eight planets.
Then one should perform the <s>abhiṣeka</s> with the <s>vajra-mudrā</s>.
Then one should accomplish [the rites for] all the planets.

body.text: atha te mahāgrahā bhagavantaṃ namasyaivam āhuḥ / vayaṃ bhagavan aṣṭau mahāgrahās tasya mahārājño rājaputrasya vā sarvadā sarvatra tathaiva sarvaṃ kariṣyāmaḥ / atha nakṣatrakṣaṇalavamuhūrtakaraṇatithiyogarāśilagnaviṣṭimaṇḍalādidevatās tathaiva namāsyaivam āhuḥ / vayam api bhagavan sarvadā tasya mahāsattvasyājñāṃ notsṛjāmaḥ / bhṛtyavat pratipālayāmaḥ / sarvanagaranigamajanapadarāṣṭrarājadhānīṃ ca pratipālayāmaḥ / utpanne tu mahābhaye yuṣmākaṃ pūjayiṣyati tasyāvaśyaṃ tad bhayaṃ na bhaviṣyati /
body.translated_text: Then those great planets, having bowed to the Blessed One, spoke thus: 'We, O Blessed One, the eight great planets, shall always and everywhere do exactly thus for that great king or prince.' Then the deities of the <s>nakṣatras</s> (lunar mansions), <s>kṣaṇas</s> (moments), <s>lavas</s> (instants), <s>muhūrtas</s> (hours), <s>karaṇas</s> (half-days), <s>tithis</s> (lunar days), <s>yogas</s> (astrological conjunctions), <s>rāśis</s> (zodiac signs), <s>lagnas</s> (ascendants), <s>viṣṭis</s>, and <s>maṇḍala</s> deities, likewise having bowed, spoke thus: 'We too, O Blessed One, shall never disobey the command of that great being. We shall attend to him like servants. We shall protect all cities, towns, districts, kingdoms, and capitals. And when a great danger arises, if he worships you, that danger shall surely not come to pass for him.'

body.text: athāṣṭau mahānāgāḥ phuṃkāradhvaninā bhagavantaṃ saṃtoṣyaivam āhuḥ /
body.translated_text: Then the eight great <s>Nāgas</s>, having delighted the Blessed One with the sound of '<s>phuṃ</s>,' spoke thus:
'We, O Blessed One, shall give our secret heart-[<s>mantras</s>] for all.'

body.text:
sādhu sādhu mahānāgā dadadhvaṃ hṛdayaṃ varam /
atha te tuṣṭā mahānāgā bhagavantaṃ namasyaivam āhuḥ /
body.translated_text: 'Well done, well done, O great <s>Nāgas</s>! Give [your] excellent heart-[<s>mantras</s>]!' Then those great <s>Nāgas</s>, delighted, having bowed to the Blessed One, spoke thus:

body.text:
oṃ phuḥ / oṃ phaḥ / oṃ phuṃ / oṃ phāṃ /
oṃ phīḥ / oṃ pheḥ / oṃ phaīḥ / oṃ phauḥ /
body.translated_text: <s>Oṃ phuḥ</s>! <s>Oṃ phaḥ</s>! <s>Oṃ phuṃ</s>! <s>Oṃ phāṃ</s>! <s>Oṃ phīḥ</s>! <s>Oṃ pheḥ</s>! <s>Oṃ phaīḥ</s>! <s>Oṃ phauḥ</s>!
Now, their <s>maṇḍala</s> is [as follows]:
One should draw a great lotus with eight petals, white in color.

body.text: tasya madhye likhed nāthaṃ vajrapāṇiṃ sukṛṣṇakam //
body.translated_text: In its center, one should draw the Lord <s>Vajrapāṇi</s>, very dark in color,

children.translated_text: All around, [as] the great serpent, threatening with seven hoods.

children.text: anantaṃ takṣakaṃ caiva karkoṭaṃ kulikaṃ tathā //
children.translated_text: <s>Ananta</s>, <s>Takṣaka</s>, <s>Karkoṭa</s>, and <s>Kulika</s>,

body.text: vāsukiṃ śaṃkhapālaṃ ca padmaṃ vai vāruṇaṃ tathā //
body.translated_text: <s>Vāsuki</s>, <s>Śaṅkhapāla</s>, <s>Padma</s>, and <s>Vāruṇa</s>.

body.text: ete lekhyāḥ samāsena patre patre phanajvalāḥ //
body.translated_text: These should be drawn, in brief, on each petal, with blazing hoods.
They should be drawn with seven hoods each, accompanied by their consorts, entwined at the neck.
Having set up eight water-vessels, adorned with <s>bali</s> (offering) and <s>naivedya</s> (food-offering),
With ghee, milk, and honey, and also artificial [substitutes] and additives.
Then, having entered [the <s>maṇḍala</s>], the <s>vajra</s>-self should attract [them] by hand with the hood [<s>mudrā</s>].

body.text: phuṃkārasahitais tu jaḥ huṃ vaṃ hoḥ pravartayet //
body.translated_text: With [the syllables] <s>jaḥ huṃ vaṃ hoḥ</s> accompanied by the '<s>phuṃ</s>' sound, one should set [the ritual] in motion.

body.text: tataḥ praveśya tān sarvān rājaṃ kṣatriyam eva vā / abhiṣiñcet phuṃkārair viṣadoṣamalāpahaiḥ /
body.translated_text: Then, having introduced them all, one should consecrate the king or <s>kṣatriya</s> with '<s>phuṃ</s>' sounds that remove the stains of poison and faults.

body.text: tataḥ sidhyanti sarve te nāgā nāmagrahād api //
body.translated_text: Then all those <s>Nāgas</s> are accomplished, even by the mere seizing of [their] names.

body.text: atha te samantaṃ tuṣṭā bhagavantaṃ namasya ca //
body.translated_text: Then they, delighted on all sides, having bowed to the Blessed One,
Make their vows, standing before [him] with palms joined.

body.text: vayaṃ bhagavataḥ śāsanābhiratasya yad idaṃ maṇḍalaṃ praviṣṭasya viṣaṃvādayāmaḥ / tadā bhagavantam eva viṣaṃvādayāmaḥ / tadāsmākaṃ taptavālukā bhaviṣyantu / ādīptena vajrenāsmākaṃ mūrdhni sphuṭiṣyanti / satataṃ samitaṃ ca tasya mahāsattvasya rakṣāvaraṇaguptiṃ kariṣyāmaḥ / mahaujobalavīryaṃ kṣepsyāmaḥ / nirviṣaṃ cāpi viṣaṃ kariṣyāmaḥ / kālena kālaṃ varṣayiṣyāmaḥ / sarvasasyāni niṣpādayiṣyāmaḥ / sarvapararāṣṭrāṇi ca vikālavṛṣṭim utsṛjāmaḥ / sarvabhayaṃ vināśayiṣyāmaḥ/ jinājñayā vajradharājñayā pratipālayiṣyāmaḥ /
body.translated_text: 'If we should deceive one who delights in the Blessed One's teaching and who has entered this <s>maṇḍala</s>, then we would be deceiving the Blessed One himself. Then may hot sand come upon us! May our heads be split by a blazing <s>vajra</s>! Constantly and always we shall provide protection, shielding, and guarding for that great being. We shall bestow great vigor, strength, and power. We shall render poison harmless. We shall send rain at the proper time. We shall bring all crops to fruition. And we shall release untimely rains upon all enemy kingdoms. We shall destroy all dangers. By the command of the <s>Jina</s> (Victor), by the command of the <s>Vajradhara</s> (Vajra-holder), we shall protect [him].'
Now the <s>sādhana</s> (practice) is [as follows]:

body.text: phuṃkāraṃ japel lakṣaṃ dhyātvā vajradharaṃ prabhum //
body.translated_text: One should recite the '<s>phuṃ</s>' syllable one hundred thousand times, having meditated upon the Lord <s>Vajradhara</s>,
Divine, garlanded with white rays, situated upon the hood at the crown.
Then, having taken the poison and meditated upon the <s>phuṃkāra-maṇḍala</s>,
One should visualize the divine '<s>phuṃ</s>' syllable there, surrounded by garlands of rays.
One should attract [the poison] with a hand shaped like a serpent-hood-noose, drawing it out.
With the wind of the '<s>phuṃ</s>' syllable, one should blow away all that poison,
That which has entered the skin, bones, and flesh.
Then one should perform all rites [against] poison, fever, toxic substances, and so forth.

body.text: muṣṭyā vai haret sarvaṃ kiṃ punaḥ phaṇamudrayeti //
body.translated_text: Even with a fist one can remove everything—how much more so with the hood-<s>mudrā</s>!

body.text: atha mahābhairavo mahādevādhipatir aṣṭabhir mahāmātṛkābhiḥ parivṛto bhagavantaṃ praṇipatyaivam āha / madbhayān mātṛkābhayāc ca bhagavan sarvadevanāgādayaḥ saṃtrastā vitrastāḥ pratrastā adhomukhībhūtā nimagnā naṣṭacetasaḥ paribhramanti tu teṣāṃ hitārthāya hṛdayaṃ pradāsyāmi / tat sādhu bhagavān adhitiṣṭhatu / sādhu sādhu mahābhairava subhairava bhāṣasva svahṛdayaṃ divyamātṛkāṇāṃ ca sarvāsām /
body.translated_text: Then <s>Mahābhairava</s>, the lord of <s>Mahādeva</s>, surrounded by the eight great <s>Mātṛkās</s> (Mother-goddesses), having prostrated to the Blessed One, spoke thus: 'Out of fear of me and fear of the <s>Mātṛkās</s>, O Blessed One, all the gods, <s>nāgas</s>, and others are terrified, frightened, alarmed, downcast, submerged, and wander about with minds lost. For their benefit I shall give [my] heart-[<s>mantra</s>]. May the Blessed One please consecrate it.' 'Well done, well done, O <s>Mahābhairava</s>, good <s>Bhairava</s>! Speak your heart-[<s>mantra</s>] and [those] of all the divine <s>Mātṛkās</s> as well.'

body.text: atha mahābhairavaḥ subhairavanādaṃ nadan evam āha /
body.translated_text: Then <s>Mahābhairava</s>, roaring with a mighty <s>Bhairava</s> sound, spoke thus:

body.text:
oṃ bhairavaiḥ bhīḥ svāhā /
oṃ bhāḥ svāhā / oṃ bhīḥ svāhā / oṃ bhūḥ svāhā / oṃ bheḥ svāhā /
oṃ bhaiḥ svāhā / oṃ bhoḥ svāhā / oṃ bhaṃ svāhā / oṃ bhaḥ svāhā /
body.translated_text: <s>Oṃ bhairavaiḥ bhīḥ svāhā</s>! <s>Oṃ bhāḥ svāhā</s>! <s>Oṃ bhīḥ svāhā</s>! <s>Oṃ bhūḥ svāhā</s>! <s>Oṃ bheḥ svāhā</s>! <s>Oṃ bhaiḥ svāhā</s>! <s>Oṃ bhoḥ svāhā</s>! <s>Oṃ bhaṃ svāhā</s>! <s>Oṃ bhaḥ svāhā</s>!

body.text:
ity ete bhagavan aṣṭau bhairavāḥ samājñākarāḥ /
athaiṣāṃ maṇḍalaṃ bhavati /
body.translated_text: 'These, O Blessed One, are the eight <s>Bhairavas</s>, obedient to command.' Now, their <s>maṇḍala</s> is [as follows]:
Having drawn a great wheel with eight spokes, one should place in the center
<s>Vajrapāṇi</s>, the great wrathful one, bearing the victory over the three worlds.
Beneath his feet, [draw] the wrathful great lord of the <s>Bhairavas</s>.
Having drawn [him] accompanied by <s>Bhairavī</s>, one should draw the others at will.
In the centers of all the spokes, one should draw the eight <s>Bhairavas</s>,
Accompanied by the <s>Mātṛkās</s>, with wrathful faces and furious minds.

body.text: dvāre dvāre tathaiveha likhed dvāriṃ sukrodhanam //
body.translated_text: At each gate likewise, one should draw a well-wrathful door-guardian.
Then, [having invoked] with the hook and other [<s>mudrās</s>], having worshipped with a skull-cup filled with blood,
Liquor, meat, divine <s>bali</s> (offering), a vessel filled with blood,
A skull-cup, a skull-fragment, and eight filled water-vessels—

body.text: rudhirair āsavair vāpi sthāpayet tasya maṇḍale //
body.translated_text: Filled with blood or liquor, one should place [them] in his <s>maṇḍala</s>.
Then, [the officiant], none other than <s>Trailokyavijaya</s> [himself], should introduce the disciples.
One should perform the <s>abhiṣeka</s> (consecration) with a skull-cup and also with the eight water-vessels.

children.translated_text: Then one should assign the [ritual] actions.
At a <s>Mātṛkā</s> shrine or at a solitary <s>liṅga</s>, the excellent <s>Trilokamathana</s> (Crusher of the Three Worlds) [practice]—

body.translated_text: Having performed worship according to the prescribed method, one should recite [the <s>mantra</s>] four hundred thousand times.
Then the sound of the great-souled <s>Bhairava</s> is heard.
Fearlessly, one should offer the <s>argha</s> (welcome-offering) with a skull-cup dyed deep red.

body.text: tataḥ paśyati taṃ kruddhaṃ bhairavaṃ duṣṭamānasam //
body.translated_text: Then one beholds that wrathful <s>Bhairava</s> with furious mind,
Filled with the host of <s>Mātṛkās</s>, surrounded by the eight <s>Bhairavas</s>.

body.text: taṃ dṛṣṭvā nirbhayo bhūtvā dadyād māṃsasupūritam //
body.translated_text: Having seen him, becoming fearless, one should offer [a skull-cup] well-filled with meat,
A skull-cup filled with liquor, while recollecting the syllable '<s>huṃ</s>.'
Then, pleased, <s>Bhairava</s> the destroyer of the wicked shall be accomplished.

body.text: brūyāt kim iccheti tad dadyāt tuṣṭamānasaḥ //
body.translated_text: He will say, 'What do you wish?' and, with a pleased mind, shall grant it.
Elixirs and alchemical substances, a sword, a <s>cakra</s> (discus), a trident,
[Sovereignty over] heaven, earth, and the underworld, kingship, and also the four continents,
The status of <s>Śakra</s> (Indra), lordship of <s>Yakṣas</s>, the state of a <s>Rākṣasa</s>, the state of a <s>Vidyādhara</s>,
Universal sovereignty among <s>Vidyādharas</s>, lordship over the three worlds—

children.translated_text: Except the gift of [<s>Bodhisattva</s>] stages—[all this he grants].

children.text: kiṃkaratvaṃ cāpi svayagaṇaṃ mātṛkāṃ vā dadāti //
children.translated_text: And he also gives servitude [of himself], his own retinue, or a <s>Mātṛkā</s>.

body.translated_text: One should request whichever <s>siddhi</s> (accomplishment) is desired.
Satisfied with the '<s>huṃ</s>' [offering], happy, having given [the boon], he departs laughing.
The frightened one he slays in an instant.

body.text: atha brahmādayo mahādevā bhagavantaṃ namasyaivam āhuḥ / vayam api bhagavata ājñayā svakalpaṃ bhāṣayāmaḥ / tad bhagavān kampām upādāyādhitiṣṭhatu / atha brahmādayo devāḥ svahṛdayam abhāṣanta /
body.translated_text: Then <s>Brahmā</s> and the other great gods, having bowed to the Blessed One, spoke thus: 'We too, by the command of the Blessed One, shall speak our own ritual procedures. May the Blessed One please accept and consecrate [them].' Then <s>Brahmā</s> and the other gods spoke their heart-[<s>mantras</s>]:

body.text: oṃ oṃ / oṃ viḥ / oṃ ruḥ / oṃ iḥ / oṃ kaḥ / oṃ gaḥ / oṃ bhṛḥ / oṃ kaḥ /
body.translated_text: <s>Oṃ oṃ</s>! <s>Oṃ viḥ</s>! <s>Oṃ ruḥ</s>! <s>Oṃ iḥ</s>! <s>Oṃ kaḥ</s>! <s>Oṃ gaḥ</s>! <s>Oṃ bhṛḥ</s>! <s>Oṃ kaḥ</s>!
Now, their <s>maṇḍala</s> is [as follows]:
One should draw the <s>maṇḍala</s> as before, with the <s>Trailokyasaṃgraha</s> (Compendium of the Three Worlds) in the center.
In front of it, one should draw the hero <s>Īśvara</s>, the trident-bearer.
Behind, one should draw <s>Brahmā</s>; to the left, the disc-bearer [<s>Viṣṇu</s>].
To the right, one should draw <s>Indra</s>, marked with the signs of his own <s>mudrā</s>.
The door-guardians likewise here, and their consorts in their own <s>maṇḍala</s>.
One should place <s>kalaśas</s> (ritual vessels) and full water-pots in the outer <s>maṇḍala</s>.
<s>Balabhadra</s>, blazing with great supernatural power.

body.text: tataḥ praviśya tān devān āhvayati vicakṣaṇaḥ //
body.translated_text: Then, having entered, the skilled one invokes those gods.

body.text: jaḥ huṃ vaṃ hoḥ surāḥ sarve praviśadhvaṃ purottame //
body.translated_text: Jaḥ huṃ vaṃ hoḥ—all gods, enter this excellent city!

body.text: atha tān tato drṣṭvā pūjayed mahāsukhaiḥ //
body.translated_text: Then, having seen them, one should worship [them] with great offerings of bliss.
Then one should cause the disciples to enter, with the <s>mudrā</s> of the <s>vajra</s>-holder.

body.text: oṃ pratīcchadhvaṃ mahāsattvā vajradharājñayā huṃ ha ha ha hoḥ /
body.translated_text: Oṃ, receive [this], great beings, by the command of <s>Vajradhara</s>! Huṃ ha ha ha hoḥ.

body.text: puṣpān prakṣipya yathāvac cakṣur udghāṭya darśayet //
body.translated_text: Having scattered flowers properly, one should open [the disciple's] eyes and show [the maṇḍala].
Then one should consecrate [the disciple] with water from the <s>kalaśa</s>, empowered by mantras.

body.text: tataḥ sarvaṃ pradadyāt tad devānāṃ tu yathepsitam //
body.translated_text: Then one should give everything as desired to the gods.

body.text: lakṣam ekaṃ dvilakṣaṃ vā kṛtvā sevāprarocitam //
body.translated_text: Having performed one hundred thousand or two hundred thousand [recitations], as the practice requires,
The <s>sādhaka</s> (practitioner) should accomplish [the worship of] those supreme gods headed by <s>Īśvara</s>.
At places such as a solitary <s>liṅga</s>, or [images of] <s>Vajrapāṇi</s>,
Or in a <s>Tathāgata</s> shrine, or at an excellent relic <s>caitya</s>,

body.text: sādhayet sādhako nityaṃ sarvadevān yathāvad iti //
body.translated_text: The <s>sādhaka</s> should constantly accomplish [the invocation of] all gods as prescribed.

body.text: ardharātre tato devā gatvā vedaya te dhruvam //
body.translated_text: Then at midnight the gods, having come, will surely declare to you:

body.text: īpsitaṃ tvayā kiṃ hitaṃ dāsyāmo yathāsukhaṃ //
body.translated_text: 'What is your desire? We shall give what is beneficial, as you please.'

body.text: vada bhadra drutaṃ cintya yena dāsyāmas te varam //
body.translated_text: 'Speak quickly, O blessed one, thinking of what boon we shall grant you.'

body.text: tato yācate mantrajño varasiddhiṃ tu devate //
body.translated_text: Then the <s>mantrajña</s> (knower of mantras) requests from the deity the supreme <s>siddhi</s> (attainment):
