body.text: rasarasāyanaṃ divyam antardhānaṃ tu khe gamam //
body.translated_text: Divine elixirs and <s>rasāyana</s> (rejuvenation), invisibility, and flight through the sky,
Pills, royal substances, and the like—one should request [these] for those who desire [them].

body.text: atha maheśvarādayo bhagavantaṃ praṇipatyaivam āhuḥ / ye bhagavan laukikalokottaramaṇḍale praviśanti teṣāṃ vayaṃ bhagavan sarvadevāḥ sarvāvaraṇāni viśodhayāmaḥ / svargamārgaṃ ca darśayāmaḥ / sugatimārgaṃ ca darśayāmaḥ / apāpamārgaṃ ca darśayāmaḥ / saddharmamārgaṃ ca darśayāmaḥ / anāmārgaṃ ca darśayāmaḥ / vivekamārgaṃ ca darśayāmaḥ / sāramārgaṃ ca darśayāmaḥ / nirvāṇamārgaṃ ca darśayāmaḥ / prahāṇamārgaṃ ca darśayāmaḥ / niḥkleśamārgaṃ ca darśayāmaḥ / buddhatvaṃ ca darśayāmaḥ / bodhisattvatvaṃ ca darśayāmaḥ / vajradharatvaṃ ca darśayāmaḥ / iti / sarvadā sarvabhayeṣu ca rakṣāvaraṇaguptim kariṣyāmaḥ / nagaranigamajanapadarājyarāṣṭrarājadhānīṃ ca rakṣayiṣyāmaḥ / viṣayadeśagrāmagoṣṭhaṃ ca rakṣayiṣyāmaḥ / rājyaṃ ca dāsyāmaḥ / prāptarājyasya rājavṛddhiṃ kariṣyāmaḥ / ekadvīpaṃ dvitīyaṃ tṛtīyaṃ caturthaṃ svargamartyapātālaṃ cakravartitvaṃ ca dāsyāmaḥ / saṃkṣepataḥ / śakratvaṃ brahmatvaṃ viṣṇutvaṃ maheśvaratvaṃ ca dāsyāma iti / atha bhagavān vajrapāṇiḥ punar api svaparṣanmaṇḍalam avalokya smitam akārṣīt / tataḥ pariṣanmaṇḍalaṃ pracalan saṃpracalan kṣubhan prakṣubhan saṃprakṣubhan jvalan prajvalan saṃprajvalan harṣan praharṣan saṃpraharṣan krīḍan prakrīḍan saṃprakrīḍan anekāny āścaryādbhutāni ca loke saṃpradṛśyante sma /
body.translated_text: Then <s>Maheśvara</s> and the others, having bowed to the <s>Bhagavān</s>, spoke thus: 'O <s>Bhagavān</s>, for those who enter the worldly and supramundane <s>maṇḍala</s>, we, all the gods, shall purify all their obscurations. We shall show them the path to heaven, the path to good destinies, the path free from sin, the path of the true <s>Dharma</s>, the path of non-attachment, the path of solitude, the path of essence, the path to <s>Nirvāṇa</s>, the path of abandonment, the path free from afflictions, the state of <s>Buddhahood</s>, the state of a <s>Bodhisattva</s>, and the state of <s>Vajradhara</s>. At all times and in all dangers, we shall provide protection, shelter, and guardianship. We shall protect cities, towns, districts, kingdoms, territories, and royal capitals. We shall protect countries, regions, villages, and cattle stations. We shall grant sovereignty. For one who has obtained kingship, we shall increase royal fortune. We shall grant rule over one continent, two, three, four, heaven, earth, and the underworld, and universal sovereignty. In brief, we shall grant the status of <s>Śakra</s>, <s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Viṣṇu</s>, and <s>Maheśvara</s>.' Then the <s>Bhagavān Vajrapāṇi</s> again surveyed his own assembly-<s>maṇḍala</s> and smiled. Thereupon the assembly-<s>maṇḍala</s> was shaking, greatly shaking, trembling, greatly trembling, intensely trembling, blazing, greatly blazing, intensely blazing, rejoicing, greatly rejoicing, intensely rejoicing, playing, greatly playing, intensely playing—and many wondrous and marvelous things appeared in the world.

body.text: atha brahmādayo devagaṇāḥ suvismayajātā bhagavantaṃ praṇipatyaivam āhuḥ / kim etad bhagavan smitasya kāraṇaṃ nākāraṇena buddhā bhagavanto bodhisattvā vā smitam utsṛjanti / tasmād bhagavān vyākarotu smitasya kāraṇam iti / atha bhagavān vajrapāṇir devānām adhyeṣaṇāvācam upaśrutyaivam āha / śrutaṃ brahmādayo devā yat puraḥ sarvabuddhaiś ca bhāṣitā mṛtyunāśanī vidyā vidyāmantramahātejā akālamṛtyunāśanī /
body.translated_text: Then <s>Brahmā</s> and the other hosts of gods, filled with great wonder, having bowed to the <s>Bhagavān</s>, spoke thus: 'What is this, O <s>Bhagavān</s>? What is the cause of this smile? Not without reason do <s>Buddhas</s>, <s>Bhagavāns</s>, or <s>Bodhisattvas</s> emit a smile. Therefore, may the <s>Bhagavān</s> explain the cause of this smile.' Then the <s>Bhagavān Vajrapāṇi</s>, having heard the request of the gods, spoke thus: 'Listen, <s>Brahmā</s> and the other gods! Previously, by all the <s>Buddhas</s> was proclaimed the <s>vidyā</s> (knowledge-spell) that destroys death—the great radiance of <s>vidyā-mantra</s>, destroyer of untimely death.'

body.text: atha bhagavantaṃ vajrapāṇiṃ praṇipatya te brahmādayo mahādevāḥ saṃhṛṣṭaromakūpajātāḥ / sādhukāraṃ prādaduḥ / sādhu sādhu bhagavan sādhu sādhu vajradhara / deśaya tu vidyāṃ mahātejāṃ mahābalaparākramāṃ yenālpāyuṣāḥ sattvā dīrgāyuṣā bhavanti / akālamṛtyugrastāś ca yenākālamaraṇād vimucyeran / apāyopapannāś ca sarvāpāyagatipathād vimucyeran / saṃsārabhayabhītāś ca sattvāḥ sukhopāyena saṃsāraparāṃmukhā bhavanti / āśur evānuttarasamyaksaṃbodhim abhisaṃbudhyanta iti / atha bhagavān vajrapāṇir brahmādīnāṃ devānām adhyeṣaṇāvacanam upaśrutyemāṃ sarvatathāgatahṛdayavidyāṃ svakāyavākcittavajrebhyo niścacāra /
body.translated_text: Then, having bowed to the <s>Bhagavān Vajrapāṇi</s>, <s>Brahmā</s> and the other great gods, their hair standing on end with delight, exclaimed: 'Excellent! Excellent, <s>Bhagavān</s>! Excellent, excellent, <s>Vajradhara</s>! Please teach the <s>vidyā</s> of great radiance and great powerful might, by which beings of short lifespan become long-lived, and those seized by untimely death may be freed from untimely dying, and those reborn in evil destinies may be freed from all paths of evil destiny, and beings frightened by the fear of <s>saṃsāra</s> may easily turn away from <s>saṃsāra</s> and swiftly attain <s>anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi</s> (supreme perfect enlightenment).' Then the <s>Bhagavān Vajrapāṇi</s>, having heard the entreaty of <s>Brahmā</s> and the other gods, issued from his own body, speech, and mind-<s>vajras</s> this <s>sarvatathāgata-hṛdaya-vidyā</s> (heart-knowledge of all Tathāgatas):

body.text: oṃ puṇye puṇye mahāpuṇye 'parimitāyuḥpuṇye jñānasaṃbhāropacite svāhā / hṛdayavidyā /
body.translated_text: Oṃ puṇye puṇye mahāpuṇye aparimitāyuḥpuṇye jñānasaṃbhāropacite svāhā. The <s>hṛdaya-vidyā</s> (heart-knowledge).

body.text:
oṃ hrīḥ svāhā / upahṛdayavidyā /
oṃ bhrūṃ svāhā / hṛdayopahṛdayavidyā /
oṃ kruṃ svāhā / hṛdayasaṃcodanīvidyā /
oṃ trāṃ svāhā / hṛdayottarā /
oṃ haṃ svāhā / guhyahṛdayā /
body.translated_text: Oṃ hrīḥ svāhā—the <s>upahṛdaya-vidyā</s> (secondary heart-knowledge). Oṃ bhrūṃ svāhā—the <s>hṛdayopahṛdaya-vidyā</s> (heart-and-secondary-heart knowledge). Oṃ kruṃ svāhā—the <s>hṛdaya-saṃcodanī-vidyā</s> (heart-activating knowledge). Oṃ trāṃ svāhā—the <s>hṛdayottarā</s> (supplementary heart-knowledge). Oṃ haṃ svāhā—the <s>guhya-hṛdayā</s> (secret heart-knowledge).
Now, the <s>maṇḍala</s> for these [deities] is as follows:

body.text: maṇḍalaṃ caturāraṃ kṛtvā madhye niveśayed aparimitāyuḥpuṇyajñānasaṃbhāratejorājaṃ nāma tathāgatam / bhrūṃkārahṛdayam/ tasyāgrato vajrapāṇim / hrīṃkārahṛdayaṃ / vāmataḥ krodham / kruṃkārahṛdayam / dakṣiṇenākāśagarbham / trāṃkārahṛdayam/ pṛṣṭhato 'bhayaṃdadaṃ nāmāryāvalokiteśvaram / haṃkārahṛdayaṃ /
body.translated_text: Having made a four-spoked <s>maṇḍala</s>, one should place in the center the <s>Tathāgata</s> named <s>Aparimitāyuḥpuṇyajñānasaṃbhāratejarāja</s> (King of the Radiance of Immeasurable Life, Merit, and Wisdom), with BHRŪṂ as his heart-syllable. In front of him, <s>Vajrapāṇi</s>, with HRĪṂ as his heart-syllable. To the left, <s>Krodha</s> (the Wrathful One), with KRUṂ as his heart-syllable. To the right, <s>Ākāśagarbha</s>, with TRĀṂ as his heart-syllable. Behind, the noble <s>Avalokiteśvara</s> named <s>Abhayaṃdada</s> (Giver of Fearlessness), with HAṂ as his heart-syllable.

body.text: tathāgatasya prabhāmaṇḍale vidyā lekhyāḥ / pañcāṣṭau kalaśāḥ sthāpyāś cakravartyabhimantritāḥ / sarvakarmikakrodhenābhimantritās ca dhūpādikaṃ sthāpayet pūjādikaṃ sarvadvārapālān eva ca /
body.translated_text: The <s>vidyās</s> should be written in the radiance-halo of the <s>Tathāgata</s>. Five or eight <s>kalaśas</s> should be placed, consecrated with the <s>cakravartī</s> [mantra]. Empowered by the <s>sarvakarmika-krodha</s> (wrathful deity of all activities), one should place incense and other [offerings], arrange the worship, and [install] all door-guardians.

body.text: tataḥ saṃpraviśya svayaṃ mantrī / ākarṣayet sugatottamaṃ saputrabhṛtyasaṃghaiś ca vṛtaṃ vidyayā saha / vidyā ca sugatavāmapārśve lekhyā / tataś cātmānam abhiṣiñcya paryaṃkena niṣadya śatasahasraṃ japet / tathāgataṃ saṃmukhaṃ paśyati vajradharāryāvalokiteśvaraṃ vā / yathepsitaṃ varaṃ pratilabhate / yadā samāhitas tadā manasā sarvakarmasamartho bhavati / tataḥ śiṣyān praveśayed vajradharamudrayā / ityabhimānam utpādayet /
body.translated_text: Then the <s>mantrī</s> (ritualist) himself enters. He should attract the supreme <s>Sugata</s> (Buddha), surrounded by his retinue of sons and attendants, together with the <s>vidyā</s>. The <s>vidyā</s> should be written on the left side of the <s>Sugata</s>. Then, having consecrated oneself, one should sit cross-legged and recite one hundred thousand [times]. One will see the <s>Tathāgata</s> face to face, or <s>Vajradhara</s>, or the noble <s>Avalokiteśvara</s>. One obtains whatever boon is desired. When absorbed [in samādhi], one becomes capable of all acts by means of the mind. Then one should cause the disciples to enter with the <s>Vajradhara-mudrā</s>. One should generate this conviction:

body.text: oṃ vajradhara ratnadhara padmadhara viśvadhara tathāgatasamayātikrama tathāgatasamayadhārako 'ham /
body.translated_text: Oṃ, O bearer of the <s>vajra</s>, bearer of the jewel, bearer of the lotus, bearer of the <s>viśva</s> [vajra]—I am the keeper of the <s>Tathāgata-samaya</s> (pledge), having crossed beyond the <s>Tathāgata-samaya</s>.

body.text: tato 'nena kṣepayet puṣpān / oṃ sarvatathāgata pratīccha hoḥ samayas tvaṃ / tatas tayā mālayāveṣṭayābhiṣiñcayet / oṃ sarvatathāgatābhiṣiñca vajradharājñāpaya huṃ bhrūṃ / oṃ vajravajrābhiṣiñca huṃ huṃ / oṃ vajraratnābhiṣiñca huṃ trāṃ / oṃ vajrapadmābhiṣiñca huṃ hrīḥ / oṃ karmaviśvābhiṣiñca aḥ huṃ kaṃ /
body.translated_text: Then with this [mantra] one should cast flowers: Oṃ, all <s>Tathāgatas</s>, receive! Hoḥ, you are the pledge. Then, having wrapped with that garland, one should consecrate [the disciple]: Oṃ, all <s>Tathāgatas</s>, consecrate! O <s>Vajradhara</s>, command! Huṃ bhrūṃ. Oṃ vajra-vajra, consecrate! Huṃ huṃ. Oṃ vajra-ratna, consecrate! Huṃ trāṃ. Oṃ vajra-padma, consecrate! Huṃ hrīḥ. Oṃ karma-viśva, consecrate! Aḥ huṃ kaṃ.

body.text: tataḥ samayaṃ dadyād ājñābhiṣekaṃ ca / tatra samayaṃ /
body.translated_text: Then one should give the <s>samaya</s> (pledge) and the <s>ājñābhiṣeka</s> (command-consecration). The <s>samaya</s> is as follows:

body.text: triratnaṃ na parityājaṃ bodhicittañ ca sadgurum //
body.translated_text: One shall not abandon the Three Jewels, the <s>bodhicitta</s> (mind of enlightenment), or the true teacher.

body.text: prāṇinaś ca na saṃghātyā adattaṃ naiva cāharet //
body.translated_text: One shall not kill living beings, nor take what is not given.

body.text: mṛṣā naiva ca bhāṣeta nācaret tatparastriyaṃ //
body.translated_text: One shall not speak falsely, nor engage with another's wife.

body.text: gurunindā na saṃkāryā nāpi chāyāṃ tu laṃghayet //
body.translated_text: One shall not slander the teacher, nor step over [the teacher's] shadow.
One shall not accept those who lack a teacher; one shall not [disrespect] the name of the <s>vajra</s>-master.

body.text: mantramudrā na nindeta devatāṃ cāpi kadācana //
body.translated_text: One shall not disparage <s>mantras</s>, <s>mudrās</s>, or deities—ever.

body.text: ninded yadi mohātmā mriyate vyādhibhir dhruvam //
body.translated_text: If a deluded person disparages, they will surely die from diseases.
Offered remnants, deity-shadows, <s>mudrās</s>, and syllable-emblems,
Whether worldly or supramundane—one shall not trample with the feet.
Those who harm the Three Jewels and the like, those deluded regarding the <s>Buddha</s>'s teaching,
Those who delight in slandering the teacher—the skilled one should diligently destroy [their negativity].
Those who are unrighteous, addicted to sin, and constantly hostile to beings—
The <s>mantrī</s> should slay out of compassion, with mantras, those who are enemies of the <s>samaya</s>.

body.text: kṛpaṇārthaṃ ca saṃgṛhya dadyāt sattve suduḥkhite //
body.translated_text: One should gather [wealth] for the sake of the poor and give to beings in great suffering.
For the purpose of <s>guru-pūjā</s> (worship of the teacher), and likewise in the practice of the <s>samaya</s>,

body.text: maṇḍalārthe hared arthaṃ kṛpaṇārthaṃ cāpi cintitam //
body.translated_text: One should take wealth for the sake of the <s>maṇḍala</s>, and also as intended for the poor.
For the benefit of <s>samayins</s> (pledge-holders) and for worship of the sons of the <s>Jinas</s> (Conquerors),
For the sake of protection, one may speak falsely, devoted to the welfare of beings.
The <s>samaya</s>-teacher's substances, and life-force among living beings at all times,
For the purpose of arousing desire [in service] of the <s>Buddhas</s>, and for guarding the <s>samaya</s>,
The <s>mantravit</s> (knower of mantras) should resort to others' wives for the purpose of <s>sādhana</s> (accomplishment).

body.text: sarvakṛt sarvabhug vā kiṃ vajrasattvapade sthitaḥ //
body.translated_text: What of being the doer of all and enjoyer of all, established in the state of <s>Vajrasattva</s>?

body.text: sidhyate naiva duṣyeta kiṃ punaḥ kṛpayānvitaḥ // iti /
body.translated_text: One attains accomplishment and is not defiled—how much more so one endowed with compassion!

body.text:
tato 'nena kiṃ me abhiṣekaṃ dadyāt /
oṃ sarvatathāgatājñāṃ te dāsyāmi gṛhṇa vajrasusiddhaye /
oṃ vajra tiṣṭha huṃ /
body.translated_text: Then with this [mantra], what consecration should one give? Oṃ, I shall give you the command of all <s>Tathāgatas</s>—receive it, for the perfect accomplishment of the <s>vajra</s>! Oṃ vajra, stand firm! Huṃ.

body.text: anena vajraṃ haste datvā karmābhiṣekaṃ dadyāt //
body.translated_text: With this, having placed the <s>vajra</s> in [the disciple's] hand, one should give the <s>karmābhiṣeka</s> (action-consecration).
Oṃ, perform all actions of the <s>Buddhas</s>! Huṃ.

body.text: tato gurugauravaṃ tena dātavyaṃ deham uttamam //
body.translated_text: Then, as <s>guru-gaurava</s> (reverence for the teacher), the disciple should offer the supreme body,

body.text: dravyaṃ dhanadhānyaṃ ca āsanaṃ yānam eva ca //
body.translated_text: Wealth, grain, a seat, and a vehicle,

body.text: varabhṛtyapuraṃ caiva rājyam aiśvaryam eva ca //
body.translated_text: An excellent servant, a city, sovereignty and dominion,
Sons, daughters, and spouse, mother, sister, and sister-in-law,

body.text: anyān apīpsitāṃs sarvān guror deyān hitāśayaḥ //
body.translated_text: And all other desired things—one with benevolent intent should give [these] to the <s>guru</s>.

body.text: tataḥ siddhiṃ tu prārthayed buddhānāṃ bodhisādhikām //
body.translated_text: Then one should pray for the <s>siddhi</s> that accomplishes <s>bodhi</s> of the <s>Buddhas</s>,
And also for whatever worldly prosperities are desired.

body.text: tato dadyād dhitārthāya siddhiṃ putrasya mantravit //
body.translated_text: Then the <s>mantravit</s> should grant the <s>siddhi</s> to the disciple for his benefit,
With a mind free from jealousy, with faith and faithful heart.

body.text: niḥsvabhāvaṃ tu dharmāṇāṃ bhāvayitvā tu cetasā //
body.translated_text: Having contemplated the essencelessness of all <s>dharmas</s> in the mind,
Visualize a moon-disc with the syllable A, and in its center one's own seed-syllable.

body.text: dhyātvā samayamudrāṃ tu cintayet tam eva ca //
body.translated_text: Having meditated, one should contemplate the <s>samaya-mudrā</s> and that very [deity].
That very [seed-syllable] transforms through the yoga of the deity's form.

body.text: tato 'dhitiṣṭhet tāṃ mudrāṃ svabijena tu mudrayā //
body.translated_text: Then one should consecrate that <s>mudrā</s> with one's own seed-syllable seal.
One should be consecrated by the <s>Buddhas</s>, properly and in sequence.
Then, having generated conviction, the skilled one should practice.

body.text: siddhiṃ tathāgatiṃ cāpi kiṃ punaś cānyasiddhayaḥ //
body.translated_text: The <s>siddhi</s> of <s>tathāgata</s>-hood [is attained]—how much more so other <s>siddhis</s>!

body.text: atha bhagavantaṃ praṇipatya brahmādayo mahādevā evam āhuḥ / kiṃ bhagavan tasya rājaputrasya rājāmātyasya kṣatriyasya brāhmaṇasya vaiśyasya śūdrasyānyasya vā hīnajaghanasya pratyantikajanapadakulajātyasyāsya maṇḍalarājapraviṣṭasya vipākaṃ bhavati /
body.translated_text: Then, having bowed to the <s>Bhagavān</s>, <s>Brahmā</s> and the other great gods spoke thus: 'O <s>Bhagavān</s>, what is the fruit of ripening for that prince, royal minister, <s>kṣatriya</s>, <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, <s>vaiśya</s>, <s>śūdra</s>, or other person of low, inferior, or borderland birth who has entered this King of <s>Maṇḍalas</s>?'

body.text: bhagavān āha / sādhu sādhu mahābrahmādayo devagaṇā yan mamedam anāgatānāṃ sattvānāṃ hitāya paripraṣṭavanta iti / śṛṇuta devagaṇasya maṇḍalarājapraviṣṭasyābhiṣiktasya likhitasya likhāpayitasyānumoditasya vanditasya pūjitasya phalavipākaṃ ceti / aham api devaputrāḥ saṃkṣepato notsāhāmi / anuśaṃsā vaktuṃ yan mama puṇyasaṃbhāraṃ tam anekaśatasahasraguṇitaṃ kṛtvā saṃkhyām api gaṇanām apy upamām api na kṣamate / yāvat sarvatathāgatānām api puṇyaskandhaṃ na kṣamate / iti /
body.translated_text: The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'Well done, well done, great <s>Brahmā</s> and hosts of gods, that you have asked me this for the benefit of future beings! Listen, hosts of gods: the fruit of ripening for one who has entered the King of <s>Maṇḍalas</s>, been consecrated, drawn or caused to be drawn [the maṇḍala], rejoiced, venerated, and worshiped—even I, O divine sons, am unable to state it in brief. The merit that I describe, multiplied a hundred thousand times, surpasses all counting, calculation, and comparison. It surpasses even the mass of merit of all the <s>Tathāgatas</s>.'

body.text: āścaryaṃ bhagavan āścaryaṃ vajradhara yad evaṃ maṇḍalapraviṣṭānāṃ sattvānāṃ phalavipākam iti / utsāhāmo vayaṃ bhagavan utsāhāmo bhagavan vajradhara maṇḍalādipraveśam /
body.translated_text: 'Wonderful, <s>Bhagavān</s>! Wonderful, <s>Vajradhara</s>! Such is the fruition of result for beings who have entered the <s>maṇḍala</s>!' 'We are eager, <s>Bhagavān</s>! We are eager, <s>Bhagavān</s> <s>Vajradhara</s>, for the initial entry into the <s>maṇḍala</s>!'

body.text: atha te devās tathaiva namasyaivam āhuḥ / santi bhagavan sattvā jambudvīpakā alpāyuṣo mandapuṇyā apāyagatikā narakapretatiryakpratyupapannā vā tesāṃ kathaṃ vayaṃ bhagavan pratipatsyāmaḥ /
body.translated_text: Then those gods, bowing likewise, spoke thus: 'There are, <s>Bhagavān</s>, beings in <s>Jambudvīpa</s> who are of short lifespan, scanty merit, destined for evil births — or already reborn as hell-beings, hungry ghosts, or animals. How, <s>Bhagavān</s>, should we act toward them?'

body.text: teṣāṃ bho devaputrā ihaiva maṇḍale praveśayadhvaṃ / praveśya cābhiṣiñcayadhvam / dharmatākṣaraṃ ca japayadhvam / tena te sattvā dīrghāyuṣkā bhavanti / puṇyahīnāḥ puṇyavanto bhavanti / apāyād vinirmuktā bhavanti / ye cāpāyotpannās teṣāṃ bho devaputrā nāmābhiṣekaṃ kuruta / pratibimbābhiṣekaṃ kuruta / stūpābhiṣekaṃ kuruta / svadevatākāyābhiṣekaṃ kuruta / antaśas tajjanyaṃ tatputraṃ tadgotraṃ tannāmadhārakaṃ vā bhṛtyaṃ vābhiṣiñcadhvaṃ saptarātradivasya saptabhir maṇḍale praveśyābhiṣekair vimucyata apāyāvaraṇāt / tannāmakenāpi devaputrā japadhvaṃ dvilakṣaṃ trilakṣaṃ catullakṣaṃ yāval lakṣaśatasahasraṃ pañcānantaryakāriṇo 'pi vimucyante / kiṃ puṇaḥ svalpapāpakāriṇa iti /
body.translated_text: 'O sons of the gods, introduce them right here into the <s>maṇḍala</s>. Having introduced them, consecrate them. And recite the <s>dharmatākṣara</s> (syllable of the Dharma). By that, those beings become long-lived. Those devoid of merit become meritorious. They become liberated from evil destinies. And for those born in evil destinies, O sons of the gods, perform the name-consecration (<s>nāmābhiṣeka</s>). Perform the image-consecration (<s>pratibimbābhiṣeka</s>). Perform the <s>stūpa</s>-consecration. Perform the consecration of one's own deity-body (<s>svadevatākāyābhiṣeka</s>). At the very least, consecrate one born of the same [clan], a son, one of the same lineage, one bearing the same name, or even a servant. Through seven consecrations [over] seven nights and days, having been introduced into the <s>maṇḍala</s>, [they are] liberated from the obstruction of evil destinies. O sons of the gods, recite even by the name alone: two hundred thousand, three hundred thousand, four hundred thousand, up to a hundred billion — even those who have committed the five heinous sins (<s>pañcānantarya</s>) are liberated. How much more so those who have committed minor sins!'

body.text: hastamātraṃ devaputrā vartulaṃ dvihastaṃ vā śāntikaṃ kuṇḍaṃ kṛtvā hīnotkṛṣṭamadhyamaṃ tannāmnā śvetasarṣapānāṃ śatasahasraṃ juhuyāt / sarvāpāyād vimucyate / tanmāṃsāsthikeśabhasmādikaṃ vā tenaiva vidhānena juhuyāt / sarvapāpād vimucyate /
body.translated_text: 'O sons of the gods, having made a round pacification fire-pit (<s>kuṇḍa</s>) one cubit or two cubits [in size] — of inferior, middling, or superior [grade] — one should offer a hundred thousand white mustard seeds with that [being's] name. [That being] is liberated from all evil destinies. Or one should offer the flesh, bones, hair, ashes, and the like of that [being] by that very method. [That being] is liberated from all sin.'
In the center, one should draw a wheel with eight white-flaming spokes.
All around, one should draw a <s>vajra</s>, a five-pronged [trident] with white rays.
Then one should make a <s>viśvavajra</s> (crossed vajra), with <s>vajra</s>, jewel, and supreme lotus.
Then one should make various <s>mudrās</s> (ritual gestures) for the destruction of sin.
For the outer <s>vajra</s>-families, one should draw the <s>mudrās</s> on the outside.
Planetary and stellar signs, and also the world-guardians.

body.text: paṭapratimāṃ tu nāthasya sthāpayed vajriṇā saha //
body.translated_text: One should set up a painted image of the Lord together with the <s>Vajrin</s> (Vajra-holder).
Ritual water-pots (<s>kalaśa</s>), full pitchers (<s>pūrṇakumbha</s>), and white offerings and food-offerings (<s>bali</s> and <s>naivedya</s>).
Having strung [the ritual threads] in brief, and having drawn [the maṇḍala] according to the proper methods,
wearing white garments, in the form of a Buddha, confident,
and recollecting that being situated in the evil destinies,
one of purified continuum should perform the fire offering (<s>homa</s>) for the pacification of obstructions caused by sin,
with ghee, milk, honey, and parched grain mixed with mustard seeds,
and the bones, flesh, and the like of that [being], or even with just the name alone. Thus.

body.text: utpādya sugatau tasya puṣṭiṃ kuryād vicakṣaṇaḥ //
body.translated_text: Having generated [faith] in the <s>Sugata</s> (Well-Gone One), the discerning one should perform the prosperity rite (<s>puṣṭi</s>) for that [being].
Two cubits, or four cubits, or eight cubits as the best —
having made a square fire-pit (<s>kuṇḍa</s>) equipped with platforms (<s>vedikā</s>) on all sides,

body.text: tasya madhye ratnapadmaṃ tu likhet pītaraśminam //
body.translated_text: in the middle, one should draw a jewel-lotus with yellow rays.

body.text: samantāl likhed ratnaṃ vedikāyāṃ tu aṃbujaṃ //
body.translated_text: All around, one should draw jewels, and on the platform, lotuses.
With the five-fold family division, one should draw <s>mudrās</s> on the outside.
Likewise for the outer deities, one should draw the hook (<s>aṅkuśa</s>) and other [implements].
Having put on yellow garments, recollecting [the being] situated in a good destiny,
one should perform the prosperity rite (<s>pauṣṭikakarma</s>) for the purpose of prosperity, for that [being's] benefit.
One should increase the lifespan, glory, beauty, and good fortune of that embodied being.

body.text: tataḥ kuryād vaśyaṃ tu tasya karma hitāya //
body.translated_text: Then one should perform the subjugation rite (<s>vaśya</s>) for the benefit of that [being].

body.text: dvihastaṃ caturhastaṃ tu kṛtvā kuṇḍaṃ dhanurākṛtim //
body.translated_text: Two cubits or four cubits — having made a bow-shaped fire-pit (<s>kuṇḍa</s>),

body.text: hastaṃ vā tasya madhye tu saṃlikhya raktam ambujam //
body.translated_text: or [one] cubit; in the middle, one should draw a red lotus.

body.text: tasyopari ca saṃlikhet saśaraṃ dhanur eva ca //
body.translated_text: On top of it, one should draw a bow with an arrow.

body.text: samantāc ca likhec cāpaṃ saśaraṃ raktavarṇakam //
body.translated_text: All around, one should draw a bow with an arrow, red in color.

body.text: bāhyatas tadvad evāsya kuryād mantrabhūtaḥ sadā //
body.translated_text: On the outside, likewise for this [ritual], one who has become [one with the] <s>mantra</s> should always [perform],
recollecting that being, adorned with red garments,
[offering] red flowers, red lotuses, or red fruits with essences.
For that [being], the gods and others [come under control] — with ghee mixed with saffron,
and with red sandalwood powder — all remain under his control.
For the destruction of that [being's] enemies, one should commence the destructive rite (<s>abhicāra</s>).
Two and a half cubits, or three cubits, or nine cubits as the best —
having made [the pit] with triple corners, with a nine-fold <s>vajra</s> in the center,

body.text: trisūcikair vṛtāṃ vedīṃ kṛtvā viśvaiś ca vajribhiḥ //
body.translated_text: having made the platform surrounded by tri-pronged [implements] and with universal <s>vajra</s>-holders,
marked with staffs, skulls, tridents, <s>vajra</s>-axes, and needles,

body.text: kārayed bāhyato cāpi tripuṭaṃ pūrvavac citram //
body.translated_text: and on the outside too, one should make a triple-fold [enclosure], variegated as before.

body.text: kalaśān balikumbhāṃś ca naivedyān sthāpayed bahu //
body.translated_text: Ritual water-pots, offering-pots, and many food-offerings should be set up.
Skull-cups filled with flesh and blood on all sides.
Wearing black garments, wrathful, [as] the Conqueror of the Three Worlds (<s>Trailokyavijayī</s>) himself,
one should destroy all sins, obstacles, and the like for that embodied being.
Then that one, whose sinful self has been destroyed, wanders happily, free from obstacles,
in the heavenly realms, in the human world, throughout the three world-realms.
By this very method, one should swiftly [perform rites] for those situated in this [present] birth.

body.text: tatas tathaiva syāt teṣāṃ yeṣām uddiśya kāryate //
body.translated_text: Then it shall likewise come to pass for those for whose sake it is performed.

body.text: anyāny api karmāṇi yathā pūrvaṃ tathā kuryāt //
body.translated_text: Other rituals too should be performed as before.

body.text: tena saṃpadyate kṣipraṃ sattvānāṃ ca sukhāvaham //
body.translated_text: By that, it quickly comes about, bringing happiness to beings.

body.text: atha brahmādayo devāḥ saṃhṛṣṭamanaso bhagavantaṃ namasyaivam āhuḥ / yo bhagavan apāyopapannānāṃ sattvānām arthāya hitāya sukhāya / etaṃ kalparājaṃ likhiṣyati likhāpayiṣyati / kiṃ punar yathānirdiṣṭam avikalpayataḥ kariṣyati / vayaṃ brahmāddayo devās tasya kulaputrasya kuladuhitur vā bhṛtyavat paripālayiṣyāmaḥ / yaś ca rājaiva rājaputro vā rājāmātyo vā yathāpaṭhituṃ mantraṃ vartayiṣyati tasya rājavṛddhiṃ kariṣyāmaḥ / viṣayadeśāṃś ca janaparivārajanasasyādirakṣāṃ ca kariṣyāmaḥ / bahudhanadhānyasamṛddhiṃ kariṣyāmaḥ / strīpuruṣadārakadārikāsaṃpadaṃ ca kariṣyāmaḥ / ṛddhiṃ ca sphītaṃ ca subhikṣaṃ ca kṣemaṃ ca kariṣyāmaḥ / yaś cedaṃ kalparājaṃ śrāddho dhvajāgrāvaropitaṃ kṛtvā nagaranigamādisu praveśayet svayaṃ vā pratyudgacched dhastiskandhāvaropitaṃ ca kṛtvā sarvagrāmanagarādikaṃ bhrāmayet / sarvamṛtyūpadravaṃ ca naśyati / tasya mahāsattvasya padaṃ jñāsyāmo bhṛtyatvena putratvena vā / yatra pāpaṃ pracariṣyati tatra bhagavān vajrapāṇiḥ svayam eva saṃbhogikaiḥ kāyair vajrasattvarūpeṇa vyavasthita iti manyāmaḥ / sa eva bhagavān vajrasattvaḥ samantabhadraḥ sarvāśāparipūrakaḥ kalparājarūpeṇa viharatīti manyāmaḥ / sarvatathāgatāś ca saparivārā viharanta iti manyāmaḥ / taṃ ca pṛthivīpradeśaṃ caityabhūtaṃ manyāmaḥ / pūjayāmo vandayāmaḥ / ārakṣiṣyāmaḥ / yaś cainaṃ kalparājaṃ pracariṣyati vajrācāryamahātapā tasya vayaṃ brahmādayo devā bhṛtyā bhavāmaḥ / ceṭatvenopatiṣṭhāmaḥ / kiṃkaratvenopatiṣṭhāmaḥ / sarvājñātve kariṣyāmaḥ / sarvahitaṃ sukhaṃ ca kariṣyāmaḥ / sarvasiddhiṃ ca prayacchāmaḥ / saṃkṣepataś ca bhagavan tasya pādarajāṃsi śirasā dhārayāmaḥ /
body.translated_text: Then <s>Brahmā</s> and the other gods, with joyful minds, having bowed to the <s>Bhagavān</s>, spoke thus: 'Whoever, <s>Bhagavān</s>, for the benefit, welfare, and happiness of beings born in evil destinies, will write or cause to be written this Ritual King (<s>kalparāja</s>) — how much more so whoever will perform it without distortion, as instructed — we, <s>Brahmā</s> and the other gods, shall protect that son or daughter of good family like servants. And whoever — whether king, prince, or royal minister — will practice the <s>mantra</s> as taught, we shall bring about the increase of his kingdom. We shall protect the territories, regions, populace, retinue, people, crops, and the like. We shall bring about prosperity of abundant wealth and grain. We shall bring about the prosperity of women, men, boys, and girls. We shall bring about prosperity, abundance, good harvest, and security. And whoever, with faith, having mounted this Ritual King on the top of a banner, would bring it into cities, towns, and the like, or would go forth to meet it himself, and having mounted it on the shoulders of an elephant, would parade it through all villages, cities, and the like — all dangers of death shall perish. We shall know the whereabouts of that great being, as servants or as sons. Wherever sin spreads, there the <s>Bhagavān</s> <s>Vajrapāṇi</s> himself, in his enjoyment-bodies, is established in the form of <s>Vajrasattva</s> — thus we regard. That very <s>Bhagavān</s> <s>Vajrasattva</s>, <s>Samantabhadra</s>, the fulfiller of all hopes, abides in the form of the Ritual King — thus we regard. And all <s>Tathāgatas</s> with their retinues abide [therein] — thus we regard. And that place on earth we regard as a sacred shrine (<s>caitya</s>). We worship, we venerate, we shall guard it. And whoever shall propagate this Ritual King — that <s>vajrācārya</s> (vajra-master) of great austerity — we, <s>Brahmā</s> and the other gods, shall become his servants. We shall serve as attendants. We shall serve as helpers. We shall carry out all commands. We shall bring about all welfare and happiness. We shall grant all accomplishments (<s>siddhi</s>). And in brief, <s>Bhagavān</s>, we shall bear the dust of his feet upon our heads.'

body.text: vandayāmo bhagavan pūjayāmo bhagavan tasya pṛṣṭhataś cānugacchāmaḥ / ye bhagavan sattvā maṇḍale 'bhiṣiktās te 'smākaṃ prabhur iti manyāmaḥ / vajrapāṇir iti manyāmaḥ / vajrasattva iti manyāmaḥ / mahāsukhasamantabhadra iti manyāmaḥ / tathāgataś ceti manyāmaḥ /
body.translated_text: 'We venerate [him], <s>Bhagavān</s>; we worship [him], <s>Bhagavān</s>; and we shall follow behind him. Those beings, <s>Bhagavān</s>, who are consecrated (<s>abhiṣikta</s>) in the <s>maṇḍala</s> — we regard them as our lords. We regard them as <s>Vajrapāṇi</s>. We regard them as <s>Vajrasattva</s>. We regard them as <s>Mahāsukha Samantabhadra</s> (Great Bliss, the All-Good). And we regard them as <s>Tathāgatas</s>.'

body.text: atha bhagavān vajrapāṇis tān brahmādīn devān evāha / sādhu sādhu brahmādayo devā yena dharmagauraveṇaiva bhūtāṃ pratijñāṃ kurvatas tat sādhu pratipadyadhvam iti /
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bhagavān</s> <s>Vajrapāṇi</s> spoke thus to those gods headed by <s>Brahmā</s>: 'Excellent, excellent, O gods headed by <s>Brahmā</s>! Since with such reverence for the <s>Dharma</s> you make a true pledge — carry it out well!'

body.text:
III
atha bhagavān vajrapāṇiḥ sarvamantravidyāhṛdayadṛḍhīkaraṇārthaṃ svahṛdayam abhāṣata /
body.translated_text:
III.
Then the <s>Bhagavān</s> <s>Vajrapāṇi</s>, for the purpose of strengthening the heart[-<s>dhāraṇī</s>] of all <s>mantras</s> and <s>vidyās</s>, uttered his own heart [<s>mantra</s>]:

body.text:
oṃ bhrūṃ trūṃ vajrapāṇi dṛdhaṃ tiṣṭha huṃ / oṃ huṃ /
oṃ vajra huṃ phat / oṃ dṛḍhavajra huṃ / oṃ vajra huṃ saḥ /
oṃ vajra huṃ sraḥ /
body.translated_text:
<s>Oṃ bhrūṃ trūṃ vajrapāṇi dṛḍhaṃ tiṣṭha huṃ</s>. <s>Oṃ huṃ</s>.
<s>Oṃ vajra huṃ phaṭ</s>. <s>Oṃ dṛḍhavajra huṃ</s>. <s>Oṃ vajra huṃ saḥ</s>.
<s>Oṃ vajra huṃ sraḥ</s>.
Then this is his <s>maṇḍala</s>:

body.text: maṇḍalaṃ pūrvaval likhya madhye vajraṃ samālikhet //
body.translated_text: Having drawn the <s>maṇḍala</s> as before, one should draw a <s>vajra</s> in the center.

body.text: atha vā vajrasattvaṃ tu samantabhadraṃ mahāsukham //
body.translated_text: Or [one should draw] <s>Vajrasattva</s>, [that is,] <s>Samantabhadra</s>, the Great Bliss (<s>Mahāsukha</s>).
In front, <s>Vajrapāṇi</s>; on the right, <s>Ratnapāṇi</s> (Jewel-Handed One).

body.text: paścime padmapāṇiṃ tu viśvapāṇiṃ tu cottare //
body.translated_text: Behind, <s>Padmapāṇi</s> (Lotus-Handed One); and on the north, <s>Viśvapāṇi</s> (Universal-Handed One).
On the outside, making a circle, one should place all the Buddhas.

body.text: tasya bāhye tu sattvākhyaṃ saṃlikhed tu yathākramam //
body.translated_text: Outside that, one should draw the <s>sattvā</s> (bodhisattvas) in proper order.
Outside that too, one should draw beings such as <s>Maitreya</s> and other great ones.

body.text: tadbāhye tu likhed bhikṣūn ānandādīn munīn tathā //
body.translated_text: Outside that, one should draw <s>bhikṣus</s> (monks) such as <s>Ānanda</s> and other sages.
On the outside, one should draw <s>Brahmā</s> and others, adorned with consorts and ritual instruments.
Planetary and stellar signs, moon and sun, [and] the four named hero-Victors.
The directional world-protectors (<s>diglokapāla</s>) should be drawn in this <s>maṇḍala</s>.
On the outside, [one should draw] hell-beings and others, and those of the animal realm in likeness.
At each and every gate, likewise.

body.text: dineṣv eteṣu daśasu prayatnato maṇḍalaṃ likhet //
body.translated_text: On these ten [auspicious] days, one should draw the <s>maṇḍala</s> with care.
Even in the dark fortnight (<s>kṛṣṇapakṣa</s>), when there is ability, the <s>maṇḍala</s> is not contraindicated.
On the fifth, the seventh, and especially on the full moon day,
the ritual procedure for the <s>maṇḍalas</s> of the Lotus-Handed One (<s>Padmapāṇi</s>) is recommended.

body.text: yāni ca krūrakarmāsu tāny ālikhet kṛṣṇe 'pi //
body.translated_text: And for fierce ritual actions, those should be drawn even in the dark [fortnight].
The <s>maṇḍalas</s> of the wrathful ones (<s>krodha</s>), especially on the full moon,
the <s>maṇḍalas</s> of the Victors (<s>Jina</s>) are recommended.
Then one should perform the preliminary consecration (<s>adhivāsanā</s>) the day before the <s>maṇḍala</s> endeavor.
First one should determine the eastern direction by the rising of the sun.
Then one should mentally conceive the arrangement of the <s>maṇḍala</s>.
Food prescribed by the <s>mantra-tantra</s>, smooth, auspicious in <s>mantra</s>-form, pure,
agreeable to the mind, should be eaten in moderation together with one's disciples.
Then at dusk, well-bathed, wearing white garments, pure,

body.text: saha śiṣyair gurur dhīmān āgacchen maṇḍalāntikaṃ //
body.translated_text: the wise master (<s>guru</s>), together with [his] disciples, should come to the vicinity of the <s>maṇḍala</s>.
On the well-anointed, well-swept area of the <s>maṇḍala</s>,
sprinkled with fragrant water consecrated with the <s>Mahākrodha</s> (Great Wrathful One) [<s>mantra</s>],
in the center, one should perform the preliminary consecration with the heart-<s>mantra</s> of the families (<s>kula</s>).
With the <s>mantra</s> of the <s>maṇḍala</s>-lord, all ritual actions should be performed.
Having made an incense-<s>maṇḍala</s> on the ground, twelve finger-breadths [in size],
touching it seven times with the palm, one should recite the <s>maṇḍala-vidyā</s> (maṇḍala-spell).

body.text: devatānāṃ tu paścān mahatāṃ nāma bodhiyā //
body.translated_text: Then [one should invoke] the names of the great deities, [and] of the <s>Bodhi</s> (Awakening).
With the heart-<s>mantra</s>, one should make offerings of fragrances, flowers, and the like in the proper portions.

body.text: kṛtvā baliś ca dātavyo dhūpaś caivābhimantritaḥ //
body.translated_text: Having done so, offerings (<s>bali</s>) should be given, and incense too should be consecrated [with <s>mantras</s>].
Then one should consecrate water mixed with sandalwood.

body.text: tasmin deyāni puṣpāṇi dhūpayec ca vidhānataḥ //
body.translated_text: Flowers should be placed in that [water], and incense should be offered according to the rite.
A tooth-stick (<s>dantakāṣṭha</s>) of <s>Udumbara</s> (cluster fig) or <s>Aśvattha</s> (sacred fig), without blemish,
neither too thin nor too thick, measuring twelve finger-breadths,
washed with fragrant water, wrapped with a thread (<s>sūtraka</s>),

body.text: dhūpitaṃ gandhadigdhaṃ ca japed ālabhya pāṇinā //
body.translated_text: fumigated and anointed with fragrance — one should recite while touching [it] with the palm

body.text: hṛdayaṃ ca bahuśaḥ saptaśo vā kulasya tu //
body.translated_text: the heart-<s>mantra</s> many times or seven times, of the [appropriate] family (<s>kula</s>).
According to the number of disciples, the collection of tooth-sticks and the like [should be prepared].
One by one, [the disciples] should chew [the tooth-sticks] at the tip end.

body.text: tato rakṣāṃ dṛḍhaṃ kṛtvā śiṣyāṇām ātmanā budhaḥ //
body.translated_text: Then, having firmly made the protection (<s>rakṣā</s>) for the disciples and himself, the wise one [should proceed].
The <s>homa</s> (fire offering) ritual, with fuel-sticks anointed with ghee,

body.text: tilaiś ca ghṛtamiśritair ghṛtair āhutihomaiś ca //
body.translated_text: and with sesame mixed with ghee, and with ghee oblations and fire offerings,
one should also offer with curd-rice.
First, for the pacification of obstacles, and then with the subsidiary heart [<s>mantra</s>],

body.text: tato 'nuśāntihomaṃ ca kuryāc chāntiṃ vā pāpasya //
body.translated_text: then one should perform the subsidiary pacification <s>homa</s>, or [a homa] for the pacification of sin.
Then one should examine the disciples and ritually prepare them (<s>adhivāsana</s>) according to the procedure.

body.text: tadahaḥ śaktitaḥ kuryāt saṃvaraṃ grahaṇaṃ tathā //
body.translated_text: On that day, according to one's ability, one should perform the taking of the vow (<s>saṃvara</s>).

body.text: teṣām evaṃ vidhānaṃ tu śucīnāṃ śuklavāsasām //
body.translated_text: For those [disciples] thus prepared—the pure ones clad in white garments—
seated facing east, one should begin the preparatory rite (<s>adhivāsana</s>).

body.text: ādau triśaranaṃ dadyād bodhicittaṃ tato guruḥ //
body.translated_text: First the <s>guru</s> should give the three refuges, then <s>bodhicitta</s> (the aspiration to awakening)—
generating it in those in whom it has not arisen, and reminding those in whom it has already arisen.
Then, with water empowered by the wrathful [<s>mantra</s>], one should sprinkle the head.
Touching the head, one should recite with concentration seven times
the heart [<s>mantra</s>] of the <s>Vidyārāja</s> (King of Sacred Knowledge), with a hand anointed with perfume.
The discerning one should touch and continue [the recitation] seven times with reverence.
In the <s>Cakravartin</s>-<s>Jina</s> family, the <s>Vidyārāja</s> has one syllable.
In the <s>Hayaśvetāmbuja</s> (White Horse-Lotus) family, the <s>Vidyārāja</s> has ten syllables.
In the <s>Sumbha-Tathā-Vajra</s> family, the <s>Vidyārāja</s> is of great supernatural power,
endowed with four <s>Huṃ</s> syllables, fierce in all ritual actions.
Common to the three families, the wrathful one is <s>Amṛtakuṇḍalin</s>,
spoken by the lord of the <s>guhyakas</s> (secret beings) for the destruction of all obstacles.
With the all-action <s>mantra</s>, touching the crown of the head, one should then recite.

body.text: prokṣayec cāpi tenaiva dhūpanena ca dhūpayet //
body.translated_text: One should also sprinkle with that same [<s>mantra</s>], and fumigate with incense.
For the consecration (<s>abhiṣeka</s>), a water-vessel (<s>kalaśa</s>) filled with all [kinds of] rice and the like,
having placed a small amount of water, empowered with the <s>Vidyārāja</s> [<s>mantra</s>],
one should perform the preparatory rite properly, offering <s>arghya</s> (welcome-water) with perfumed water.
Having scattered flowers, one should perform the preparatory rite with incense.

body.text: ahany ahani trisaṃdhyaṃ tatsamyak parijaped budhaḥ //
body.translated_text: Day after day, at the three junctures (<s>sandhyā</s>), the wise one should properly perform the complete recitation.
With that [recitation], one should perform the consecration again with the empowered [water] in the <s>maṇḍala</s>.
For all the disciples assembled, with palms joined, facing north,
one should then give tooth-sticks (<s>dantakāṣṭha</s>) according to the sequence of seats.
Having the disciples face east, [having them] chew the tooth-sticks and the like, from outside [the maṇḍala],

body.text: sphuṭayet pūrṇaṃ khāditvā kṣipeyuś ca na pārśvataḥ //
body.translated_text: when fully chewed, they should split [the stick] and throw it, not to the side,

body.text: samyak kṣiptaṃ dantakāṣṭhaṃ pated abhimukhaṃ yadā //
body.translated_text: but straight ahead. When the tooth-stick thrown falls facing forward,

body.text: jñeyāt tasyottamāsiddhir yasya cāpi unmukhaṃ bhavet //
body.translated_text: one should know that his is the supreme <s>siddhi</s> (accomplishment); and for whomever it falls face-upward,
falling with the tip pointing east, that is declared the middling <s>siddhi</s>.

body.text: udaṅmukhena tu cakṣu vidyāsiddhis tu laukikī //
body.translated_text: If facing north, it is the eye—the mundane <s>vidyā-siddhi</s> (accomplishment of sacred knowledge).
If the thrown tooth-stick somehow falls face-downward,

body.text: tadā pātālasiddhiḥ syād bhavān nāsty atra saṃśayaḥ //
body.translated_text: then it would be the subterranean <s>siddhi</s> (<s>pātāla-siddhi</s>)—there is no doubt about this.
For the disciples who have performed ritual ablution and are seated as before,
the <s>guru</s> should give perfumed water with the all-action <s>mantra</s>.
For each one to drink, he should give three palmfuls.
Having drunk there itself, rising up, one should conduct oneself with one or many [practices].

body.text: tataḥ pūjāṃ punaḥ kṛtvā dhūpam utkṣipya pāṇinā //
body.translated_text: Then, having performed worship again, raising incense with the hand,
the wise one should make a request, devotedly relying on the deity:

body.text: pūrvam āmantrayed mantraṃ yasya tad maṇḍalaṃ bhavet //
body.translated_text: 'First one should address the <s>mantra</s> [deity] to whom this <s>maṇḍala</s> belongs,'
by that sequential order, the invitation of the deities [is performed]:
'<s>Bhagavān</s>! O <s>Vidyārāja</s> named so-and-so, homage to you!'
'Tomorrow I wish to draw a <s>maṇḍala</s>, O compassionate one,'
'for the sake of compassion toward the disciples and for the worship of you.'

body.text: tan me bhaktasya bhagavan prasādaṃ kartum arhasi //
body.translated_text: 'Therefore, <s>Bhagavān</s>, please be gracious to me, your devotee.'
'May the Buddhas, the compassionate Lords of the World, attend to me,'

body.text: arhanto bodhisattvāś ca yā cānyā mantradevatā //
body.translated_text: 'the <s>Arhats</s> and <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, and whatever other <s>mantra</s>-deities,'
'the deities, the world-protectors (<s>lokapālas</s>), and whatever beings of great supernatural power,'
'whatever beings devoted to the Teaching who possess the divine eye—'

body.text: aham amukanāmnā tu amukaṃ maṇḍalaṃ śubham //
body.translated_text: 'I, named so-and-so, [will create] this auspicious <s>maṇḍala</s> named so-and-so,'
'on my own ground I shall make it, with worship according to my ability.'

body.text: anukampām upādāya saśiṣyasya tu tan mama //
body.translated_text: 'Taking up compassion, for me together with my disciples,'

body.text: maṇḍale sahitāḥ sarve sānidhyaṃ kartum arhatha //
body.translated_text: 'all of you assembled in the <s>maṇḍala</s>, please grant your presence.'

body.text: evam uktvā tu yā vācā namas kṛtvā bhagavataḥ //
body.translated_text: Having spoken thus, having made obeisance to the <s>Bhagavān</s> with those words,

body.text: stotropahāraṃ kṛtvā ca tataḥ kuryād visarjanam //
body.translated_text: and having made an offering of praise, one should then perform the dismissal.
Having given a Dharma teaching connected with dispassion to the disciples,

body.text: kṛtvā prācchiraso dhīmān sthāpayet kuśalaṃ stare //
body.translated_text: the wise one, with heads bowed, should place [them to sleep] on a bed of <s>kuśa</s> grass.
When the night has passed, one should ask [them] about their dream visions.

body.text: śrutvā dine nirviśaṃkaḥ śubhaṃ vā yadi vāśubhaṃ //
body.translated_text: Having heard, whether auspicious or inauspicious, on that day without hesitation,
the holder of the Buddha [lineage] should establish the seven families for the kings [of mantra].

body.text: tatas tvaṃ samayaṃ putra saṃvaraṃ jinabhāṣitam //
body.translated_text: 'Then you, O son, [should uphold] the pledge (<s>samaya</s>), the vow (<s>saṃvara</s>) spoken by the Victorious Ones:'

body.text: śraddhayā guror ājñāṃ ca pālaya prāṇino na tvayā ghātyāḥ //
body.translated_text: 'With faith, guard the <s>guru's</s> command. Living beings are not to be killed by you.'

body.text: nādattaṃ grāhyaṃ kāmamithyā na kāryā siddhim icchatām //
body.translated_text: 'What is not given should not be taken. Sexual misconduct should not be committed by those desiring <s>siddhi</s>.'

body.text: na madyaṃ peyaṃ māṃsādi bhakṣaṃ naiva kadācana //
body.translated_text: 'Liquor should not be drunk. Meat and the like should never be eaten.'

body.text: sattvānām ahitaṃ na kāryaṃ tyājyaṃ ratnatrayaṃ na ca //
body.translated_text: 'Harm should not be done to beings. And the Three Jewels (<s>Ratnatraya</s>) should not be abandoned.'
'The <s>bodhicitta</s>, the heart-<s>mudrā</s>, the <s>guru</s>, and the deities likewise—'

body.text: alaṃghyā guror ājñā yataḥ pāpaṃ tu laṃghayet //
body.translated_text: 'the <s>guru's</s> command should not be transgressed. From transgression comes sin.'

body.text: na laṃghayec ca nirmālyaṃ tacchāyāṃ nākramet //
body.translated_text: 'One should not step over consecrated offerings (<s>nirmālya</s>), nor tread upon their shadow,'
'nor upon the forms of <s>mudrās</s> likewise.'

body.text: na nindayed mantradevatāṃ grahakarmāṇi na kurvīta //
body.translated_text: 'One should not revile <s>mantra</s>-deities. One should not perform actions of harmful seizure.'
'And one should not revile practitioners of other paths (<s>tīrthikas</s>).'
'In brief, one should not entertain doubt, suspicion, or uncertainty'
'regarding one's own <s>tantra</s>, the deities, and the like, likewise.'
'With firm faith, properly, through the consecration of the All-Knowing One (<s>Sarvavid</s>),'
'with complete vessels and the like, the tenfold consecration for the ten [stages], as one wishes.'
Then the <s>vajra</s> and bell (<s>ghaṇṭā</s>) should be given into the hand.
Then, having taken the seven jewels beginning with the wheel (<s>cakra</s>),
for the attainment of universal sovereignty (<s>cakravartitva</s>), kingship, and lordship,
and for the shattering of sin, one should perform the consecration.
For the disciple who wishes to accomplish the <s>mantra</s>, one should announce the command:
Then, with faith, bowing the head, whatever wealth is available
should be given to the <s>guru</s>.
Treasure-stores, rice, silver, gold, vehicles, and houses;
seats, boys, girls, men, and women should be given;
villages and cities, as desired;
with a mind of joyful devotion, one should present offerings (<s>dakṣiṇā</s>).

body.text: āśusiddhaye gurave saṃkṣipta ātmānam api nivedayet //
body.translated_text: For swift accomplishment, to the <s>guru</s>, in brief, one should offer even oneself.
In this very life, all pleasures without remainder; and in the next world, the supreme bliss;
Buddhahood is attained—how much more, then, the happiness of the gods!
By reviling the <s>guru</s>, who is equal to all Buddhas, the <s>vajrācārya</s>—
there is the attainment of perpetual suffering. Therefore, one should not revile the master.
The <s>yogī</s> should not revile vajra-brothers, vajra-sisters, or the [vajra-]mother.

body.text: upanāhaṃ ca na kuryāt // ratnatrayopakāriṇo na kṣamet //
body.translated_text: One should not bear malice. One should not tolerate those who harm the Three Jewels.
Those who revile the <s>guru</s>, the wicked, and those who transgress the <s>samaya</s> pledges likewise—
and those who do such harm—[should not be tolerated].
Thus abiding, one attains the <s>siddhi</s> spoken by the All-Knowing One (<s>Sarvavid</s>).
One who is compassionate toward all beings attains <s>siddhi</s> swiftly.

body.text: atha khalu bhagavān devendrasadevalokahitasukhārthāya sādhanavidhim abhāṣata / paṭe bhagavantaṃ sarvavidaṃ tathaiva likhet / dakṣiṇe sarvadurgatipariśodhanarājaṃ tathāgatam / vāme śākyamunim / sarvadurgatipariśodhanasyādhastād āryāvalokiteśvaraṃ candrārkavarṇapadmapāṇim / śākyamuner adhastād vajrapāṇim / tayor madhye bhaiṣajyarājaṃ nīlavarṇam ekena hastena hāritakīphalaṃ dhārayantam apareṇa varadaṃ kārayantam / hayagrīvatrailokyavijayau ca duṣṭadamanatatparau svadevatābhimukhau likhet / tayor madhye locanāmāmakīpāṇḍuravāsinītārāḥ svacihnakarā likhet / tāsām adhastāt puṣkariṇīṃ makaramatsyaśvetamaṇḍukādisahitām anekajalajapuṣpaparipūrṇāṃ likhet / dhūpadīpagandhamālyanaivedyapuṣpaphalāni nānāprakārāṇi ca likhet / adhastāc ca sādhakaṃ añjaliṃ kṛtvā praṇamantaṃ likhed niṣaṇṇam /
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bhagavān</s>, for the benefit and happiness of <s>Devendra</s> and the world of the gods, spoke the method of accomplishment (<s>sādhana</s>): On a cloth (<s>paṭa</s>), one should draw the <s>Bhagavān Sarvavid</s> (the All-Knowing One) in the same manner. On the right, the <s>Tathāgata Sarvadurgatipariśodhana-rāja</s>. On the left, <s>Śākyamuni</s>. Below <s>Sarvadurgatipariśodhana</s>, the noble <s>Avalokiteśvara</s>, moon-and-sun-colored, with a lotus in hand. Below <s>Śākyamuni</s>, <s>Vajrapāṇi</s>. Between those two, <s>Bhaiṣajyarāja</s> (Medicine King), blue in color, holding a <s>harītakī</s> fruit in one hand and making the gesture of granting (<s>varada</s>) with the other. <s>Hayagrīva</s> and <s>Trailokyavijaya</s>, both intent on subduing the wicked, should be drawn facing their respective deities. Between those two, <s>Locanā</s>, <s>Māmakī</s>, <s>Pāṇḍuravāsinī</s>, and <s>Tārā</s> should be drawn with their respective emblems in hand. Below them, one should draw a lotus pool with <s>makaras</s>, fish, white frogs, and the like, filled with various aquatic flowers. Incense, lamps, perfume, garlands, food-offerings, flowers, fruits, and various other [items] should be drawn. And below [all], the practitioner (<s>sādhaka</s>), making <s>añjali</s> and bowing, should be drawn seated.

body.text: tataḥ paṭasatyādhiṣṭhānam avalambya cakṣurunmīlanaṃ kṛtvā pūjayet / tato yadi nimittaṃ paśyet siddhyati śīgram / yadi na paśyec ciraṃ siddhyati / hasituṃkarmaśabdaṃ ca ghaṇṭādhvanigarjitam eva ca //
body.translated_text: Then, relying on the empowerment of the truth of the cloth [image], having performed the eye-opening [ceremony], one should worship. Then, if one perceives an omen, accomplishment comes quickly. If one does not perceive [an omen], accomplishment comes after a long time. Laughter, the sound of ritual action, and the sound of bells and thunder—

body.text: bhikṣubrāhmaṇakanyāś ca phalāni ca dṛṣṭvā śīghram //
body.translated_text: upon seeing monks, brahmins, maidens, and fruits, quickly
one attains accomplishment among the supreme, middling, and inferior <s>siddhis</s>.
Then one should empower the cloth with <s>mantras</s> and <s>mudrās</s>.
And with whatever is available, one should worship. Sitting before it,
having performed self-protection and the like with [the mantra of] <s>Trailokyavijaya</s>,
and having meditated on one's own true nature (<s>ātmatattva</s>),

body.text: lakṣatrayaṃ ṣaṭlakṣāṇi vā japed yāvat siddhinimittaṃ bhūtam /
body.translated_text: one should recite three hundred thousand or six hundred thousand [times], until the sign of accomplishment appears.

body.text: tato vivekasthāne 'ṣṭau 'śatāni pūrayet / mantraṃ cānūnādhikaṃ japet /
body.translated_text: Then in a secluded place, one should complete eight hundred [recitations]. One should recite the <s>mantra</s> neither too few nor too many times.

body.text:
tato japāvasāne maṇḍalaṃ pūrvavac cintayitvā /
vipulāṃ ca pūjāṃ kṛtvā rātrīm ekāṃ japet /
body.translated_text: Then at the conclusion of the recitation, having visualized the <s>maṇḍala</s> as before, and having made extensive worship, one should recite for one night.

body.text:
tataḥ pradhānaṃ ca tatputraṃ ca devāṃś ca yadi paśyati /
tadā yathābhājanam īpsitottamasiddhiṃ vijñāpayet /
devatā nityaṃ tuṣṭāḥ siddhiphalaṃ tasya dadati /
namaskṛtya ca siddhim uttamādikāṃ gṛhṇīyāt /
gururatnatrayasvabhāgaṃ datvā /
tato nityaṃ vicaret tadabhāveṣu prājñaḥ /
body.translated_text: Then, if one sees the principal [deity], his son, and the gods, then according to one's capacity, one should request the desired supreme <s>siddhi</s>. The deities, being always pleased, grant the fruit of accomplishment to that person. Having made obeisance, one should receive the supreme and other <s>siddhis</s>. Having given the <s>guru's</s> and the Three Jewels' portion, the wise one should then always conduct himself [accordingly]; in the absence of those [siddhis], [one should continue practice].

body.text: gṛhītvā svayaṃ samācaret / sarvasattvahitakārī cānekakalpaṃ tiṣṭhet / asiddhau sarvakarmakaro bhavet / yakṣanakṣatragrahādayo vacanamātreṇa bhṛtyavac chāntikādisarvakarmakarā bhavanti /
body.translated_text: Having received [the siddhi], one should conduct oneself accordingly. Being a benefactor of all beings, one should abide for many <s>kalpas</s> (aeons). In the case of non-accomplishment, one becomes a performer of all [ritual] actions. <s>Yakṣas</s>, <s>nakṣatras</s> (asterisms), <s>grahas</s> (planets), and others, by mere word, like servants, become performers of all actions—pacification and the like.

body.text: atha khalu devendro bhagavantam etad avocat / bhagavan pāpakāriṇāṃ nārakādivaśībhūtānāṃ sattvānāṃ nārakādiduḥkhaprahāṇāya kathaṃ pratipattavyam / bhagavān āha / devendra śṛṇu nārakavaśagatasattvānāṃ mahāpāpakāriṇāṃ teṣāṃ yathā nārakaduḥkhebhyo 'nāyāsato muktir bhavati tathā śṛṇu / tathaiva maṇḍalaṃ likhitvāṣṭottaraśatajaptaiḥ kalaśaiḥ pūrvavad abhiṣekaṃ kalpayet / tataḥ sarvapāpagatāḥ sarvanārakādiduḥkhebhyaḥ śīghraṃ vimucyante / te ca vimuktapāpamahātmānaḥ śuddhāvāsadeveṣūtpannāḥ / satataṃ buddhadharmasaṃgītim prāpnuvanti / avaivartikabhūmipratiṣṭhitāś ca krameṇa bodhiṃ sākṣāt kurvanti /
body.translated_text: Then <s>Devendra</s> said this to the <s>Bhagavān</s>: '<s>Bhagavān</s>, for beings who are sinners and have fallen under the power of hell and other [evil destinies], for the abandonment of the suffering of hell and the like, how should one proceed?' The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: '<s>Devendra</s>, listen! For beings who have fallen under the power of hell, who are great sinners—listen to how liberation from the sufferings of hell comes about effortlessly for them: Having drawn the <s>maṇḍala</s> in the same manner, one should arrange the consecration as before with water-vessels empowered with one hundred and eight recitations. Then those who have gone to the state of all sins are swiftly liberated from all the sufferings of hell and the like. And those great beings, freed from sin, are born among the <s>Śuddhāvāsa</s> (Pure Abode) gods. They constantly attain the recitation of the Buddha-<s>Dharma</s>. Established on the irreversible stage, they gradually realize awakening (<s>bodhi</s>) directly.'

body.text: tatpratibimbaṃ vā nāma ca kuṃkumena likhitvā //
body.translated_text: Or, having written their image or name with saffron (<s>kuṃkuma</s>),
for the liberation of beings from the great fear of the three evil destinies,
the <s>mantra</s>-practitioner, devoted to the welfare of others, should compassionately perform the consecration.
Then that <s>yogī</s> should consecrate with <s>mantras</s> and <s>mudrās</s>.
Having fashioned a deity-image, one should install it inside a <s>caitya</s> (reliquary shrine).
Having written the heart [<s>mantra</s>] of one's own and others' deities at the heart-region of that [image],
having generated a mind equal to the deity, one may also install [the image] in a house.

body.text: tannāma ca vidarbhya mantraṃ kuṃkumena likhitvā //
body.translated_text: And having interleaved that [being's] name and written the <s>mantra</s> with saffron (<s>kuṃkuma</s>),
one should perform the <s>caitya</s> ritual until completing one hundred thousand [recitations].
For the destruction of the sins of great sinners, one should even complete ten million (<s>koṭi</s>) [recitations].

body.text: evaṃ kṛte te 'vaśyaṃ narakād muktā bhavanti //
body.translated_text: When this is done, they are certainly liberated from hell.
Likewise, liberated from animal [rebirth] as well, they are born among the assemblies of gods.

body.text: tannāma ca vidarbhya yathoktamantraṃ sahasraṃ japet //
body.translated_text: And having interleaved that [being's] name, one should recite the prescribed <s>mantra</s> one thousand times.

body.text: kadācit śatasahasram api pūrayed yāvat koṭim api pūrayet //
body.translated_text: Sometimes one should even complete a hundred thousand, or even up to ten million (<s>koṭi</s>).
They are born among the assemblies of gods.

body.text: tannāmavidarbhya kuśalo lakṣaśataṃ vā yāvac chatasahasram //
body.translated_text: The skillful one, having interleaved that [being's] name, [should recite] a hundred thousand or up to one hundred thousand times.
One should perform the <s>homa</s> (fire oblation) — they become freed from the sins of the great hells.
Until such time as signs arise in the place of the blazing fire,
Sesame, white mustard seeds, and rice grains mixed with goat's milk,

body.text: samidhāś ca gandhāktās tāvad yathāvidhi hotavyāḥ //
body.translated_text: And sacrificial sticks anointed with fragrance should be offered according to the rite.

body.text: tatas te niyataṃ devanikāyeṣūtpannā nimittam upadarśayanti /
body.translated_text: Then they, certainly born in the classes of <s>devas</s> (gods), manifest signs.

body.text: kadācid devottamā utpannā atha vā kuṇḍamadhye śvetapradakṣiṇajvālā nirmalordhvajvalanam / avakīrṇasaṃdattajvalanaṃ vidyudiva nirmalaṃ sthiram / etāny aganimittāni paśyati / atha vaiśvānalatātmānaṃ tathaiva darśayanti / candravannirmalaṃ śuklamukhavarṇajvalitam / etannimittadarśanāt teṣāṃ narakādi vimuktipāpasphoṭanasvargotpattayo jñātavyāḥ /
body.translated_text: Sometimes, born as supreme <s>devas</s>, or in the middle of the fire-pit, a white clockwise flame, a pure upward blaze, a scattered-and-collected burning, pure and steady like lightning — these are the fire-signs one sees. Then they show themselves in the form of <s>Vaiśvānara</s> (the universal fire). Pure like the moon, with a white-faced blazing complexion — from seeing such signs, one should know that their liberation from hell and other [evil destinies], the bursting open of sins, and rebirth in heaven [have occurred].
One should dig a fire-pit measuring four cubits according to the rite,
Surrounded by <s>vajras</s> at the perimeter, one should draw a wheel in the center,
One should draw the <s>mudrās</s> of the five families in their respective directions as prescribed,
Likewise one should draw the lord of beings for the <s>sattvas</s>,
Then full vessels, dishes filled with <s>bali</s> (offerings),

body.text:
cāṣṭau ṣoḍaśaṃ vā sthāpyāni bhakṣabhojananaivedyāni ca /
puṣpamālādayas tathaiva ca vitānadhvajapaṭādibhir uttamachatraiś ca / samyagvibhūṣaṇīyam /

children.translated_text: Thus, in the supreme <s>homa</s>-fire-pit, one should duly make offerings.
Having drawn thus, the knower of rites should summon the assembly of <s>devas</s>,

body.translated_text: Either eight or sixteen should be placed, along with food, eatables, and <s>naivedya</s> (food offerings), flower garlands and so forth, likewise with canopies, banners, cloths, and excellent parasols — it should be properly adorned.
The knower of mantras, with mantra and <s>mudrā</s>, should present the <s>argha</s> (water-offering) as a welcoming gift,

body.text: saṃkṣepataḥ pūjāṃ kṛtvā devagaṇanāgayakṣagandharvāvasthitaḥ / karpūracandanakuṃkumavastrālaṃkārabhūṣito 'bhimantritadhūpaṃ dhūpayet / puṣpamālādibhiś ca pūjayet / cūḍāyāṃ bāhau ca tathaiva mantraṃ likhitvā bandhayet / hṛtkaṇṭhamukhapradeśe sarvavidyādhiṣṭhānaṃ kuryāt / lalāṭorṇākarṇadvaye śiraḥśikhābāhudvaye / nāsākaṭijānupādanāsikāgracakṣurdvaye / guhyendriyapradeśeṣv evam anyeṣv api mantrākṣarāṇy ekāntaśubhāni vinyaset/ tato durgatipariśodhanāyāsanasahitaṃ tanmadhye sthāpayet /
body.translated_text: Having briefly performed worship, situated among the assemblies of <s>devas</s>, <s>Nāgas</s>, <s>Yakṣas</s>, and <s>Gandharvas</s>, adorned with camphor, sandalwood, saffron, garments, and ornaments, one should offer empowered incense. One should worship with flower garlands and so forth. On the crown and the arms, having likewise written the mantra, one should bind it. At the heart, throat, and mouth areas, one should perform the empowerment of all <s>vidyās</s>. At the forehead, <s>ūrṇā</s>, both ears, head-crest, both arms, nose, waist, knees, feet, tip of the nose, both eyes, and the secret organ areas — thus in these and other places one should arrange the supremely auspicious mantra-syllables. Then one should place in the middle the <s>Durgatipariśodhana</s> (Purification of Evil Destinies) together with its seat.
Then the <s>mantrī</s> (practitioner) should cover it with an empowered cloth.

body.text: tato hutabhujaṃ samyakprajvālya / sahasrajvālya / sahasrajvālākulakāyaṃ kuṇḍendudusannibhaṃ śāntam anantam agnim ākṛṣyārghaṃ parikalpayet / tathaiva ca buddhimān agrataḥ pratimādikaṃ sthāpayet / tathāgatagaṇaṃ tathaivākṛṣyārghādikaṃ parikalpayet tathaiva yathoktapūjā kartavyā /
body.translated_text: Then, having properly kindled the fire, having ignited a thousand flames, having drawn in the fire — peaceful, infinite, resembling the moon in the fire-pit with a body filled with a thousand flames — one should prepare the <s>argha</s> offering. Likewise, the wise one should place the image and so forth in front. Having likewise drawn in the assembly of <s>Tathāgatas</s>, one should prepare the <s>argha</s> and other offerings, and likewise the worship as prescribed should be performed.

body.text: tata āhutiṃ havyaṃ pūrayitvā jvalanāya parikalpayitvā jinādinīm aṣṭottaraśataṃ parikalpayet / tataḥ śodhanamantrarājasyaikaviṃśatim āhutiṃ parikalpayet /
body.translated_text: Then, having filled the oblation and offering material, having prepared it for the fire, one should make one hundred and eight oblations to the <s>Jinas</s> (Victors) and others. Then one should make twenty-one oblations of the king of purification mantras.

body.text: tataś cākṛṣya śvetamukham upakaraṇair vā vāratrayam arghādinā ca pūjayet / vajrapāṇiṃ padmapāśadharaṃ trailokyarūpaṃ pādapadmākrāntapāpaṃ sarvālaṃkārālaṃkṛtaṃ saṃbuddhakirīṭinaṃ cintayed atha vā likhet / tasya ḥrdayena śatasahasraṃ yāvat koṭiṃ vā juhuyāt /
body.translated_text: Then, having drawn in the white-faced one, one should worship three times with requisites or with <s>argha</s> and so forth. One should visualize — or draw — <s>Vajrapāṇi</s> holding a lotus and noose, in the form of the lord of the three worlds, with sins crushed under his lotus-feet, adorned with all ornaments, wearing a crown of <s>Saṃbuddhas</s>. With his <s>hṛdaya</s> (heart-mantra), one should make oblations up to one hundred thousand or even ten million times.

body.text: nimitte ca samutpanne pāpasaṃtatiprahāṇaṃ tathaiva jñātavyam / tato bhasmībhūtaṃ vajrasaṃhāramantreṇa yathāvidhi saṃharet / bhasmāny asthirajāṃsi ca gandhodakapañcagavyasahitāni śodhanamantreṇa lakṣaṃ japtvā pindīkṛtya karpūragandhamṛdbhir miśrīkṛtya pratimāṃ caityadevatāṃ vā kuryāt / ekadvitricatuḥpañcavāraṃ vāṣṭottaraśatavāraṃ vā /
body.translated_text: When signs arise, one should know that the destruction of the continuity of sin has likewise occurred. Then, having reduced to ashes, one should collect them according to the rite with the <s>vajra</s>-dissolution mantra. The ashes and bone-dust, combined with fragrant water and <s>pañcagavya</s> (the five products of the cow), having recited the purification mantra one hundred thousand times, having formed into a mass, having mixed with camphor, fragrance, and clay, one should make an image, a <s>caitya</s> (stūpa), or a deity [figure] — one, two, three, four, five times, or one hundred and eight times.
Having empowered with mantras and <s>mudrās</s>, one should recite two hundred thousand times.

body.text: tataś caityaṃ jvalati pratimā vā hasati //
body.translated_text: Then the <s>caitya</s> blazes, or the image smiles,

body.text: gandhadhūpaprabhā jighrati paśyati devādīṃ nānāprakārām yasya ṛddhiprātihāryāṇi ca patanti puṣpādīni / śaṃkhabherīvaṃśavīṇādīnāṃ ca śabdāḥ śrūyante /
body.translated_text: It smells fragrances, incense, and radiance; it sees <s>devas</s> and others of various kinds, and miraculous displays of supernatural power, and flowers and the like fall; and the sounds of conch shells, drums, flutes, <s>vīṇās</s> (lutes), and other instruments are heard.

body.text: kadācid devatāni nimittāni pāpabahalatayā yadi na paśyet tadāṣṭau lakṣasahasrāṇi japet /
body.translated_text: If sometimes, due to the heaviness of sins, one does not see the divine signs, then one should recite eight hundred thousand times.

body.text: yāvan nimittaṃ bhavati tathāgataṃ pūjayitvā // susamāhito japet /
body.translated_text: Until such time as signs appear, having worshipped the <s>Tathāgata</s>, one should recite with well-concentrated mind.

body.text:
tato 'nte rātrīm ekāṃ vidhijño japet /
tadāvaśyaṃ pāpaviśuddhātmā paśyati /
devatārūpakāyaṃ tatsantānaṃ parijānāti /
etāni nimittāni jñātvā avikalpacitto /
maitrīkṛpāparītaḥ sarvakarmāṇi kuryāt /
body.translated_text:
Then, at the end, for one night, the knower of rites should recite.
Then assuredly, the one whose self is purified of sin sees it.
One perceives the deity's form-body and its continuity.
Having recognized these signs, with a mind free from conceptual elaboration,
Suffused with loving-kindness and compassion, one should perform all the rites.

body.text: evam api yadi na saṃbhavati tadā tannāmamātraṃ likhitvā caityamālāṃ kuryāt pratimāṃ vā kṛtvā / homābhiṣekakṛte sati / niyataṃ svargeṣūtpadyante / bhasmasarṣapavālukādīṃś ca nāma vidarbhyābhimantrya samudragāminyāṃ nadyāṃ kṣipet / tataḥ pāpīyaso 'pi durgati vimokṣati /
body.translated_text: If even thus it does not succeed, then having written merely the name, one should make a <s>caitya</s>-garland, or having made an image, when the <s>homa</s> and <s>abhiṣeka</s> (consecration) are performed, they are certainly reborn in the heavens. And ashes, mustard seeds, sand, and the like, having empowered them with the name using a <s>darbha</s> (sacred grass) brush, one should cast them into a river flowing to the ocean. Then even the most sinful one is liberated from evil destinies.

body.text: uttamakuśalabījam utpāditavato buddhatvaphalasamanvāgatasya dānaśīlakṣāntivīryadhyānaprajñāhetuprabhāvitasya puṇyavato lokasya durgati bhagneti /
body.translated_text: For one who has planted the supreme seed of merit, endowed with the fruit of buddhahood, empowered by the causes of <s>dāna</s> (generosity), <s>śīla</s> (morality), <s>kṣānti</s> (patience), <s>vīrya</s> (vigor), <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation), and <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom) — for such a meritorious being, evil destiny is shattered.
What more need be said? There is no doubt in this.

body.text: yaś cānutpāditakuśalamūlo yaś ca nāstikadṛṣṭir bodhimārgād nivṛttas tasya śāsanavidveṣiṇo 'pakāriṇaḥ pāpānabhijñasyamātṛ pitṛvipriyacittasya bodhicittanisṛtavītarāgaghātakasya devatābuddhadharmasaṃghamantramudrāganādīnāṃ
body.translated_text: But for one who has not planted roots of merit, who holds nihilistic views, who has turned away from the path of awakening, who is hostile to the teaching, who harms others, who is unaware of sin, who has a mind hostile to mother and father, who has killed an <s>Arhat</s> who has abandoned passion and departed from <s>bodhicitta</s>, and who holds views of non-existence regarding deities, <s>Buddha</s>, <s>Dharma</s>, <s>Saṅgha</s>, mantras, <s>mudrās</s>, <s>gaṇas</s> (assemblies), and so forth —

body.text: ca nāstitvādṛṣṭyādīnāṃ ca pāpīyasām eṣāṃ prajñopāyābhāve muktir nāstīti sugatajinair bhāṣitam /
body.translated_text: — and for such sinful ones of nihilistic and similar views, in the absence of <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom) and <s>upāya</s> (skillful means), there is no liberation — thus it has been declared by the <s>Sugatas</s> (Well-gone Ones), the <s>Jinas</s> (Victors).

body.text: atha śakrādaya utpalapadmalocanāḥ sādhv iti toṣayanti sma / saṃtoṣayitvā pūjayanti sma / śakreṇa ca parahitaratena yathāvijñaptaṃ /
body.translated_text: Then <s>Śakra</s> and the others, with lotus and blue-lotus eyes, exclaimed "Excellent!" and were delighted. Having been delighted, they worshipped. And by <s>Śakra</s>, who delights in the welfare of others, it was communicated as understood.

body.text: dvitīyaṃ trisūcikavajrasahitena varado vāmenaikena triśūladhāri dvitīyena khaḍgadhārī sarpayajñopavītanīlakaṇṭho lekhyo 'nena /
body.translated_text: The second one, with a trident-<s>vajra</s>, boon-granting with the left hand, holding a trident with one [right hand] and a sword with another, with a serpent as sacred thread and a blue throat — he should be drawn with this:
"Oṃ <s>Paśupati</s> <s>Nīlakaṇṭha</s> <s>Umāpriya</s> Svāhā!"

body.text: athāsya mudrā bhavati / dakṣiṇahastena vāmamuṣṭina kṛtvā kanīyasīm aṃguṣṭhenākramya śeṣāṃgulavajralakṣaṇāḥ kṛtvānāmikāṃ tarjanīṃ ca vajrākāreṇa kañcin nāmayet / iyaṃ paśupater mudrā / viṣṇur garudārūḍhaḥkṛṣṇavarṇaś caturbhujaḥ / dakṣiṇabhujābhyāṃ gadāvajradharaḥ / vāmābhyāṃ śaṃkhacakradharaḥ /
body.translated_text: And this is his <s>mudrā</s>: with the right hand making a left fist, pressing the little finger with the thumb, making the remaining fingers into <s>vajra</s>-marks, and bending the ring finger and index finger somewhat in a <s>vajra</s>-shape — this is the <s>mudrā</s> of <s>Paśupati</s>. <s>Viṣṇu</s>, mounted on <s>Garuḍa</s>, dark-colored, four-armed; with his two right arms holding a mace and <s>vajra</s>; with his two left arms holding a conch and discus.
<s>Vajrahemā</s>, golden-colored, with seat, arms, and weapons like <s>Viṣṇu</s>,

body.text: vajraghaṇṭāmayūrārūḍho raktavarṇaḥ ṣaḍmukho dakṣiṇabhujābhyāṃ śaktivajradharaḥ / vāmābhyāṃ kukkuṭaghaṇṭāvajradharaś ca /
body.translated_text: <s>Vajraghaṇṭā</s>, mounted on a peacock, red-colored, six-faced, holding a spear and <s>vajra</s> with his two right arms, and holding a rooster, bell, and <s>vajra</s> with his two left arms.
<s>Vajrakaumārī</s> should be known as similar to <s>Vajraghaṇṭā</s>.

body.text: maunavajro haṃsārūḍhaḥ kanakavarṇaś caturmukho dakṣiṇabhujābhyāṃ vajrākṣasūtradhārī / vāmābhyāṃ daṇḍakamaṇḍaludhārī /
body.translated_text: <s>Maunavajra</s>, mounted on a swan, golden-colored, four-faced, holding a <s>vajra</s>-rosary with his two right arms, and holding a staff and water-pot with his two left arms.
<s>Vajraśānti</s> should be known as similar to <s>Brahmā</s>.

body.text: vajrāyudhaḥ śvetagajārūḍho gauravarṇo vāmabhujena viśvavajradharo dakṣiṇena lokottaravajradharaḥ /
body.translated_text: <s>Vajrāyudha</s>, mounted on a white elephant, fair-colored, holding a double-<s>vajra</s> with the left hand and a supramundane <s>vajra</s> with the right.
<s>Vajramuṣṭi</s> should be known as similar to <s>Vajrāyudha</s>.

body.text: vajrakuṇḍalī krodhaś ca rathārūḍho dakṣiṇakareṇa sapadmena vajradharo vāmena sapadmenādityamaṇḍaladharo raktavarṇaḥ / vajrāmṛtā vajrakuṇḍalikrodhavad eva /
body.translated_text: <s>Vajrakuṇḍalī</s>, a <s>krodha</s> (wrathful deity), mounted on a chariot, holding a <s>vajra</s> with a lotus in the right hand, and holding a sun-disc with a lotus in the left hand, red-colored. <s>Vajrāmṛtā</s> is similar to <s>Vajrakuṇḍalī-krodha</s>.

body.text: vajraprabhakrodhaḥ sitavarṇo haṃsārūḍho dakṣiṇakareṇa vajradhārī vāmena padmacandradharaḥ /
body.translated_text: <s>Vajraprabha-krodha</s>, white-colored, mounted on a swan, holding a <s>vajra</s> with the right hand, and holding a lotus-moon with the left.
<s>Vajrakānti</s> is similar to <s>Vajraprabha-krodha</s>.

body.text: vajradaṇḍakrodhaḥ kacchapārūḍho nīlavarṇo dakṣiṇakareṇa vajradhārī vāmena daṇḍadharaḥ /
body.translated_text: <s>Vajradaṇḍa-krodha</s>, mounted on a tortoise, blue-colored, holding a <s>vajra</s> with the right hand, and holding a staff with the left.
<s>Daṇḍavajrāgrī</s> is similar to <s>Vajradaṇḍa-krodha</s>.

body.text: vajrapiṃgalakrodho 'jārūḍho raktavarṇo dakṣiṇakareṇa vajradharo vāmena mānuṣam ādāya bhakṣayan avasthitaḥ /
body.translated_text: <s>Vajrapiṃgala-krodha</s>, mounted on a goat, red-colored, holding a <s>vajra</s> with the right hand, and with the left hand seizing and devouring a human being.
<s>Vajramekhalā</s> is similar to <s>Vajrapiṃgala-krodha</s>.

body.text: vajraśauṇḍo gaṇapatir gajavāhano dakṣiṇakareṇa vajraṃ dhārayed vāmena lāṃgalaṃ dhārayed avasthitaḥ / sitavarṇaḥ /
body.translated_text: <s>Vajraśauṇḍa</s> <s>Gaṇapati</s>, riding an elephant, holding a <s>vajra</s> with the right hand, holding a plough with the left, white-colored.

body.text: vajraviṇayā vajraśauṇḍavad ayan tu viśeṣo yad uta vāmakareṇa khaṭvāṃgadhāriṇīti /
body.translated_text: <s>Vajraviṇayā</s> is similar to <s>Vajraśauṇḍa</s>, but with this distinction: she holds a <s>khaṭvāṅga</s> (skull-staff) in the left hand.

body.text: vajramālo gaṇapatiḥ śyāmavarṇaḥ kaukilarathārūḍho dakṣiṇakareṇa vajradharo vāmena kusumamālādharaḥ /
body.translated_text: <s>Vajramāla</s> <s>Gaṇapati</s>, dark-colored, mounted on a cuckoo-chariot, holding a <s>vajra</s> with the right hand, and holding a flower-garland with the left.

body.text: vajrāsanā vajramālāvad ayan tu viśeṣo yad uta vāmakareṇa śaktidhāriṇīti /
body.translated_text: <s>Vajrāsanā</s> is similar to <s>Vajramālā</s>, but with this distinction: she holds a spear in the left hand.

body.text: vajravaśī śukarathārūḍho gauravarṇo dakṣiṇakareṇa vajradharo vāmena makaradhvajadhārī /
body.translated_text: <s>Vajravaśī</s>, mounted on a boar-chariot, fair-colored, holding a <s>vajra</s> with the right hand, and holding a <s>Makara</s>-banner with the left.

body.text: vajravaśā vajravaśīvad ayan tu tasyā viśeṣo yad uta raktavarṇeti /
body.translated_text: <s>Vajravaśā</s> is similar to <s>Vajravaśī</s>, but with this distinction: she is red-colored.

body.text: vijayavajro gaṇapatir maṇḍūkārūḍhaḥ sitavarṇo dakṣiṇakareṇa vajradharo vāmena khaḍgadharaḥ /
body.translated_text: <s>Vijayavajra</s> <s>Gaṇapati</s>, mounted on a frog, white-colored, holding a <s>vajra</s> with the right hand, and holding a sword with the left.
<s>Vajrasenā</s> is similar to <s>Vijayavajra</s>.

body.text: vajramusaladūtaḥ puṣpavimānārūḍho gauravarṇo dakṣiṇakareṇa vajradharo vāmena musaladharaḥ /
body.translated_text: <s>Vajramusala-dūta</s> (vajra-pestle messenger), mounted on a flower-chariot, fair-colored, holding a <s>vajra</s> with the right hand, and holding a pestle with the left.

body.text: vajradūtī vajramusalavad ayan tu tasyā viśeṣo yad uta vāmena khaṭvāṃgadhāriṇīti /
body.translated_text: <s>Vajradūtī</s> is similar to <s>Vajramusala</s>, but with this distinction: she holds a <s>khaṭvāṅga</s> (skull-staff) in the left hand.

body.text: vajrāniladūto nīlavarṇo mṛgārūḍho dakṣiṇakareṇa vajradhārī vāmena paṭadhārī / vegavajriṇī vajrāniladūtavat /
body.translated_text: <s>Vajrānila-dūta</s> (vajra-wind messenger), blue-colored, mounted on a deer, holding a <s>vajra</s> with the right hand, and holding a banner with the left. <s>Vegavajriṇī</s> is similar to <s>Vajrānila-dūta</s>.

body.text: vajrānaladūto 'jārūḍho raktavarṇa ūrdhvajvālāprabhas triśikhājvālo dakṣiṇabhujābhyāṃ vajrakavacadharo vāmābhyāṃ daṇḍakamaṇḍaludharaś ca / vajrajvālā vajrānalavat /
body.translated_text: <s>Vajrānala-dūta</s> (vajra-fire messenger), mounted on a goat, red-colored, with upward-blazing radiance, triple-crested flames, holding <s>vajra</s> and armor with his two right arms, and holding a staff and water-pot with his two left arms. <s>Vajrajvālā</s> is similar to <s>Vajrānala</s>.

body.text: vajrabhairavadūto nīlo vetālārūḍho dakṣiṇakareṇa vajradhārī vāmena gadādhārī /
body.translated_text: <s>Vajrabhairava-dūta</s> (vajra-terror messenger), blue, mounted on a <s>vetāla</s> (zombie), holding a <s>vajra</s> with the right hand, and holding a mace with the left.

body.text: vajravikaṭā dūtī vajrabhairavavad ayan tu viśeṣo 'syā yad uta vāmena pāśadhāriṇīti /
body.translated_text: <s>Vajravikaṭā-dūtī</s> is similar to <s>Vajrabhairava</s>, but with this distinction: she holds a noose in the left hand.

body.text: vajrāṃkuśaceṭaḥ śeṣanāgārūḍho nīlo varāhamukhaḥ / dakṣiṇena vajradharo vāmenāṃkuśadharaḥ /
body.translated_text: <s>Vajrāṅkuśa-ceṭa</s> (vajra-hook servant), mounted on <s>Śeṣa-nāga</s>, blue, with a boar's face, holding a <s>vajra</s> with the right hand, and holding a hook with the left.

body.text: vajramukhī ceṭī puruṣavāhanā nīlā varāhamukhī dakṣiṇena vajradharā vāmena khaḍgadharā /
body.translated_text: <s>Vajramukhī-ceṭī</s> (vajra-face female servant), with a human mount, blue, with a boar's face, holding a <s>vajra</s> with the right hand, and holding a sword with the left.

body.text: vajrakālaceṭako mahiṣārūḍho nīlo dakṣiṇakareṇa vajradharo vāmena yamadaṇḍadharaḥ /
body.translated_text: <s>Vajrakāla-ceṭaka</s> (vajra-time servant), mounted on a buffalo, blue, holding a <s>vajra</s> with the right hand, and holding <s>Yama</s>'s staff with the left.

body.text: vajrakālī ceṭī vetālavāhanā vāmakareṇa khaṭvāṃgadhāriṇī dakṣiṇakareṇa vajradhāriṇī kṛṣṇavarṇā /
body.translated_text: <s>Vajrakālī-ceṭī</s> (female servant), with a <s>vetāla</s> (zombie) mount, holding a <s>khaṭvāṅga</s> (skull-staff) in the left hand, holding a <s>vajra</s> in the right hand, black-colored.

body.text: vajravināyakaceṭaka undurārūḍhaḥ sitavarṇo gajamukho dakṣiṇakarābhyāṃ vajraparaśudharo vāmābhyāṃ triśūladharo daṇḍadharaś ca / sarpayajñopavītaḥ / vajrapūtanā ceṭī nīlavarṇa dakṣiṇena vajradharā vāmena saṃmārjanikādharā / undurārūḍhā /
body.translated_text: <s>Vajravināyaka-ceṭaka</s>, mounted on a rat, white-colored, elephant-faced, holding a <s>vajra</s>-axe with his two right hands, and holding a trident and staff with his two left hands, with a serpent as sacred thread. <s>Vajrapūtanā-ceṭī</s>, blue-colored, holding a <s>vajra</s> with the right hand, holding a broom with the left, mounted on a rat.
